metadata.source: Dāmodaraguptaviracitaṃ Kuṭṭanīmatam : The Bawd's Counsel, Being an eighth-century verse novel in Sanskrit by Dāmodaragupta Newly edited and translated into English by Csaba Dezso & Dominic Goodall. Groningen: Egbert Forsten, 2012. ISBN 978 90 6980 158 2

children.translated_text: He is victorious — born of desire (<s>Saṃkalpa</s>), the bee that kisses the hundred-petaled [lotus] that is the face of <s>Rati</s> —
he whose abode is in the sidelong glances from the corner of the eyes of women who are enamored of him. // 1 //
Setting aside the mass of faults and fixing your mind upon even a small portion of merit, O noble ones,
listen to this teaching of the procuress (<s>kuṭṭanī</s>), composed by <s>Dāmodaragupta</s>. // 2 //
There exists indeed a city named <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, an ornament among all the regions of the earth, endowed with prosperity and virtues,
whose people are skilled and accomplished. // 3 //
For those embodied beings who enjoy its pleasures at will,
the temple of the body adorned with the crescent moon [i.e., the abode of <s>Śiva</s>] is indeed not hard to attain. // 4 //
With bodies adorned by the moon [i.e., smeared with ashes], devoted to prosperity, surrounded by excellent serpents —
even the courtesans in this city have attained equality with the form of <s>Paśupati</s> (<s>Śiva</s>). // 5 //
With the banners set fluttering by the wind hurled from the peaks of the exceedingly lofty divine temples,

children.text: mañjaritamiva virājati yatra nabho vaijayantībhiḥ // DKuṭṭ_6 //
children.translated_text: the sky there appears as if blossoming. // 6 //
Reddened by the lac-dye dripping from the soles of the feet of women who ceaselessly pass by,

children.text: sthalakamalavatīṃ lakṣmīṃ bibharti vasudhātalaṃ yatra // DKuṭṭ_7 //
children.translated_text: the surface of the earth there bears the beauty of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, as if it were a land of lotuses. // 7 //
Where, in every quarter of sky and earth, the sound of women's ornaments drowns out all other noise,
the faults of students reciting their lessons cannot be detected by their teachers. // 8 //
She [the city] shines like a valley of the <s>Vindhya</s> mountains, attended by rutting elephants,
and like a long dark night, illuminated by blazing sacrificial fires. // 9 //
She is endowed with hosts of ascetics and their virtues, like a collection of Vedic meters always replete with sages;
like a row of forests full of <s>sāla</s> trees, and like a Turkish army with dense perfume. // 10 //
In her, the multitude of stars is low-born, the owls are always fond of faults,
in prose there is a falling away from [good] conduct, [there is] obstructing others' homes, and likewise in dice. // 11 //
The trident-bearers dwell among serpents, on the platforms there is alchemy,
in lovemaking there is the assault of women, and in the rutting and falling of elephants there is the cutting off of gifts. // 12 //
The sun's rays are fierce, there is no discrimination in the hearts of friends,
among yogis there is the taking up of the staff, and in words requiring separation (<s>pragṛhya</s>) there is the breaking of <s>sandhi</s>. // 13 //
In the method of metrical analysis, the heavy [syllables/elders] are not straight in their conduct,
in the <s>vīṇā</s> there is slander, and in the dwellings of the twice-born there is a lack of serenity. // 14 //
The fitting of appropriate meters [/suitable conduct], the works of genuine poets [/the evil deeds of the good in the world],

children.text: ramaṇīvacane yasyāṃ mādhuryaṃ kāvyabandhe ca // DKuṭṭ_15 //
children.translated_text: and sweetness in the speech of lovely women as well as in poetic composition — all these are found in her. // 15 //
In whose garden groves there are <s>tamāla</s> leaves, and on women's faces also,

children.text: nakharaprahārakaṇitaṃ tantrīvādye ca suratakalahe ca // DKuṭṭ_16 //
children.translated_text: and the sound of scratching by nails — both in stringed instruments and in the quarrels of love. // 16 //
Delightful as <s>Nandana</s> grove, full of wise people, frequented by the celestial <s>Gaṅgā</s> —

children.text: amarāvatīva yānyā viśvasṛjā nirmitā jagati // DKuṭṭ_17 //
children.translated_text: this city is another <s>Amarāvatī</s>, as if fashioned by <s>Brahmā</s> himself in this world. // 17 //
In that city, causing grief in the hearts of amorous men like the body of <s>Garuḍa</s> [to serpents],
attracting the heart of the Lord [<s>Śiva</s>], like the daughter of the king of snow-mountains [<s>Pārvatī</s>],
with eyes [/serpents] attached to her body [/enjoyments], like the form of the mountain-bearing [<s>Viṣṇu</s>/<s>Mandara</s>],
elevated above spears [/tridents], like a line painted on the body of the demon of darkness [<s>Andhaka</s>],
there dwelt a courtesan, the embodied power of the abode of the mind [<s>Kāma</s>],
the ornament of all women of the quarter, named <s>Mālatī</s>. // 20 //
She was the dwelling-place of charming words, the abode of playful gestures, the foundation of love,
the ground for jests, the home of witty conversation. // 21 //
She once heard, while she had ascended to the rooftop of her white mansion,
this verse (<s>āryā</s>) being sung by someone, which fell upon her ear by chance: // 22 //
'Casting far away the intoxication of youth and beauty, courtesans
should learn with effort the methods of winning the hearts of lovers.' // 23 //

children.text: śrutvātha vipulajaghanā manasīdaṃ mālatī cakāra ciram /
children.translated_text: Having heard this, broad-hipped <s>Mālatī</s> reflected in her mind for a long time:
'This has been taught most aptly, as if by a true friend, by this good man reciting.' // 24 //
'So let us go and ask <s>Vikarālā</s>, who has experienced all the ways of the world,
at whose door a flood of suitors sits day and night.' // 25 //

children.text: iti manasi sā niveśya drutataramavatīrya veśmanaḥ śikharāt /
children.translated_text: Having thus resolved in her mind, she quickly descended from the top of her house
and, accompanied by her retinue, went to the fine dwelling of <s>Vikarālā</s>. // 26 //
Then [she saw one] with sparse and protruding teeth, a sunken chin, a thick flat nose-tip,
her body a loose skin marked by prominently sagging nipples over dried-up breasts, // 27 //
with deep and reddened eyes, earlobes hanging without ornament,
with a few grey hairs, and an elongated neck interlaced with visible veins, // 28 //
wearing a pair of white washed garments, with a neck-string strung with various medicinal herbs and gems,

children.text: tanvīmaṅgulimūle tapanīyamayīṃ ca vālikāṃ dadhatīm // DKuṭṭ_29 //
children.translated_text: and wearing at the base of her thin finger a small ring made of gold — // 29 //
surrounded by a company of courtesans, her eyes intent on the tributes brought by suitors,
seated on a chair — she beheld <s>Vikarālā</s>. // 30 //
Upon seeing her, she performed a bow with her forehead touching the ground,
was asked about her welfare, and took the seat that was offered. // 31 //
Then, with hands folded in a cup, respectfully rising from her seat,
<s>Mālatī</s> spoke these words to <s>Vikarālā</s>, finding the right moment: // 32 //
'You make <s>Hari</s> [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] [a man] without the <s>Kaustubha</s> gem, the Sun without the lord of elephants, <s>Indra</s> without riches,

children.text: adraviṇaṃ draviṇapatiṃ niyataṃ matigocare patitam // DKuṭṭ_33 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Kubera</s>, the lord of wealth, penniless — whoever falls within the range of your intellect. // 33 //
'This very lover-class, whose splendor has been stripped away, wearing rags for covering,
proclaims your intellectual prowess while eating in charity-houses. // 34 //
'<s>Dhanavarmā</s>, all his other occupations abandoned, has attained the status of a footstool
for the feet of <s>Narmadā</s>, having surrendered all his wealth to her. // 35 //
'<s>Nayadatta</s>, the middle son of <s>Sāgaradatta</s>, who has come under [your influence],

children.text: prīṇayati Madanasenāṃ vidhāya pitṛmandiraṃ riktam // DKuṭṭ_36 //
children.translated_text: gratifies <s>Madanasenā</s>, having made his father's house empty. // 36 //
'<s>Narasiṃha</s>, the son of the <s>Bhaṭṭa</s>, at whose feet <s>Mañjarī</s> has playfully placed herself,

children.text: paritoṣaṃ vrajati paraṃ mṛdu mṛdnan pāṇiyugalena // DKuṭṭ_37 //
children.translated_text: attains supreme satisfaction, gently pressing [her feet] with both his hands. // 37 //
'<s>Śubhadeva</s>, son of the initiate <s>Bhavadeva</s>, whose wealth has been entirely consumed,
though rebuked, does not abandon the doorway of <s>Kesarasenā</s>'s house. // 38 //
'Other common women too, having overwhelmed their suitors,
reduce them to mere rags — this is the display of your teachings! // 39 //
'Men of low birth, devoid of qualities, sick, rejected —
even such have been served by me, manifesting the excellence of passion. // 40 //
'Mother, what shall we do? Through the affliction of an adverse fate upon our constitutions,
we cannot attain what we desire, even by offering our own bodies as merchandise. // 41 //
'Therefore, mother, bestow your grace — tell me too about the men worth enjoying,
and the techniques of the courtesan's art — the methods of shooting the net of <s>Kāma</s>'s arrows [into their hearts].' // 42 //
As she spoke thus, <s>Vikarālā</s>, stroking her back affectionately with her hand,
spoke these charming words to the beautiful <s>Mālatī</s>: // 43 //
'This very mass of hair of yours, O beautiful one, like a spiral of smoke rising from the burning [fire] of <s>Smara</s> (Love),
makes the entire class of suitors into your servants. // 44 //
'This very play of your gently arching eyebrows, O slender-waisted one,
adorned with a sweetly smiling, enchanting glance, humbles even the steadfast. // 45 //
'This very radiance of your face exceedingly multiplies the desire of the beloved of <s>Rati</s> (<s>Kāma</s>);

children.text: śrutipathamapyupayātā niyataṃ tava kāmināṃ manasi // DKuṭṭ_46 //
children.translated_text: even reaching only the path of hearing, it surely dwells in the minds of lovers. // 46 //
'This very row of teeth, whose radiance rivals the beauty of eternal loveliness,

children.text: utpādayati nitāntaṃ tava Manmathadāhavedanāṃ puṃsām // DKuṭṭ_47 //
children.translated_text: produces exceedingly in men the burning sensation of <s>Manmatha</s>'s (Love's) fever. // 47 //
'This very conversation of yours, O playful one, surpassing the sound of the <s>kokilā</s> (cuckoo),
is wondrous — like a perfected <s>mantra</s> for the complete charming of serpents. // 48 //
'This very pair of breasts of yours, O one of serpentine grace, is the abode of <s>Makaraketu</s> (the Love god);
O one rich in enjoyments, it is the instrument of pleasure — any other means is futile. // 49 //
'This very pair of arms of yours, beautiful as tender lotus-stalks, O serpentine one —

children.text: kasya na janayati madanaṃ kanakāṅgadabhūṣaṇaṃ sutanu // DKuṭṭ_50 //
children.translated_text: adorned with golden armlets, in whom does it not arouse desire, O beautiful one? // 50 //
'This very middle region [waist] of yours, O one skilled in carrying out <s>Kandarpa</s>'s (Love's) commands,

children.text: prakṛśo 'pi śarīrabhṛto daśamīṃ prāpayati manmathāvasthām // DKuṭṭ_51 //
children.translated_text: though slender, brings embodied beings to the tenth stage of love-sickness. // 51 //
'This very line of hair [on the belly], bearing the beauty of a bowstring for the bow of the mind-born (<s>Kāma</s>),

children.text: dadhatī vidadhāti tava smarasāyakaśalyaviklavān yūnaḥ // DKuṭṭ_52 //
children.translated_text: makes young men distressed, pierced by the arrows of <s>Smara</s> (Love). // 52 //
'These very broad hips of yours, lovely as a slab of golden stone,
are the means of subjugating young men and the destroyer of the self-control of ascetics, O elephant-thighed one. // 53 //
'This very pair of thighs of yours, resembling the interior of a plantain stem, captivating the heart —

children.text: vada sundari nābhimataṃ madanajvaratāpaśāntaye kasya // DKuṭṭ_54 //
children.translated_text: tell me, beautiful one, whose desire it does not fulfill for the cooling of the fever of love? // 54 //
'This pair of calves, well-rounded like the graceful movement of a golden creeper of the wishing-tree of your youth —

children.text: jaṅghāyugalaṃ necchati kāmaphalaprāptaye ka iva // DKuṭṭ_55 //
children.translated_text: who indeed does not desire it for the attainment of the fruit of <s>Kāma</s>? // 55 //
'This pair of lotus-feet of yours, surpassing the color of pomegranate in redness, excelling the beauty of land-lotuses —

children.text: tava caraṇasarojayugaṃ kasya na mānasamalaṅkurute // DKuṭṭ_56 //
children.translated_text: whose mind does it not adorn? // 56 //
'This very gait of yours puts to shame the lord of elephants, laughs at the swan —

children.text: tava līlāvati lalitaṃ yūnāṃ hṛdayāni mathnāti // DKuṭṭ_57 //
children.translated_text: O playful one, your graceful movement churns the hearts of young men. // 57 //

children.text: tadapi yadi te kutūhalamavadhānaṃ saṃvidhāya tanumadhye /
children.translated_text: 'But even so, if you are curious, compose your attention, O slender-waisted one,
and listen — I shall tell you according to the extent of my own wisdom. // 58 //
'First of all, take up with great effort the son of a royal officer or a <s>bhaṭṭa</s>,
if you desire wealth that is abundant and under your own control, O beautiful one. // 59 //
'When his father is always away at the military camp, the <s>Bhaṭṭa</s>'s son, himself a lord in the neighboring village,
is invariably attracted, like a <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem), O daughter. // 60 //

children.text: śṛṇu tasya cāruhāsini veṣagrahaṇaṃ ca ceṣṭitaṃ caiva /
children.translated_text: 'Listen, O one of charming smile, to his manner of dress and his behavior,

children.text: nipatati ca yathā tūrṇaṃ priyasurabhikusumaśarāsanaprasare // DKuṭṭ_61 //
children.translated_text: and how he quickly falls into the net of the bow of the one whose arrows are fragrant blossoms [<s>Kāma</s>]: // 61 //
'With a thick topknot set up, with hair arranged to a length of five fingers,
with a leaf-ornament placed in his drooping ear, fitting against his row of teeth, // 62 //
'wearing rings on his fingers and a golden necklace as ornaments,
his body anointed with saffron, wrapped in garments slightly yellowed [by it], // 63 //
'resplendent with a dangling garland of flowers and a gold ornament adorning his neck,
wearing shoes with <s>tauruṣkika</s> (Turkish) [incense] and other [fragrances] inserted within, sealed with wax, // 64 //
'with horse-hair tied to his head in bunches wound with threads of various colors,
in one ear a betel-leaf packet, in the other a lead foil, // 65 //
'wearing a lower garment of intense golden hue tinted with saffron,
and bearing around his neck a garland-necklace of thick glass beads, // 66 //
'with nails decorated with scorpion-marks, and a conch-and-discus emblem tied at the base of his hand,
followed by a servant carrying a betel-box, he who cultivates his first youth — // 67 //
'seated in the midst of a great arena of leading merchants, traders, rogues, and gamblers,
on a bench placed by the executioner's [/guard's] station, with a few sturdy legs, // 68 //
'attended by five or six retainers who place their swords on their laps, who speak roughly,
who bear themselves with great arrogance, // 69 //
with the front portion of his body wrapped in [a garment] placed on his back by a most skillful servant —
his cheek propped in his hand, the intervals [between studies] held back, puffed up with self-importance. // DKuṭṭ_70 //
Heedless of the context, again and again he recites with raised eyebrows,
mostly hymns and verses, with a mind lost in devotion, studying whatever comes. // DKuṭṭ_71 //
Rolling his head with wonder, from an excess of emotion, he strikes those seated beside him,
and with exclamations of 'Ah!' 'Alas!' 'Bravo!' he interrupts the hearing of another's fine speech. // DKuṭṭ_72 //

children.text: idamukto rahasi ruṣā tātena nṛpo nṛpeṇa tāto 'pi /
children.translated_text: 'Father told the king this in private, in anger; and the king told father this' —
thus he reveals to people the mutual trust and affection between his father and the king. // DKuṭṭ_73 //
Not knowing the art of leaf-cutting, or even if he does know some skill in the arts,

children.text: prakaṭayati janasamāje bibhrāṇaḥ patrakartarīṃ satatam // DKuṭṭ_74 //
children.translated_text: he always displays a leaf-cutting scissors in public gatherings, showing off. // DKuṭṭ_74 //
In the science of drama declared by <s>Brahmā</s>, in singing, and in playing the <s>muraja</s> (drum) and other instruments,
the skill of <s>Bhaṭṭaputra</s> (the minister's son) surpasses even <s>Nārada</s> and others. // DKuṭṭ_75 //
In <s>vasunanda</s>, <s>citradaṇḍaka</s>, <s>muktāyudha</s>, <s>khaḍga</s> (sword), <s>dhenu</s> (cow-hold), and <s>bandha</s> (lock) [wrestling techniques],

children.text: vrajati purato 'sya niyataṃ bhārgavatāṃ Paraśurāmo 'pi // DKuṭṭ_76 //
children.translated_text: even <s>Paraśurāma</s> of <s>Bhārgava</s> lineage would certainly walk behind him. // DKuṭṭ_76 //
He considers <s>Vātsyāyana</s> ignorant, <s>Maya</s> a fool, <s>Bābhravya</s> an outsider to be kept at a distance,

children.text: gaṇayati manmathatantre paśutulyaṃ rājaputraṃ ca // DKuṭṭ_77 //
children.translated_text: Master <s>Dattaka</s> and the prince as equal to animals in the science of love. // DKuṭṭ_77 //

children.text: yaḥ prārthito 'pi yatnātkavacaṃ rādhāsuto dadāti sma /
children.translated_text: The generosity of <s>Karṇa</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>'s son), who even when earnestly entreated used to give his armor [reluctantly] —
this one, who showers wealth without a thought, laughs at that virtue of giving. // DKuṭṭ_78 //
As for the lion, who displays his valor even against a deer whose sole instinct is to flee —

children.text: siṃhasya tasya śauryaṃ trapākaraṃ bhaṭṭaputrasya // DKuṭṭ_79 //
children.translated_text: that lion's courage is put to shame by <s>Bhaṭṭaputra</s>. // DKuṭṭ_79 //
Even in hunting there is excitement and victory over a moving target;

children.text: bhaṭṭabhayena na khelati bhaṭṭasutaḥ kiṃ tvatiprakaṭam // DKuṭṭ_80 //
children.translated_text: out of fear of his father (<s>Bhaṭṭa</s>), the son of <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> does not play — but why state what is so obvious? // DKuṭṭ_80 //
Thus, delighted inwardly by the pleasing words spoken by his own servant,
he says: 'This fellow is making a fool of me!' // DKuṭṭ_81 //

children.text: katamatkatamallagnaṃ prasthānaṃ kā ca nartakī bhadrā /
children.translated_text: 'On which date is the departure to which [festival]? Which dancer is the virtuous one?'
'Who dances at the crossroads following the techniques taught by <s>Kohala</s> and <s>Bharata</s>?' // DKuṭṭ_82 //

children.text: kīdṛk tvaṃ layamārge dhavalukaracite ca bhāṇake kīdṛk /
children.translated_text: 'How are you at rhythmic patterns? And how at the <s>dhaulaka</s> and <s>racita</s> [forms], and in the <s>bhāṇaka</s> [monologue]?' —
thus he eagerly questions the dance instructor about the performance from the very beginning. // DKuṭṭ_83 //
With a devoted heart, he removes the flower garland from his neck and presents it to the dancer,
and at the appropriate moment, with a mouthful of betel, offers a 'Bravo!' as well. // DKuṭṭ_84 //
The grace of arm movements, body positions, the charm of lifting and turning sideways —

children.text: anayaiva nirmitāni sthānakaśuddhiśca cāturasryaṃ ca // DKuṭṭ_85 //
children.translated_text: she alone has created these; and the purity of postures and the four-cornered symmetry too. // DKuṭṭ_85 //
With well-distributed emotional <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments), with varied gestures of <s>abhinaya</s> (dramatic representation), and with marvelous sequences of movements,
she surpasses even <s>Rambhā</s> (the celestial nymph) — what then of the rest of the mortal world of dancers? // DKuṭṭ_86 //
Thus, when the attendants have departed, without stopping, his neck stretched high with eagerness,
the connoisseur praises the performer, grasping only fragments of the metrical feet. // DKuṭṭ_87 //
'Generally, O child, the son of <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> behaves and dresses in this manner;'

children.text: taṃ madanavāgurāntaḥ pātayasi yathā tathā brūmaḥ // DKuṭṭ_88 //
children.translated_text: 'we shall tell you how to cast him into the snare of <s>Madana</s> (the god of love).' // DKuṭṭ_88 //
'A woman who is clever, bold, skilled in reading others' minds,
should be carefully employed as a messenger to him — one adorned with indirect speech.' // DKuṭṭ_89 //

children.text: sa upetya tayāvasare tāmbūlaṃ sumanasaśca dattvettham /
children.translated_text: 'She should approach him at the right moment, offer betel and flowers, and then',
'address him thus, O beautiful one, with words that kindle the fire of <s>Makaradhvaja</s> (the god of love):' // DKuṭṭ_90 //
'The accumulated merit of a thousand births has borne fruit for us today,
since you, O delight of the eyes, have come within the range of our vision.' // DKuṭṭ_91 //
A courtesan displays affection through the progression of flattery, love and lover's quarrels, and grief born of separation,
like an actress, through the discipline of her training. // DKuṭṭ_92 //
Whether elderly or in the bloom of youth, whether of low birth or of noble lineage,

children.text: rogavati dṛḍhaśarīre samacittā yoginaśca gaṇikāśca // DKuṭṭ_93 //
children.translated_text: whether ailing or of robust body — courtesans and yogis are equanimous [toward all]. // DKuṭṭ_93 //
Even when she has been lavishly attended, the public wife of a man whose wealth has been exhausted

children.text: pātayati dṛśaṃ vrajataḥ spṛhayā paridhānamātre 'pi // DKuṭṭ_94 //
children.translated_text: casts her glance at the departing one, longing even for his garment alone. // DKuṭṭ_94 //
Thus, for men whose minds have been firmly perfumed [with attachment], now before them,
is the telling of the bodiless arrow's wound inflicted by the beautiful women of the pleasure quarter. // DKuṭṭ_95 //
Merely because my friend, scorched by vain desire, having altogether discarded the gravity of propriety,

children.text: mukharayati māṃ durāśādagdhasakhī tena kathayāmi // DKuṭṭ_96 //
children.translated_text: importunes me — therefore I speak. // DKuṭṭ_96 //
'First, <s>Mālatī</s>'s heart was struck by the arrow of the flower-bowed one (<s>Kāma</s>),

children.text: caramaṃ ramaṇīvallabha locanaviṣayaṃ tvayā bhajatā // DKuṭṭ_97 //
children.translated_text: when you, O lord beloved of beautiful women, entered the range of her eyes.' // DKuṭṭ_97 //
'One moment her limbs are horripilated, the next she is in a state of excruciating burning pain;
one moment trembling has arisen, and the next moment her body is drenched in perspiration.' // DKuṭṭ_98 //
'Now she breaks into inexplicable laughter, now she abandons her composure and weeps loudly;

children.text: roditi gāyati ca punaḥ punaśca maunāvalambinī bhavati // DKuṭṭ_99 //
children.translated_text: then she sings, and yet again she lapses into silence.' // DKuṭṭ_99 //

children.text: patati muhuḥ paryaṅke muhuraṅke parijanasya muhuravanau /
children.translated_text: 'She falls now upon the couch, now into the lap of her attendants, now upon the ground,
now upon a bed of tender sprouts, now into water — burning with the fire of <s>Anaṅga</s> (bodiless Kāma).' // DKuṭṭ_100 //
'Like a buffalo cow smeared with mud, like a swan-hen encircled by lotus-stalk bracelets,
O handsome one, like a peahen she has become an enemy of serpents.' // DKuṭṭ_101 //
'Plantain, sandalwood paste, lotus, pearl-necklace, thick camphor,
moonstone and moonlight — none of these cool the fire of <s>Madana</s> (Kāma) burning her.' // DKuṭṭ_102 //

children.text: apasāraya ghanasāraṃ kuru hāraṃ dūra eva kiṃ kamalaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Take away the camphor, put aside the necklace, what use are lotuses?'

children.text: alamalamāli mṛṇālairiti vadati divāniśaṃ bālā // DKuṭṭ_103 //
children.translated_text: 'Enough, enough with lotus stalks, O garland-maker!' — thus the maiden speaks day and night. // DKuṭṭ_103 //
'Brought near in fantasy, her mind's activity surging,
she embraces you tightly; then, by the pressure of her own arms [finding nothing], she falls into embarrassment.' // DKuṭṭ_104 //
'The fragrance-bearing wind, the singing of cuckoos, the humming of bee-swarms —

children.text: iyamiyatī sāmagrī ghaṭitā vidhinaiva tadvināśāya // DKuṭṭ_105 //
children.translated_text: this much materiel has been assembled by Fate itself for her destruction.' // DKuṭṭ_105 //

children.text: abalāṃ balinā nītāṃ daśāmimāṃ makaraketunā rakṣa /
children.translated_text: 'Rescue this helpless woman, brought by the powerful <s>Makaraketu</s> (banner-of-the-sea-monster, i.e. Kāma) to this plight;

children.text: āpatpatitoddhṛtaye bhavati hi śubhajanmanāṃ janma // DKuṭṭ_106 //
children.translated_text: for the birth of the noble-born is for the deliverance of those who have fallen into danger.' // DKuṭṭ_106 //

children.text: no gṛhṇanti yathārthā arthijanairnigaditā giraḥ prāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Seekers of favors do not usually take literally the words spoken to them;

children.text: Mālatyā guṇaleśaṃ śṛṇu dhṛṣṭatayā tathāpi kathayāmi // DKuṭṭ_107 //
children.translated_text: even so, boldly I shall describe a fraction of <s>Mālatī</s>'s qualities — hear me.' // DKuṭṭ_107 //

children.text: āsphālayato nūnaṃ dhanuratanoḥ kausumaṃ rajaḥ patitam /
children.translated_text: 'Surely the pollen that fell when the bodiless one (<s>Kāma</s>) was twanging his floral bow

children.text: saṃhṛtya sā sumadhyā viśvasṛjā nirmitā tena // DKuṭṭ_108 //
children.translated_text: was gathered up, and from it the Creator fashioned her, that slender-waisted one.' // DKuṭṭ_108 //
'Her beauty, ever clinging [to <s>Śiva</s>], mocks the loveliness of the daughter of the Mountain (<s>Pārvatī</s>),
on account of which even half the body of the lord of serpents' ornament (<s>Śiva</s>) has not melted.' // DKuṭṭ_109 //
'She bears near her curling locks, dark as a row of bees,
what looks like the shadow of <s>Rāhu</s>'s mouth upon the half-orb of the moon.' // DKuṭṭ_110 //
'The lotus has unstable beauty, and the disc of the moon is devoid of playful charm —

children.text: kena sametu samatvaṃ hṛdayapriya Mālatīvadanam // DKuṭṭ_111 //
children.translated_text: with what can the face of <s>Mālatī</s> be compared, O heart's beloved?' // DKuṭṭ_111 //
'A bee, having hovered over her eyes, its superior quality indicated by the fragrance,
descends upon the lotus at her ear — even worthlessness is virtuous at the right moment.' // DKuṭṭ_112 //
'Upon her lower lip, which bears a natural redness that surpasses the luster of the <s>bandhujīva</s> (noon flower),
any application of <s>alaktaka</s> (lac dye) would be mere play at adornment for her.' // DKuṭṭ_113 //
'It is remarkable that slenderness belongs to her waist, which is grasped by folds [of skin];

children.text: athavā no vidhivihitā mahatāpyapanīyate tanutā // DKuṭṭ_114 //
children.translated_text: but then, thinness ordained by Fate cannot be removed even by the great.' // DKuṭṭ_114 //
'Leaving aside the rest — her broad hips, the dwelling-place of <s>Smara</s> (Kāma),
if they fall within the line of vision, would disturb even the meditation of the sage <s>Kapila</s>.' // DKuṭṭ_115 //
'Beholding the pair of thighs of that plantain-bodied one, [thighs] comparable to plantain [stems],
even <s>Makaradhvaja</s> (Kāma) himself would suddenly realize the purpose of his own arrow.' // DKuṭṭ_116 //
'She, moving languidly from the weight of her hips, has not come within the range of your eyes;

children.text: tiṣṭhati tena manohara Śarajanmā brahmacaryeṇa // DKuṭṭ_117 //
children.translated_text: therefore, O charming one, the flower-born one (<s>Kāma</s>) remains in the state of celibacy.' // DKuṭṭ_117 //
'If somehow <s>Madhusūdana</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) were to behold her — the very essence of the weaponless one's (<s>Kāma's</s>) arsenal —
he would consider the body of <s>Lakṣmī</s> placed upon his chest as a burden of worthlessness.' // DKuṭṭ_118 //

children.text: yadi patati sā kathaṃ cidvīkṣaṇaviṣayaṃ harasya tadavaśyam /
children.translated_text: 'If she were somehow to fall within the range of <s>Hara</s>'s (<s>Śiva</s>'s) vision, then certainly
reaching the other half of his body, she would make the three worlds inauspicious.' // DKuṭṭ_119 //
'That the Creator fashioned such unparalleled beauty, surpassing all women —
I consider that a mere coincidence, like a crow and a palm fruit.' // DKuṭṭ_120 //
'For one who has not beheld her body, the abode of innate grace,

children.text: manye nākādhipateḥ sahasramapi cakṣuṣāṃ viphalam // DKuṭṭ_121 //
children.translated_text: I consider even the thousand eyes of the lord of heaven (<s>Indra</s>) to be fruitless.' // DKuṭṭ_121 //

children.text: śithilayatu kusumacāpaṃ kṣipatu śarān bāṇadhau Manojanmā /
children.translated_text: 'Let the flower-bowed one (<s>Kāma</s>) loosen his bow, let him cast away his arrows in the quiver —

children.text: saṃsārasārabhūtā vicarati bhuvi Mālatī yāvat // DKuṭṭ_122 //
children.translated_text: so long as <s>Mālatī</s>, the very essence of existence, walks upon the earth.' // DKuṭṭ_122 //
'Whatever has been breathed forth by <s>Vātsyāyana</s>, <s>Madanodaya</s>, <s>Dattaka</s>, the courtesan's manual, the prince's guide, and others —
all of that dwells in the region of her heart.' // DKuṭṭ_123 //
'In [the works of] <s>Bharata</s>, <s>Viśākhila</s>, <s>Dattila</s>, and in tree-science, <s>Āyurveda</s>, painting, and <s>sūtra</s> literature,
in the art of leaf-cutting, in the craft of deception, and in the science of cooking and confections,' // DKuṭṭ_124 //

children.text: ātodyavādanavidhau nṛtte gīte ca kauśalaṃ tasyāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'in the art of playing instruments, in dance, and in song — her skill',

children.text: abhidhātuṃ yadi śakto vadanasahasreṇa bhogināmīśaḥ // DKuṭṭ_125 //
children.translated_text: 'even the lord of serpents (<s>Śeṣa</s>) with his thousand mouths could [barely] describe.' // DKuṭṭ_125 //
'With her garment slipping and swaying, unrestrained, <s>Mālatī</s> impetuously
falls upon [her lover] in private, her mind languid with the desire for love — but not for the unmeritorious.' // DKuṭṭ_126 //
'Her moaning at that moment, mingled with the sound of jingling bracelets from the vigorous striking of love's passion —
that does not reach the ears of one of little merit.' // DKuṭṭ_127 //
'If, when addressed thus, [he] remains indifferent in the midst of these virtues,
then the messenger, displaying anger, should address him thus:' // DKuṭṭ_128 //
'Is this the arrogance of good fortune? The pride of youth's play and beauty?

children.text: sahajapremopanatāṃ Mālatikāṃ na bahu manyase yena // DKuṭṭ_129 //
children.translated_text: Is this why you do not esteem <s>Mālatikā</s>, who has approached you with spontaneous love?' // DKuṭṭ_129 //

children.text: na gaṇayati yā kulīnān draviṇavataḥ śāstravedinaḥ praṇatān /
children.translated_text: 'She who does not regard noble-born men, wealthy men, learned men, or humble supplicants —

children.text: sā bhavadarthe śuṣyati kusthānaniveśitaṃ dhiganurāgam // DKuṭṭ_130 //
children.translated_text: she wastes away for your sake. Curse upon a love bestowed on the unworthy!' // DKuṭṭ_130 //
'A lotus in the fierce sun; a crescent moon on <s>Śambhu</s>'s (<s>Śiva</s>'s) head, which is full of ashes;

children.text: sā ca tvayi paśukalpe yadabhiratā tena me kṛśatā // DKuṭṭ_131 //
children.translated_text: that she is enamored of you, who are like a beast — that is the cause of my emaciation.' // DKuṭṭ_131 //
'Having clung to a <s>khadira</s> tree (acacia) — which is not straight, not juicy, hard, difficult to grasp, and not smooth —
is it any wonder that <s>Mālatikā</s> becomes an object of censure?' // DKuṭṭ_132 //
'Or rather, what fault is there? A crow, embarrassed by the disparity [in worth],

children.text: svādhīnāmapi sarasāṃ pariharati mṛṇālikāṃ dhvāṅkṣaḥ // DKuṭṭ_133 //
children.translated_text: avoids even the juicy lotus stalk that is freely available to him.' // DKuṭṭ_133 //

children.text: mātra kariṣyasi khedaṃ niṣṭhuramukto 'si yanmayā subhaga /
children.translated_text: 'Do not grieve, O handsome one, that I have spoken harshly to you;
for the harsh words spoken by a friend of an enamored young woman are an ornament to young men.' // DKuṭṭ_134 //
'Like moonlight to the moon, like the forest-garland to the slayer of <s>Kaṃsa</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>),
like the creeper of the flower-bow to the beloved of Spring (<s>Kāma</s>),' // DKuṭṭ_135 //
'like the playful intoxication of <s>Balarāma</s> (the plough-bearer), like a pearl necklace to a pair of breasts —

children.text: ramyāpi sā sugātrī ramyatarā bhavatu saṃgatā bhavatā // DKuṭṭ_136 //
children.translated_text: lovely as she already is, that fair-limbed one would be lovelier still united with you.' // DKuṭṭ_136 //

children.text: kiṃ bahunā yadi yūnāmupari vidhātuṃ samīhase caraṇam /
children.translated_text: 'In short, if you desire to place your foot upon the heads of all young men,
then quickly take this jewel among women, radiant with love, upon your lap.' // DKuṭṭ_137 //
Then, [the young man], heir to the dominion of <s>Madana</s> (Love), whose desire has blossomed from hearing those words,
O beautiful one, he who has come to your dwelling should be attended to by you in this manner: // DKuṭṭ 138 //
Rising from afar [to greet him], bowing, and offering your own seat —
with the edge of your garment, the washing of his pair of feet should be performed. // DKuṭṭ 139 //
Showing slightly, as if without effort, the armpit, the belly, the base of the arm, and the region of the breasts,
you shall quickly withdraw from the sight of the <s>nāyaka</s> (lover) in haste. // DKuṭṭ 140 //
Then, furnished with a couch, radiant with lamps, flowers, and the fragrance of incense,
beautiful with a spread canopy, [he is] led into the bedchamber. // DKuṭṭ 141 //
Your mother, O heavy-hipped one, having respectfully performed the welcoming rites and so forth,
should congratulate him with these special words, with great effort: // DKuṭṭ 142 //
"Today the blessings have borne fruit, today the chosen deities are satisfied;
the ornament of all auspiciousness — for he has adorned this dwelling! // DKuṭṭ 143 //
For <s>Kusumabāṇa</s> (the Flower-Arrowed one, Kāma), who is fashioning a fitting match,
the long labor of drawing his bow has at last borne fruit! // DKuṭṭ 144 //

children.text: vinyasya śirasi caraṇaṃ subhagā gaṇikājanasya sakalasya /
children.translated_text: Placing her foot upon the head of the entire community of courtesans, the fortunate one,
may the dear girl now raise aloft the victory-banner of good fortune! // DKuṭṭ 145 //
Daughters alone are praiseworthy — shame on the world that is satisfied with the birth of sons!
For through such an alliance, sons-in-law like you are obtained!" // DKuṭṭ 146 //
"Though one of firm acquaintance and a knower of qualities, though one like you is not fit to be asked for anything,
yet, O delight of my heart, I speak thus out of affection for my daughter: // DKuṭṭ 147 //

children.text: sahajapremopahṛtā nyastā tvayi Mālatī tathā kāryam /
children.translated_text: This <s>Mālatī</s>, entrusted to you, carried by innate love — may you act in such a way

children.text: na yathā bhavati varākī tvadvipriyajanmanāṃ śucāṃ vasatiḥ // DKuṭṭ_148 //
children.translated_text: that the poor girl does not become a dwelling-place of sorrows born from your displeasure." // DKuṭṭ 148 //
Wearing soft, washed, and perfumed garments, and unvulgar ornaments,
having absorbed the fragrance of incense, you shall stand near your lover, O slender one. // DKuṭṭ 149 //

children.text: sasnehaṃ savrīḍaṃ sasādhvasaṃ saspṛhaṃ ca paśyantī /
children.translated_text: Gazing with affection, with modesty, with trepidation, and with longing,
with your body somewhat visible, with sparse and charmingly playful conversation — // DKuṭṭ 150 //
When the mother has departed, and the chamber is free of attendants,

children.text: abhiyuñjāne ramaṇe vāmācaraṇaṃ kṣaṇaṃ kāryam // DKuṭṭ_151 //
children.translated_text: when the lover makes his advances, you should display a moment of coyness. // DKuṭṭ 151 //
When he, whose mind is set on the battle of love, pulls you forcefully to him,
acting with feigned resistance, you shall produce a slight contraction of your limbs. // DKuṭṭ 152 //
When the act of love has commenced, gradually revealing the genuine agitation of your heart,
you shall surrender your limbs without apprehension, without pretense, O daughter. // DKuṭṭ 153 //

children.text: yadyadvāñchati hantuṃ yaddaṃṣṭuṃ yacca vilikhituṃ gātram /
children.translated_text: Whatever limb he wishes to strike, to bite, or to scratch with his nails,
that very limb should be withdrawn with agitation, and then offered back again. // DKuṭṭ 154 //
At a bite, a pained exclamation of 'huṃ!'; in pressing and squeezing, various throat-sounds;
at nail-scratching, a hissing 'sīt!'; and at strikes, an excessive cry. // DKuṭṭ 155 //
Releasing short, labored breaths, your body bristling with goosebumps,
perspiring in every limb — you shall augment the passion of men. // DKuṭṭ 156 //
The sounds of cuckoos, quails, geese, pigeons, and horses' hearts [i.e., their sounds]
should be imitated by you at the appropriate time with sweet, melodious throat-sounds. // DKuṭṭ 157 //

children.text: mā mā māmatipīḍaya muñca kṣaṇamadaya no samarthāsmi /
children.translated_text: "Stop! Stop! Don't press me so hard! Release me for a moment, O heartless one! I cannot bear it!"
Thus, with stammering, indistinct syllables, you should address the lover. // DKuṭṭ 158 //
Compliance that follows his lead, coyness, boldness, and incapacity —

children.text: surateṣu darśayiṣyasi kāmukabhāvaṃ sphuṭaṃ buddhvā // DKuṭṭ_159 //
children.translated_text: in lovemaking you shall display these, having clearly perceived the lover's temperament. // DKuṭṭ 159 //
An improper, shameless conduct, with all composure cast far away, with an unbridled spread of passion —
such behavior you shall practice when the frenzy of love has intensified. // DKuṭṭ 160 //
Heedless of nail-scratches, with eyes half-closed, exhausted,
at the conclusion of the lover's act, you shall remain with limbs gone slack. // DKuṭṭ 161 //
Quickly [reaching for] the covering of the hips, [displaying] helpless slenderness, a smile with embarrassment,

children.text: khedālasāṃ ca dṛṣṭiṃ janayiṣyasi mohanacchede // DKuṭṭ_162 //
children.translated_text: and a gaze languid with fatigue — you shall produce these at the breaking of the swoon [of passion]. // DKuṭṭ 162 //
After the act of love has been performed, having touched water in a secluded spot,

children.text: prakṣālya pāṇipādaṃ sthitvā kṣaṇamāsane samūhya kacān // DKuṭṭ_163 //
children.translated_text: having washed the hands and feet, standing a moment on the seat, having gathered your hair, // DKuṭṭ 163 //
having applied mouth-fragrance, ascending the bed, having shown affection,

children.text: iti vakṣyasi taṃ ramaṇaṃ dṛḍhataramāliṅgya rabhasataḥ kaṇṭhe // DKuṭṭ_164 //
children.translated_text: you shall speak thus to that lover, embracing him tightly around the neck in haste: // DKuṭṭ 164 //
"O son of the <s>Bhaṭṭa</s>, surely your wife is dear to you, for, your heart being attached,
the embrace of another woman does not give you full satisfaction! // DKuṭṭ 165 //

children.text: saphalaṃ tasyā janma spṛhaṇīyā saiva sakalalalanānām /
children.translated_text: Fruitful is her birth, she alone is enviable among all women;

children.text: Gaurī tayaiva mahitā subhagaṅkaraṇaṃ tapastayācaritam // DKuṭṭ_166 //
children.translated_text: <s>Gaurī</s> is honored by her alone; the austerity for making one beloved has been performed by her! // DKuṭṭ 166 //
She alone is the abode of virtues, her lineage alone is always praiseworthy —

children.text: yasyāḥ śubhaśatabhājaḥ pāṇigrahaṇaṃ tvayā vihitam // DKuṭṭ_167 //
children.translated_text: she whose hand in marriage, the vessel of a hundred blessings, was received by you! // DKuṭṭ 167 //
Let that fortunate woman remain — she is the ornament of both families, the noble-hipped one,

children.text: yā nāpayāti bhavato Lakṣmīriva Narakavairiṇo hṛdayāt // DKuṭṭ_168 //
children.translated_text: who does not depart from your heart, like <s>Lakṣmī</s> from the heart of <s>Narakavairin</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>, the foe of <s>Naraka</s>)! // DKuṭṭ 168 //
Those upon whom you merely cast your water-lily-like eyes out of curiosity —

children.text: tā api satyaṃ sundara harṣollasitā na mānti gātreṣu // DKuṭṭ_169 //
children.translated_text: even they, O handsome one, truly do not remain composed in their limbs, being elated with joy!" // DKuṭṭ 169 //
"Even a slight affection from a lord usually makes light-minded [women] chatty;
since my mind is devoted to my own interest, I therefore make this request of you: // DKuṭṭ 170 //
Whether from intense passion and youth, or from fickleness, or from curiosity, or from tenderness,

children.text: madbhāgyasampadā vā dūtyā vā kauśalātsvabhāvādvā // DKuṭṭ_171 //
children.translated_text: or by the good fortune of my destiny, or through a messenger's skill, or by your own nature — // DKuṭṭ 171 //
This shoot of love shown to us, our means of livelihood —

children.text: bādhā nātra vidheyā gaṇikājanavṛttamanyathā buddhvā // DKuṭṭ_172 //
children.translated_text: let no harm be done to it by thinking otherwise of the ways of courtesans. // DKuṭṭ 172 //

children.text: yena snehaḥ krodhaḥ śāṭhyaṃ dākṣiṇyamārjavaṃ vrīḍā /
children.translated_text: For affection, anger, craftiness, courtesy, straightforwardness, and modesty —
these exist in them too, brought forth by the nature of being alive. // DKuṭṭ 173 //
For courtesans whose hearts are overpowered by intense love that arises without pretense,
who cannot bear separation from their beloved — their lives are [worth] but a blade of grass." // DKuṭṭ 174 //
"Now hear the wondrous tale I shall narrate of what happened —

children.text: adyāpi bibharti vaṭo viśeṣaṇaṃ yadabhisambandhāt // DKuṭṭ_175 //
children.translated_text: in connection with which, even today, the banyan tree bears its distinctive mark. // DKuṭṭ 175 //
There is a great city, the ornament of the earth, the home of <s>Sarasvatī</s>'s family,
known by the name <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>, eclipsing the abode of <s>Purandara</s> (Indra). // DKuṭṭ 176 //
As if fashioned by <s>Viśvakarman</s> as a model to show his own craft,

children.text: darśayituṃ nijaśilpaṃ varṇakamiva Viśvakarmaṇā vihitam // DKuṭṭ_177 //
children.translated_text: to <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) inquiring about the skill of creating the city of the three worlds — // DKuṭṭ 177 //
Not resorted to by misfortunes, not overcome by the fault of being overwhelmed,
not seized by calamities, untouched by the impurities of the <s>Kali</s> age — // DKuṭṭ 178 //
The netherworld [is famed] for its serpents, the ocean for its multitude of watery gems,
the celestial abode for its hosts of gods, the city of <s>Kuvera</s> for its accumulations of wealth — // DKuṭṭ 179 //
the abode of <s>Asuras</s> for its lovely women, the encampment of the Golden Mountain for its <s>Gandharvas</s>,
the city of <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) for its sacrificial posts, the dwelling of sages for its wealth of tranquility — // DKuṭṭ 180 //
Let alone the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> of intellect purified by the study of all <s>śāstras</s> —

children.text: sadasadguṇanirṇītau lalanā api nikaṣabhūmayo yasmin // DKuṭṭ_181 //
children.translated_text: even the women in that [city] are touchstones in the assessment of good and bad qualities! // DKuṭṭ 181 //
[<s>Dharma</s> (righteousness)] veiled in a blanket of smoke from the fire of sacrifice, out of fear of the <s>Kali</s> age,
though dwelling in concealment, is still inferred there by [his] deeds. // DKuṭṭ 182 //

children.text: apaharati pidhātumiva svakalaṅkaṃ śaśadharaḥ prasārya karān /
children.translated_text: As if to conceal his own blemish, the moon, extending his hands [of light],

children.text: rātrau yatra vadhūnāṃ lāvaṇyaṃ vadanakoṣebhyaḥ // DKuṭṭ_183 //
children.translated_text: steals at night the loveliness from the faces of the young brides there. // DKuṭṭ 183 //
Wearing dark garments the color of the curtain of darkness, the crowd of women on secret love-trysts
[goes forth], its own canopy of bodily radiance [serving] to thwart the union with their beloveds. // DKuṭṭ 184 //
Where the community of travelers, wounded by the sharp arrows flying from the corners of the eyes of full-hipped women,
relaxes their yearning for reunion with their own wives. // DKuṭṭ 185 //

children.text: yatra ca kulamahilānāmalpatvaṃ vacasi pāṇipāde ca /
children.translated_text: And where, in the women of good family, there is littleness in speech and in the hands and feet,
transparency in their hearts, and wideness in their restless, large eyes; // DKuṭṭ 186 //
heaviness in the burden of their full breasts, and density in the innate passion of the soul,
beauty of folds in the waist region, and [devotion] in the rites of worship of the family deity; // DKuṭṭ 187 //
depth in their nature and in the navel — the quiver of the flower-arrows of <s>Kāma</s>,
breadth in the hips and in the mind devoted to the worship of elders; // DKuṭṭ 188 //
in the deer-like, wide-eyed women — charm that steals the essence of lotuses,
curliness in the rows of curls, and the amorous play of youth. // DKuṭṭ 189 //
Restraint of the senses, [and] the <s>Rāhu</s>-demon of non-injury [grasping] the darkness [of evil],

children.text: stabdhatvaṃ sālatarau hāralatā taralasaṃgatā yasmin // DKuṭṭ_190 //
children.translated_text: stiffness in the <s>śāla</s> trees, and pearl-necklaces in the company of the trembling. // DKuṭṭ 190 //
The serpents there are those who look into others' cavities [i.e., faults]; the lips of beloveds are bitten;
the experience of needle-pain belongs to those engaged in the practice of dance. // DKuṭṭ 191 //
Though bent in body, yet exceedingly straightforward; though slow in gait, yet delightful —
such is the community of women there, devoted to the instruction of elders yet naturally naive. // DKuṭṭ 192 //
In that [city], purified by hundreds of sacrifices, the foremost among the twice-born, like <s>Puruhūta</s> (Indra) [himself],

children.text: gururiva vidyāvasatirvasati sma Purandaro nāmnā // DKuṭṭ_193 //
children.translated_text: the abode of learning, like a preceptor, dwelt one named <s>Purandara</s>. // DKuṭṭ 193 //
Who constantly mocked the truthfulness of the son of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>), the conquest of the Flower-Bow by the foe of the three cities (<s>Śiva</s>),

children.text: Harinābhipaṅkajabhuvo vijitendriyatāṃ jahāsa yaḥ satatam // DKuṭṭ_194 //
children.translated_text: and the mastery over the senses of <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) born from the navel-lotus. // DKuṭṭ 194 //

children.text: nyakkṛtavṛṣa iti Śarve yācaka iti kaustubhābharaṇe /
children.translated_text: In him who subdued the bull, there was no high regard for <s>Śarva</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) [as merely 'subduer of the bull']; nor for the wearer of the <s>Kaustubha</s> ornament [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] as 'a beggar';

children.text: pīḍitavasudhāsuta iti Kapile na babhūva yasya bahumānaḥ // DKuṭṭ_195 //
children.translated_text: nor for <s>Kapila</s> as 'the one who oppressed the sons of the earth (<s>Vasudhā</s>).' // DKuṭṭ 195 //
He who was keen in following the path [of dharma], yet averse to the destruction of the bodies of living beings, even while [appearing] avaricious;
who avoided another's wife, yet delighted in the women of his elders [i.e., ancestral traditions]. // DKuṭṭ 196 //
In whose great lineage, like a lake that is the natural dwelling of all living beings,
the birthplace of good conduct, the spread of the impurities of <s>Kali</s> was held in check — // DKuṭṭ 197 //
The taking up of the sword in the context of offerings to the ancestors was not from pride of valor;

children.text: truṭanaṃ mekhalikānāṃ vaṭukajane no ratājisaṃmarde // DKuṭṭ_198 //
children.translated_text: the breaking of girdles among the young was not in the crush of the battle of love. // DKuṭṭ 198 //
Disputes over the differences in Vedic recensions were not born from the anger of inheritance-division;

children.text: tejasvitā havirbhuji na śamaikarateṣu bhūmideveṣu // DKuṭṭ_199 //
children.translated_text: fiery splendor was in the sacrificial fire, not in those gods-on-earth (<s>Brāhmaṇas</s>) devoted solely to tranquility. // DKuṭṭ 199 //
Stumbling belonged only to the aged; the trembling of the lip only to those reciting prayers;

children.text: yajatāmeva samidhruci reṇājina eva kṛṣṇasamparkaḥ // DKuṭṭ_200 //
children.translated_text: the glow of kindling-sticks only to those performing sacrifice; contact with the dark belonged only to the deerskin. // DKuṭṭ 200 //
He had one son, who illuminated both sides of his entire family [maternal and paternal],

children.text: nāmnā Sundarasenaḥ Kaca iva vacasāmadhīśasya // DKuṭṭ_201 //
children.translated_text: named <s>Sundarasena</s>, like <s>Kaca</s> the [son] of the lord of speech (<s>Bṛhaspati</s>). // DKuṭṭ 201 //
Deeming that the Flower-Bow [Kāma] had been reduced to ashes by the fire of <s>Paśupati</s>'s (<s>Śiva</s>'s) eye,

children.text: aparamiva kusumacāpaṃ ratirataye nirmame Dhātā // DKuṭṭ_202 //
children.translated_text: <s>Dhātṛ</s> (the Creator) fashioned him, the handsome one, as another Flower-Bow, for the sake of <s>Rati</s>'s (Love's) pleasure. // DKuṭṭ 202 //
Let alone other women of good family — upon beholding his beauty,

children.text: sāpi mahāmunidayitā kṛcchreṇa rarakṣa cāritram // DKuṭṭ_203 //
children.translated_text: even the beloved of the great sage [<s>Arundhatī</s>] preserved her chastity only with difficulty! // DKuṭṭ 203 //
Seeing his broad chest, bearing the beauty of a golden plate,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā cirāya Lakṣmīrharihṛdaye duḥsthitaṃ mene // DKuṭṭ_204 //
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmī</s> long thought herself ill-placed upon the heart of <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>). // DKuṭṭ 204 //

children.text: kathamīdṛgyadi na kṛtaḥ śaśiśakalairatha kṛtaḥ kathaṃ vyathakaḥ /
children.translated_text: "How could he have been made thus, if not from moon-crescents? And yet, if so made, how is he painless [i.e., warm, not cold like the moon]?"
Thus, the company of women gazing at him could not arrive at a conclusion. // DKuṭṭ 205 //
He who had taken from the moon its serene form, from the mountain its firmness,

children.text: jaladharata unnatatvaṃ gāmbhīryaṃ yādasāṃ patyuḥ // DKuṭṭ_206 //
children.translated_text: loftiness from the clouds, depth from the lord of waters,

children.text: yo vinayasya nivāso vaidagdhyasyāśrayaḥ sthiteḥ sthānam /
children.translated_text: He who is the abode of modesty, the refuge of wit, the foundation of steadfastness,
the temple of kind words, the dwelling-place of virtuous conduct,
He who is <s>Madana</s> (the god of love) for women, the moon for the lotus-cluster of good people,
the touchstone of virtues, and the roadside tree for the community of travelers,
Devoted to the company of good people, a touchstone for the essence of poetry and stories,
a wish-fulfilling tree for his dear ones, and a playground for the sports of <s>Lakṣmī</s> (the goddess of fortune),
like the ocean and the moon, waxing and waning together with his friend,
pure under every test — such was the one named <s>Guṇapālita</s>.

children.text: tena samaṃ sa kadā cittiṣṭhanrahasi prasaṅgataḥ patitām /
children.translated_text: Once, while standing alone with him in a secluded place, by chance
he suddenly heard this noble verse being sung by someone:
"Those who do not learn the customs, natures, and speech of foreign lands,

children.text: samupāsate na ca gurūnviṣāṇavikalāsta ukṣāṇaḥ // DKuṭṭ_212 //
children.translated_text: and do not attend upon teachers — they are oxen lacking horns."
Having heard this, <s>Sundara</s> then spoke these words to his chief friend:
"This is a fine song, <s>Guṇapālita</s>, well sung by this person.
The conduct of good men, the deeds of the wicked, the various cries of the marketplace,
the humor devised by the clever, the crooked tales told by loose women,
the discussion of weighty and abstruse treatises, the ways of libertines, the tricks of swindlers,
the earth with its ocean-moats — a man who wanders about comes to know all this.
Therefore, abandoning the meager comforts of staying at home, in the prospect of manifold gains,

children.text: sthāpaya gamanārambhe vayasya hṛdayaṃ mayā sahitaḥ // DKuṭṭ_216 //
children.translated_text: set your heart upon commencing the journey, my friend, together with me."
To him who had spoken thus, his companion whose soul was eager for superior gains,

children.text: ūce Sundarasenaṃ lajjita iva sahacaro vacanam // DKuṭṭ_217 //
children.translated_text: the companion spoke these words to <s>Sundarasena</s>, as if embarrassed:

children.text: abhyarthanānubandho lajjākara eva mādṛśāṃ kiṃ tu /
children.translated_text: "The persistence of entreaty is indeed embarrassing for people like me; however,

children.text: ākarṇaya kathayāmaḥ pathikānāṃ yāni duḥkhāni // DKuṭṭ_218 //
children.translated_text: listen — let me tell you the sufferings of travelers.
His body covered in rags, his strength exhausted by the toil of long roads,
grey with clouds of dust, at the end of the day he seeks shelter:

children.text: mātarbhagini dayāṃ kuru mā maivaṃ niṣṭhurā bhava tavāpi /
children.translated_text: 'Mother, sister, show mercy! Do not be so harsh — even your own

children.text: kāryavaśena gṛhebhyo niryānti bhrātaraśca putrāśca // DKuṭṭ_220 //
children.translated_text: brothers and sons leave their homes when compelled by duty.'

children.text: kiṃ vayamutpāṭya gṛhaṃ prātargantāra īdṛgeva satām /
children.translated_text: 'Are we going to uproot your house? We shall leave in the morning.' Such is the lot of good folk —

children.text: bhavati nivāso yasminnija iva pathikāḥ prayānti viśrāmam // DKuṭṭ_221 //
children.translated_text: a house where travelers find rest as if it were their own.

children.text: adya rajanīṃ nayāmo yathā kathaṃ cittvadāśraye mātaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Somehow we shall pass this night under your shelter, mother;

children.text: astaṅgato vivasvānvada samprati kutra gacchāmaḥ // DKuṭṭ_222 //
children.translated_text: the sun has set — tell us, where shall we go now?'
Thus, uttering various pitiful words, standing at the doorway of house after house,
the wretch is rebuked by the housewives, who say:

children.text: na sthita iha gehapatiḥ kiṃ raṭasi vṛthā prayāhi devakulam /
children.translated_text: 'The master of the house is not here; why do you cry out in vain? Go to the temple.'

children.text: kathite 'pi nāpagacchati paśya manuṣyasya nirbandham // DKuṭṭ_224 //
children.translated_text: 'Even after being told, he does not leave — look at the man's obstinacy!'

children.text: atha yadi kathaṃ cidaparaḥ punaḥ punaryācito gṛhasvāmī /
children.translated_text: Then, if somehow another householder, entreated again and again,
points with contempt to a crumbling corner of the house saying 'Sleep here' —
there the wife quarrels for a whole watch of the night,

children.text: ajñātāya kimarthaṃ vāso dattastvayeti saha bhartrā // DKuṭṭ_226 //
children.translated_text: fighting with her husband: 'Why have you given lodging to a stranger?'

children.text: īdṛgayaṃ saralātmā kiṃ kuruṣe bhagini tāvako bhartā /
children.translated_text: 'Such is your simple-natured husband, sister — what can you do?

children.text: sthāsyasi gehe 'vahitā bhramanti khalu vañcakā evam // DKuṭṭ_227 //
children.translated_text: You will stay at home unguarded — such cheats do indeed wander about like this.'
Thus, having set her mind on begging for utensils and such from the neighboring house,
a woman who has come over speaks to her with an air of intimacy.
Having wandered past more than a hundred houses, the traveler, tormented by hunger,
eats the alms collected together — rice, horse-gram, small chickpeas, lentils, and the like.
His food is at another's mercy, the earth is his bed, a temple is his house —
fate has made a piece of brick the traveler's pillow.
When he had spoken thus, and at the next opportunity for <s>Sundarasena</s>,
this song was sung by someone in the course of conversation:
"For men whose minds are fixed solely on their desired goal, their own excellent home is a temple of the gods, the surface of the earth is a most delightful bed,
and meager food is <s>amṛta</s> (ambrosia)."
And having heard this, the son of <s>Paurandara</s> said to his friend with delight:

children.text: mama hṛdayagataṃ prakaṭitametena sataiva bhavatu gacchāvaḥ // DKuṭṭ_233 //
children.translated_text: "This person has revealed what is in my heart — so be it, let us go!"
Then, with his companion as his second, his mind resolved to plunge into the ocean of hardships,
<s>Sundarasena</s> departed from <s>Kusumapura</s> (Pāṭaliputra), unnoticed by his father.
Observing the gatherings of the witty, practicing all manner of weapons,
comprehending the meanings of the <s>śāstras</s> (treatises), beholding various curiosities,
learning the arts of leaf-cutting, painting, and wax-modeling,
dance enriched with song, and the various kinds of playing stringed instruments, drums, and the like,
understanding the wiles of cheats, the crooked tales and jests of libertines and courtesans —
<s>Sundarasena</s>, accompanied by his friend, wandered over the entire earth.
Then, having mastered all the <s>śāstras</s> (treatises), having learned the ways of all people,
desiring to return home, he reached the mountain <s>Arbuda</s> (Mount Abu).
Recognizing that <s>Sundara</s> was eager to see its summit,
<s>Guṇapālita</s> said: "Behold this king of mountains!"
"This one, endowed with cool, clear waters streaming from its plateau slopes,
was placed in the desert by the <s>Himālaya</s> (the snowy mountain), as if out of compassion for the world.
With a crest graced by the cool-rayed moon, with ascetics dwelling on its slopes who feed on wind, possessing caves,
frequented by <s>Vidyādharas</s> (celestial beings), it bears the splendor of <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva) himself.
Here, thinking 'flowers are united with the treetops' — having formed this conviction, I believe —

children.text: abhilaṣati samuccetuṃ tārā niśi mugdhakāminīsārthaḥ // DKuṭṭ_242 //
children.translated_text: a troop of innocent young women longs to pluck the stars at night.
It is a wonder that beside this mountain even the seven <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages) stand still;

children.text: athavā kasyākarṣaṃ na karoti samunnatirmahatām // DKuṭṭ_243 //
children.translated_text: but then, whose admiration does the eminence of the great not compel?
Perceiving that the path through the sky for the horses of the sun is without support,

children.text: ayamavanidharo manye viśrāntyai vedhasā vihitaḥ // DKuṭṭ_244 //
children.translated_text: I think this mountain was fashioned by <s>Brahmā</s> (the Creator) as a resting place for them.
Having resorted to this mountain, the herbs of the cool-rayed moon have come into proximity;
nearness to a lord is generally obtained through the favor of his benefactors.
As if to water the elephants of the directions, this mountain releases
showers of waterfall droplets, wearied from bearing the earth — for there is indeed fellow-feeling among those engaged in a common task.
Its beauty carried off by <s>hārīta</s> (green pigeons), gladdened by parrots, lovely with the repose of <s>Vyāsa</s> (the sage),
with <s>bharadvāja</s> (skylarks) resting upon it — this mountain rivals the hermitage of sages.
On this mountain, there are those who are free from attachment, who strive for the means to attain the next world,

children.text: gandhavahabhojanā api na hiṃsakāḥ phalabhujo 'pi na plavagāḥ // DKuṭṭ_248 //
children.translated_text: who feed on wind, yet are not harmful; who eat fruits, yet are not monkeys;

children.text: śubhakarmaikaratā api ṣaṭkarmāṇo yatā api svavaśāḥ /
children.translated_text: who are devoted solely to auspicious deeds, who perform the six duties, who are self-controlled yet self-reliant,

children.text: anabhimataraudracaritāḥ Śivapriyā api vasanti śamaniratāḥ // DKuṭṭ_249 //
children.translated_text: who are averse to terrible conduct, who are dear to <s>Śiva</s>, and who dwell devoted to tranquility.
Like an embodiment of the cool-rayed moon — marked with a deer, adorned with the seven leaves (the constellation);
like the path of the blazing sun — covered with <s>palāśa</s> (flame-of-the-forest) trees; like the wife of a <s>Rākṣasa</s> (demon) —
as if filled with longing — in rut; as if dressed for a tryst — adorned with <s>tilaka</s> (trees);
graced with <s>dhava</s>, <s>hari</s> (yellow), and <s>pīlu</s> trees — like the courtyard before a king's palace;
covered with thickets of <s>Arjuna</s> trees and <s>bāṇa</s> (arrow-grass) — like the army of the lord of the <s>Kurus</s>;
filled with thousands of bears — like the splendor of the celestial realm;
like the army of the <s>Dānavas</s> (demons) — abounding in <s>riṣṭaka</s> (soap-nut) trees; like the night —
with fireflies and <s>rohiṇī</s> (red stars) — this lovely mountain slope shines.

children.text: iti darśayati vayasye Sundarasene ca paśyati prītyā /
children.translated_text: While he was thus showing his friend, and while <s>Sundarasena</s> was looking with delight,
this song, fitting the occasion, was sung by someone:
"Those who behold the summit of <s>Arbuda</s>, which surpasses the ridge of heaven —

children.text: bahuviṣayaparibhramaṇaṃ manye kleśāya kevalaṃ teṣām // DKuṭṭ_255 //
children.translated_text: for them, I think, much wandering through various lands has been merely for this end."

children.text: ākarṇya ca sa babhāṣe mahātmanānena yuktamupagītam /
children.translated_text: And having heard this, he said: "What this great soul has sung is fitting.

children.text: śikhariśiraḥ paśyāmo vayasya ramyaṃ samāruhya // DKuṭṭ_256 //
children.translated_text: Let us see the lovely mountain peak, my friend, by climbing up."
Then, having ascended the excellent mountain, gazing at the various temples of the gods,
at the pools, the garden grounds, the lakes, and the rivers, he wandered about in wonder.
Like a flash of lightning bereft of clouds, like moonlight dimmed without the moon,

children.text: Ratimiva Manmatharahitāṃ śriyamiva Harivakṣasaḥ patitām // DKuṭṭ_258 //
children.translated_text: like <s>Rati</s> without <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love), like <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune) fallen from the chest of <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu) —
the choicest handiwork of <s>Vidhātṛ</s> (the Creator), the essence of all living beings,
the exemplar of all things beautiful, the victorious weapon of the mind-born one (<s>Kāma</s>) —
resplendent with blossoming flowers, the sole graceful swan on the river of the <s>śṛṅgāra rasa</s> (erotic sentiment),
a playful tendril-vine of grace, an arrow piercing the armor of concentration of ascetics —
wandering on the ground made lovely by heaps of flowers in the garden pavilion,
he beheld a young woman enjoying herself with her friend.
As he gazed at her, having become a target for the arrows of <s>Smara</s> (the god of love),
this thought remained long in the mind of him who was overwhelmed by a weight of wonder:
"Where indeed has this most extraordinary skill of the Creator arisen,

children.text: yena viruddhānāmapi ghaṭitaikatra sthitistathā hīyam // DKuṭṭ_263 //
children.translated_text: by which even mutually opposed qualities have been united and made to abide together? For she is:
graceful in body and flawless; radiant with brilliant, sparkling stars (eyes) and captivating;
with a lotus-face beyond description; with a voice that surpasses the sound of the <s>vīṇā</s>;
with a body of well-arranged form and beautifully fashioned joints and limbs;
rich with high breasts; and radiant as the rays of the autumn moon;
with a gait of pleasing grace, and feet of praised arrangement;
with an exceedingly broad hip region, and a beauty that pervades her entire body."
Then, as love manifested, she too suddenly cast a sidelong glance,

children.text: sāpi babhūva mṛgākṣī hastagatā Kusumacāpasya // DKuṭṭ_267 //
children.translated_text: and that doe-eyed one fell into the hands of <s>Kusumacāpa</s> (the flower-bowed god of love).
As she took shelter at the foot of a tree, instantly forgetting all other activities,
on her creeper-like body, the <s>sāttvika bhāvas</s> (involuntary physical responses) began to sprout.
That very splendor of the garden, at that very moment, remembering <s>Smara</s> (the god of love),

children.text: tāṃ vyathayitumārebhe prabhorhi kṛtyaṃ karoti khalu sarvaḥ // DKuṭṭ_269 //
children.translated_text: began to torment her — for everyone indeed carries out the work of their lord.
From her limbs, moist as fresh firewood, perspiration flowed forth,
as if from wood being burned by the fire of <s>Manobhava</s> (Love) kindled within.
Fallen into the net of <s>Kusumaśara</s> (the flower-arrowed god), making repeated rolling movements of her eyes,

children.text: animeṣaṃ paśyantī matsyavadhūmanucakāra sā tanvī // DKuṭṭ_271 //
children.translated_text: gazing without blinking, that slender one imitated the wife of a fish.
Her body rigid, yet trembling; covered with goosebumps; perspiring; sighing —

children.text: vidadhe tāmasamaśaraḥ krīḍati hi śaṭho viśiṣṭamāsādya // DKuṭṭ_272 //
children.translated_text: the unequal-arrowed one (<s>Kāma</s>) made her thus, for the rogue plays indeed when he finds a worthy target.
The heaving of her pair of breasts with her sighs, the elegance of her coquetry,
the captivating tenderness of her eyes caused by the love she yearned for,

children.text: anuraktyā vadanaruciṃ vacasi ca gamane ca sādhvasaskhalanam /
children.translated_text: the glow on her face from passion, and the faltering from bashfulness in her speech and gait —
Love, acting upon her, brought her an excess of charm. // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 274 //
Even with her beloved near her side, though struck by the shower of <s>Kāma</s>'s arrows,

children.text: na śaśāka sābhidhātuṃ cittagataṃ praṇayabhaṅgato bhītā // DKuṭṭ_275 //
children.translated_text: she was unable to speak what was in her heart, afraid of a breach of modesty. // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 275 //
Then <s>Ālī</s>, knowing the state of her mind, drawing her dear friend whose gaze was fixed,

children.text: Madanena dahyamānāṃ vihasitaviśadaṃ jagāda tāmālī // DKuṭṭ_276 //
children.translated_text: said with a bright smile to her who was being burned by <s>Madana</s> (Love). // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 276 //
"O <s>Hāralatā</s>, put away the agitation of the body burned by <s>Hara</s>'s wrathful roar!
True affection born of genuine feeling is not a commodity for courtesans." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 277 //
"Reject the man devoid of wealth; show regard for a man of ample fortune.

children.text: asmādṛśāṃ hi mugdhe dhanasiddhyai rūpanirmāṇam // DKuṭṭ_278 //
children.translated_text: For us, O innocent one, the creation of beauty is for the acquisition of wealth." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 278 //
"Bestowing attachment on a charming man without regard for gaining wealth,
you are laughed at, O slender-waisted one, by the assemblies of experienced courtesans." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 279 //
"Those whose youth is praiseworthy, upon whom fortune has smiled,

children.text: phalitaṃ yeṣāṃ sukṛtaṃ jīvitasukhitārthitā yeṣām // DKuṭṭ_280 //
children.translated_text: whose merit has borne fruit, who desire the pleasures of life — // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 280 //
they will inevitably pursue you of their own accord, pierced by <s>Madana</s>'s arrows.

children.text: na hi madhulehāḥ sundari mṛgyante cūtamañjaryā // DKuṭṭ_281 //
children.translated_text: For honey-bees are not sought out by the mango blossoms, O beautiful one!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 281 //
When <s>Ālī</s> had spoken thus, <s>Hāralatā</s>, her whole body shattered by the storm of Love's arrows,
spoke with difficulty, her syllables faltering indistinctly: // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 282 //
"Friend, make an effort now, for when one is overwhelmed by the great pain that has no remedy,

children.text: kroḍīkṛtā vipattyā na bhavantyupadeśayogyā hi // DKuṭṭ_283 //
children.translated_text: one seized by calamity is no longer fit for advice." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 283 //
"My beloved is not in my power; the gentle breeze, the garden fragrant with flowers —

children.text: iyatī khalu sāmagrī bhavati kṣīṇāyuṣāmeva // DKuṭṭ_284 //
children.translated_text: such a combination indeed occurs only for those whose life is nearing its end." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 284 //
Understanding that <s>Ālī</s> was agitated in body by the force of the poison of <s>Madana</s>'s serpent,
<s>Paurandarī</s> (<s>Śaśiprabhā</s>) approached and said with a bow: // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 285 //
"Even if the embarrassment born of the courtesan's nature obstructs speech,

children.text: tadapi kathitavyameva snigdhāpadi na hi nirūpyate yuktam // DKuṭṭ_286 //
children.translated_text: still it must be told — in a friend's calamity, propriety is not to be weighed." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 286 //

children.text: etāvati saṃsāre parigaṇitā eva te sujanmānaḥ /
children.translated_text: "In this entire world, those of noble birth can be counted

children.text: āpatsu paritrāṇavyākulamanasāṃ sphuranti ye buddhau // DKuṭṭ_287 //
children.translated_text: who, when calamities arise, appear in the mind with hearts anxious for rescue." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 287 //

children.text: yasminneva muhūrte cakṣurviṣayaṃ gato 'si mama sakhyāḥ /
children.translated_text: "From the very moment you came within the sight of my friend,

children.text: tata evārabhya gatā vidheyatāṃ dagdhamadanasya // DKuṭṭ_288 //
children.translated_text: from that very instant, the one burned by Love surrendered her will to you." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 288 //
"Piercing through the armor of her bristling hair, they fell upon her inner being —
those arrows released from the bow of the Mind-born (<s>Kāma</s>) within her heart." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 289 //

children.text: kiṃ vidadhātu varākī kutra samāśvasitu yātu kaṃ śaraṇam /
children.translated_text: "What is the poor girl to do? Where shall she find solace? To whom shall she go for refuge?

children.text: pīḍayati bhṛśaṃ yasyā nityaśucirdakṣiṇo mṛduḥ pavanaḥ // DKuṭṭ_290 //
children.translated_text: She who is so painfully tormented by the ever-pure, southerly, gentle breeze?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 290 //
"When her voice has become choked with sobs, the cuckoos, abandoning their long vow of silence,

children.text: hṛṣṭā vyathayanti sakhīṃ jātāvasarā nirargalaṃ virutaiḥ // DKuṭṭ_291 //
children.translated_text: joyfully torment my friend unrestrainedly with their cries, having found their opportunity." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 291 //
"When her gait becomes stumbling and confused, the geese, tireless, with the slender-limbed girl,
having long found their opportunity, contentedly strut back and forth." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 292 //
"Even though burned by the breezes of her warm sighs, the bee upon her

children.text: alakakusumaṃ na muñcati kṛcchreṣvapi dustyajā viṣayāḥ // DKuṭṭ_293 //
children.translated_text: does not release the flower in her hair — in times of distress, the objects of sense are hard to abandon." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 293 //

children.text: no vārayasi tathā māṃ sāmpratamiti kathayatīva madhulehaḥ /
children.translated_text: "'You do not ward me off as before now!' — thus the bee seems to say,
buzzing at the ear of her whose body is without strength, clinging to the flower worn as an ear-ornament." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 294 //
"From her loosened creeper-like arm, her golden bracelet has fallen;
its reaching the ground — in that indeed lies the cause of her open-handedness." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 295 //
"Loosened by the string of her girdle at one step from her buttocks — how wondrous!
But then, association with the wife of a great one is surely destined to end in a fall." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 296 //
"Having taken Love to her breast, though the necklace was thus cherished, once broken,
it torments my friend at once — from what is shattered within, whence can come well-being?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 297 //
"The sweat-water staining her garment, mixed with tears darkened by collyrium,
falling upon the surface of her breasts, imitates the confluence of waters at <s>Prayāga</s>." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 298 //
"Tormented by the five fires — the cuckoo's call, the Malaya breeze, flowers, <s>Smara</s> (Love), and the bee —
the young woman performs the <s>pañcatapas</s> (five-fire penance), yearning for the pleasure of your embrace." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 299 //

children.text: na parāṃ patati varākī daśamīṃ yāvanmanobhavāvasthām /
children.translated_text: "The poor girl has not yet fallen to the tenth and final stage of Love's sickness;

children.text: trāyasva subhaga tāvaccharaṇāgatarakṣaṇaṃ vrataṃ mahatām // DKuṭṭ_300 //
children.translated_text: save her meanwhile, O fortunate one — the protection of those who seek refuge is the vow of the great." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 300 //
Then, upon hearing her words, realizing with respect that Love had arisen in the girl,
<s>Guṇapālita</s>, fearful of disgrace in his heart, said to his friend: // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 301 //

children.text: yadyapi Māraprasaro durvāraḥ prāṇināṃ nave vayasi /
children.translated_text: "Though <s>Māra</s>'s (Love's) assault is irresistible for living beings in the bloom of youth,

children.text: cintyaṃ tadapi vivekibhiravasānaṃ veśayoṣitāṃ premṇaḥ // DKuṭṭ_302 //
children.translated_text: the wise should still reflect upon the end-result of love for courtesans." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 302 //
"The fickle love, passion, desire, lust, and lovesickness of courtesans
are well known to wax and wane along with one's wealth, O friend." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 303 //
"How could a man of noble birth consort with those women
for whom a lover seen for a moment and one of deep-rooted affection are both equally unprecedented?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 304 //

children.text: pradyumnaḥ pradyumno virūpakaḥ khalu virūpakaḥ satatam /
children.translated_text: "<s>Pradyumna</s> is <s>Pradyumna</s> (handsome); the ugly one is always ugly;

children.text: susnigdhaḥ susnigdho rūkṣo rūkṣastu gaṇikānām // DKuṭṭ_305 //
children.translated_text: the affectionate is affectionate, and the harsh is harsh — all according to the courtesans' reckoning of wealth." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 305 //

children.text: yāsāṃ jaghanāvaraṇaṃ parakautukavṛddhaye na tu trapayā /
children.translated_text: "For those women, the covering of their hips is for increasing others' curiosity, not out of modesty;

children.text: ujjvalaveṣā racanā kāmijanākṛṣṭaye na tu sthitaye // DKuṭṭ_306 //
children.translated_text: brilliant attire and adornment are for attracting lovers, not for their own sake." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 306 //
"Their consumption of meat is for the suffering it inflicts on men (through seduction), not from craving;

children.text: ālekhyādau vyasanaṃ vaidagdhyakhyātaye na tu vinodaḥ // DKuṭṭ_307 //
children.translated_text: their devotion to painting and such arts is for the fame of their sophistication, not for amusement." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 307 //

children.text: rāgo 'dhare na cetasi saralatvaṃ bhujalatāsu na prakṛtau /
children.translated_text: "The colour is on their lips, not in their hearts; straightness is in their creeper-like arms, not in their nature;
the eminence is in the weight of their breasts, not in conduct that the virtuous would approve." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 308 //
"Heaviness is in their hips, not in their treatment of noble men whose wealth has been extracted;
laziness is in their manner of walking, not in their schemes for deceiving men." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 309 //
"Discrimination of complexion belongs to their cosmetics, not to their choice in amorous encounters;
the clinging of passion is to their lips, not in their exclusive devotion to any particular man." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 310 //
"They are passionate even with a boy, inflamed with desire even with the old,
lovely-eyed even with the impotent, and longing even for the chronically ill." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 311 //
"Covered with drops of sweat (that are feigned), with garments whose dampness does not arise from genuine feeling,
displaying trembling (that is contrived), and hard as thunderbolt-stone at their core —" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 312 //
"fickle-hipped, ignoble, cuckoos (nurtured by others), with artificially reddened eyes,
skilled at surrendering every limb, yet never yielding the region of the heart —" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 313 //
"though not born of a serpent-family, they are expert in inflicting the pain of a serpent's bite;
though lamps of <s>Kandarpa</s> (Love), they are devoid of any connection with real affection." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 314 //
"Though having abandoned the coupling with bulls, they are indifferent to any particular man in the act of love;
though devoted solely to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (dark things/money), they forever love <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> (gold-cushioned wealth)." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 315 //
"Like the slopes of Mount <s>Meru</s>, their hips are frequented by thousands of <s>Kimpuruṣas</s> (sub-human lovers);
like the policies of kings, they are well-guarded against unprofitable associations." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 316 //
"Like lotuses, they flourish from the scraping of many friends' hands (wealth extracted from many patrons);
like <s>Ḍākinīs</s>, they are endowed with the skill of extracting blood (wealth) by attraction." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 317 //
"Present for every man, devoted to their purpose, enriched by various transformations,

children.text: bahulārthagrāhiṇyaḥ prakṛtaya iva durgrahā gaṇikāḥ // DKuṭṭ_318 //
children.translated_text: seizing abundant wealth — courtesans are like the <s>prakṛtis</s> (material nature), hard to comprehend." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 318 //

children.text: sādaramāśliṣya ciraṃ kusumastabakaṃ ca naraviśeṣaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: "Embracing with affection for a long time both a cluster of flowers and a particular man,

children.text: riktīkartuṃ nipuṇaṃ kṣudrāḥ kṣudrāśca cumbanti // DKuṭṭ_319 //
children.translated_text: bees and base women are skilled at draining them both dry." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 319 //

children.text: paramārthakaṭhorā api viṣayagataṃ lohakaṃ manuṣyaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: "Hard at the core in reality, yet they attract both iron and a wealthy man —
lodestones and women who live by their beauty both draw them in." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 320 //
"Constantly mounted by males, adorned with artificial passion and erotic charm,
beaten on the haunches — such are both she-elephants and courtesans." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 321 //
"Though raised up by proper qualities (or proper weights), when a piece of gold is placed before them,

children.text: jhagiti patanti mukhena prakaṭapramadāḥ kalādhikāśca tulāḥ // DKuṭṭ_322 //
children.translated_text: they instantly fall face-first — brazen women and scales alike, the latter being more skilled in the art." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 322 //
"Beautiful on the outside, hollow within, hard by nature —

children.text: dāsyaḥ samudgikā iva maṇanti yantraprayogeṇa // DKuṭṭ_323 //
children.translated_text: slave-girls and cosmetic boxes alike function only through the application of mechanical contrivance." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 323 //
"Those ill-fated men who form attachments to those courtesans

children.text: te niḥsaranti niyataṃ pāṇidvayamagrataḥ kṛtvā // DKuṭṭ_324 //
children.translated_text: will inevitably depart with both hands held out empty before them." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 324 //
While he was thus advising his friend <s>Sundarasena</s>, tormented by love,
a set of three songs was sung by someone who had come from the vicinity: // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 325 //
