"He who, having subdued through memory a beautiful young woman of lovely form brought before him,

children.text: pariharati yo jaḍātmā prathamo 'sau nāliko vinā bhrāntim // DKuṭṭ_326 //
children.translated_text: then rejects her — that dull-witted man is the first fool, beyond doubt." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 326 //
"For this alone is the fruit of birth, this alone the fruit of life for men —
that youth passes in the pleasure of union with women of ample, swaying hips." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 327 //
"Their whole bodies being consumed by the rows of flames from the fire-arrows of the Flower-god,
women of intense love do not yearn for men of little merit." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 328 //
Having listened to these words, the son of <s>Purandara</s> (<s>Indra</s>) said to his friend:

children.text: mama hṛdayādiva kṛṣṭvā gītamidaṃ sādhunānena // DKuṭṭ_329 //
children.translated_text: "This song has been well drawn, as if from my very heart, by him. // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 329 //
So let us go to console <s>Hāralatā</s>, distressed by the Bodiless One's (<s>Kāma</s>'s) arrows, with her trembling fawn-like eyes.

children.text: āśvāsayituṃ yāmo guṇapālita kiṃ vikalpitairbahubhiḥ // DKuṭṭ_330 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Guṇapālita</s>, what use are many deliberations?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 330 //

children.text: atha yatra kāpi gaṇikā gaṇayantī paricitaṃ hṛtadraviṇam /
children.translated_text: Then a certain courtesan, reckoning up a familiar patron whose wealth had been taken,
blocked him with the pretext of jealousy just as he was entering her house. // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 331 //
Another courtesan, seeing a lover who had been tricked reduced to tattered old clothes,

children.text: veśyā viṣīdati sma kṣapākṣaye vṛttakartavyā // DKuṭṭ_332 //
children.translated_text: despaired — at the end of the night, her livelihood was exhausted. // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 332 //
One slave-girl, by a stroke of fate catching sight of a broken-down gallant who had fallen into her view,

children.text: jvalitā ruṣā bhujiṣyā jagrāha javena dhāvitvā // DKuṭṭ_333 //
children.translated_text: blazed with anger and seized him, running swiftly after him. // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 333 //
Another <s>kuṭṭanī</s> (procuress) said to a man stripped of his wealth who stood at the door of a patron's house inside:
"Go away, you whose body matches your fortunes — depart!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 334 //
Another courtesan, displaying the scratches and bite-marks, proclaiming the love-battle with a prince,

children.text: aparā puraḥ sakhīnāṃ vāravadhūrātatāna saubhāgyam // DKuṭṭ_335 //
children.translated_text: before her friends, flaunted her good fortune at length. // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 335 //
Another, a <s>kheḍā</s> (lower-rank courtesan) whose price had been raised by the rivalry of lovers,
bore herself with the arrogance of beauty and pride among the courtesans. // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 336 //
A certain <s>kuṭṭanī</s>, running in haste, intervened to stop

children.text: sambhramato dhāvitvā nivārayāmāsa kuṭṭanī kalaham // DKuṭṭ_337 //
children.translated_text: the quarrel between two lovers who had drawn weapons in anger over a single courtesan. // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 337 //

children.text: dhanamāhṛtya bahubhyo bhujyata ekena kena citsārdham /
children.translated_text: "Having collected wealth from many, she is enjoyed together with some one man" —

children.text: iti dhanavantaṃ kāminamāvarjayati sma kāpi vāravadhūḥ // DKuṭṭ_338 //
children.translated_text: thus a certain courtesan was winning over a wealthy patron. // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 338 //
Then a certain gallant, singing a mere two-line song with elegance,
wandered before a slave-girl, performing various amusing antics. // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 339 //
A certain penniless lover, through the contrivance of employing another man,
was performing worship at the shrines of courtesans enriched by wealth. // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 340 //

children.text: tvayi saktena mayā gṛhamujjhitamadhunā pareva jātāsi /
children.translated_text: "Attached to you, I abandoned my home; now you have become like a stranger!"
Thus a certain man, failing to obtain his gift, reproached a courtesan. // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 341 //
Another, having spent the night with a different man, having defeated old gallants before their eyes —

children.text: tyājayati sma bhujaṅgaḥ kaścidgaṇikāṃ dviguṇabhāṭīm // DKuṭṭ_342 //
children.translated_text: a certain lover was making a courtesan give up a double fee. // 342 //
'Have you seen, <s>Viśeṣaka</s>, the cluster of bracelets on <s>Śaśiprabhā</s>'s arms?

children.text: bāḍhaṃ bhaṇa bhaṇa kīdṛk cārutarā sā mayā dattā // DKuṭṭ_343 //
children.translated_text: Indeed, tell me, tell me — how beautiful was that which I gave her?' // 343 //
'Today is the fourth day since the pair of Chinese silk garments was given,

children.text: tadapi paruṣā vilāsā vada Madanaka kiṃ karomyatra // DKuṭṭ_344 //
children.translated_text: and yet <s>Vilāsā</s> remains harsh — tell me, <s>Madanaka</s>, what should I do about this?' // 344 //

children.text: snehaparā mayi Kelī Kalahaṃsaka kiṃ tu rākṣasī tasyāḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Kelī</s> is affectionate toward me, <s>Kalahaṃsaka</s>, but her mother is a demoness —

children.text: mātā nātmīkartuṃ varṣaśatenāpi śakyate pāpā // DKuṭṭ_345 //
children.translated_text: the wicked one cannot be won over even in a hundred years!' // 345 //
'Prepare the fragrant offering of flowers and saffron — why do you stand there bewildered?

children.text: adya tava dayitikāyāḥ Kiñjalkaka nartanāvasaraḥ // DKuṭṭ_346 //
children.translated_text: Today is the occasion for your beloved's dance performance, <s>Kiñjalkaka</s>!' // 346 //

children.text: yadi nāma pañca divasāntvayi kurute prema dhanalavaṃ dṛṣṭvā /
children.translated_text: 'Even if for five days she shows you affection upon seeing a morsel of money,

children.text: tadapi Taraṅgavatī sā Kandarpaka kiṃ vṛthā garvaḥ // DKuṭṭ_347 //
children.translated_text: still, that <s>Taraṅgavatī</s> — O <s>Kandarpaka</s>, why this vain pride?' // 347 //

children.text: jīvadveṣin Lāsaka parihara dūreṇa mūḍha Harisenām /
children.translated_text: 'You who hate your own life, <s>Lāsaka</s>, stay far away from <s>Harisenā</s>, you fool!
Her son, bound in passion for her, is dangerously engaged [in her business].' // 348 //
'See the majesty of moonrise! — <s>Kesarayā</s>, having momentarily placed a cloth
over a cluster of suitors, now struts about with neck stiff.' // 349 //

children.text: kaumārakaṃ vidhātuṃ vāñchasi kila ramaṇa Madanasenāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Do you wish to take the virginity of <s>Madanasenā</s>, my dear man?

children.text: icchāmi kiṃ tu tasyā mātrātīva prasāritaṃ vadanam // DKuṭṭ_350 //
children.translated_text: I too would like that, but her mother's face is stretched out [with greed] excessively.' // 350 //
'O <s>Vibhrama</s>, what great <s>tapas</s> has borne this fruit — that wine is being enjoyed,
given by <s>Devadattā</s>, intoxicated and reeling, the remainder from what she drank with her own hand!' // 351 //
'Why has the dwelling of <s>Kuvalayamālā</s> been suddenly abandoned, <s>Līlodaya</s>?

children.text: kiṃ vidadhāmastasmin bhrātardāsyā vinā mūlyam // DKuṭṭ_352 //
children.translated_text: What can we do about it, brother — without paying the price for a slave-girl?' // 352 //
'The night passes for <s>Indīvaraka</s>, robbed of all his wealth,
as he now massages the feet of <s>Tilakamañjarī</s>, O <s>Mañjīraka</s>.' // 353 //

children.text: adyāpi bālabhāvaṃ nikhilaṃ na jahāti Madanikā tadapi /
children.translated_text: 'Even now <s>Madanikā</s> has not entirely given up her girlish ways, and yet,

children.text: prauḍhimnā Makarandaka sakalā lalanā adhaḥ kurute // DKuṭṭ_354 //
children.translated_text: in maturity, O <s>Makarandaka</s>, she puts all women to shame.' // 354 //
'Go, <s>Kubjā</s>, and tell that merciless dance-teacher:

children.text: Hārā sukumāratanuḥ kimiti śramamadya kāritā bhavatā // DKuṭṭ_355 //
children.translated_text: "<s>Hārā</s> is of delicate body — why has she been made to exert herself today by you?"' // 355 //
'Come out! What is this preoccupation with teaching a parrot-chick, <s>Suratādevī</s>?
Your lover is sitting outside, waiting for you.' // 356 //
'She has fallen onto the couch in the bedchamber, exhausted from playing the <s>vīṇā</s>;

children.text: utthāpaya tāṃ tvaritaṃ smaralīlāṃ Bhaṭṭaputra āyātaḥ // DKuṭṭ_357 //
children.translated_text: wake her up quickly, <s>Smaralīlā</s> — the <s>Bhaṭṭa</s>'s son has arrived!' // 357 //

children.text: kimidaṃ yathāsthitatvaṃ tava Mādhavi yanmuhurvadantyā me /
children.translated_text: 'What is this indifference of yours, <s>Mādhavī</s>? Though I tell you again and again,
you do not put on the ornament given by the son of <s>Śrīvigraharāja</s>.' // 358 //
'What shall we do, mother, about this absent-mindedness of <s>Indulekhā</s>?

children.text: pānakrīḍāsaktyā patitāpi na cetitā kanakatāḍī // DKuṭṭ_359 //
children.translated_text: From her addiction to drinking and merrymaking, a gold coin fell and she did not even notice!' // 359 //

children.text: nakulaḥ payo na pāyita iti roṣavaśādiyaṃ hi duḥśīlā /
children.translated_text: '"The mongoose was not given its milk" — and so out of spite, this ill-tempered one,

children.text: nāśnāti Kāmasenā punaḥ punaḥ prārthyamānāpi // DKuṭṭ_360 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kāmasenā</s>, refuses to eat, even though entreated again and again.' // 360 //
'O <s>Mukulā</s>, [you are] protected by the son of <s>Śrībala</s>, a spinner of wool — what is to be won from her?
Having abandoned a comfortable existence, she is engaged day and night in tending sheep!' // 361 //
'Your palms have become reddened and swollen, <s>Sulalitā</s>;
do not continue playing ball so excessively!' // 362 //

children.text: abhirāma ḍomba bhāṭī prathamamiyaṃ gṛhyate samutpanne /
children.translated_text: 'Welcome, O <s>Ḍomba</s>! This fee is to be taken first, upon the arising [of the relationship];

children.text: snehe tu Kusumadevyāstvaṃ prabhavasi jīvitasyāpi // DKuṭṭ_363 //
children.translated_text: but once <s>Kusumadevī</s>'s affection grows, you will have power even over her very life.' // 363 //
'Give the betrothal gift first, if you are curious about <s>Candrasenā</s>;
once the task is accomplished, you shall give something as she desires.' // 364 //
'That son of <s>Nagararoṭabhaṭṭa</s> is not a generous giver, mother;
he is shameless, of deceitful conduct, even though admonished again and again. // 365 //

children.text: kṣapayati vasanāni sadā haṭhena sakalāni Suratasenāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He constantly wears out all of <s>Suratasenā</s>'s garments by force,
but does not give even a single thread of wool — the wretch claims it is cotton.' // 366 //

children.text: bhagini na muñcati veśma kṣaṇamapi me kapaṭarājaputro 'sau /
children.translated_text: 'Sister, that fake prince does not leave my house even for a moment;
defeated, with no other woman available — like a holy ford occupied by a naked [ascetic].' // 367 //
Hearing such conversations uttered by rogues and procuresses,

children.text: taṃ veśasaṃniveśaṃ paśyan praviveśa dayitikāveśma // DKuṭṭ_368 //
children.translated_text: and seeing that spectacle of the courtesan quarter, he entered the dwelling of his beloved. // 368 //
As if drawn by longing, as if bathed by the flowing streams of her affectionate eyes,
<s>Hāralatā</s> honored him as he arrived near. // 369 //
Having properly taken his seat, bowing his head, and saluting her friend,
<s>Sundarasena</s> spoke these words most humbly, at the auspicious moment: // 370 //
'O handsome one, what need of many pitiful speeches composed in the anguish of love's torment?
Here sits <s>Hāralatā</s> — her very life depends on you.' // 371 //
'Let the youth of you both pass in lovemaking free of all restraint, beautiful with the bond of natural affection,

children.text: kāryāntarāntarāyaiḥ suparihṛtaṃ yātu yauvanaṃ bhavatoḥ // DKuṭṭ_372 //
children.translated_text: well-protected from the interruptions of other affairs.' // 372 //
'May your lovemaking always be merciless, of unceasing desire, with shame destroyed, of unsteady conduct,
with ever-increasing passion.' // 373 //
Having thus given their blessing, when the attendants withdrew inside,
the Flower-armed one (<s>Kāma</s>) grew greatly, his essence being the intimate relish of secrecy. // 374 //
What was appropriate for intense love, what was befitting new passion,
what was delightful in youth, and what was the fruit of the purpose of living — // 375 //
boldness itself was adornment, indecent behavior itself was honor,
fearlessness itself was elegance, and instability itself was the basis of dignity — // 376 //
seizing the hair was a favor, striking was a kindness, a bite was for delight,
scratching with nails was a blessing, tight embracing of the body was exaltation — // 377 //
a kiss was eager to swallow, a caress was desirous of crushing the limbs,
a tight embrace wished to enter entirely within — in that [lovemaking]. // 378 //
It was as if performed by passions incarnate, as if radiance was brought by colors of love,
as if set in motion by affection itself, as if brought to full bloom by the essence of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment). // 379 //
Modesty was a vice, steadiness was wrong, discrimination was injury,

children.text: hrepaṇamaguṇo yasmin tatsurataṃ prastutaṃ tābhyām // DKuṭṭ_380 //
children.translated_text: and shame was a flaw in that lovemaking enacted by those two. // 380 //

children.text: prārambha eva tāvatprajvalito dhagiti Manasijo yasmin /
children.translated_text: At the very outset, the Mind-born (<s>Kāma</s>) was ignited in a flash;
the special states of that one, once fully aroused, cannot be described. // 381 //
Numbed by natural passion — for those two youths, versed in the <s>Kāmaśāstra</s>,
among the various techniques, their learning fell into disarray. // 382 //
Nothing was unruly, nothing unspeakable, nothing to be examined, nothing to be concealed, nothing unbearable
for those two in that unbroken, fully commenced battle of love. // 383 //
The studied repertoire of varied amorous caresses that the slender woman had practiced in lovemaking —
her natural seizure by love's possession rendered it all cut up and scattered. // 384 //
Who is able to enumerate the acts of those two lovers, caught in the wheel of <s>Rati</s> (love),

children.text: kaḥ parigaṇanaṃ kartuṃ raticakrāviṣṭaramaṇayoḥ śaktaḥ // DKuṭṭ_385 //
children.translated_text: whose natural passion illumined the gestures taught by the master of love's art? // 385 //
The young woman, a tender creeper of limbs, her body overwhelmed by the firm man, not only

children.text: na vyathitā mudamāpa prabhavati khalu cittajanmanaḥ śaktiḥ // DKuṭṭ_386 //
children.translated_text: was not pained but experienced delight — truly, the power of the mind-born (<s>Kāma</s>) prevails! // 386 //

children.text: kiṃ ramaṇīṃ ramaṇo 'viśaduta ramaṇī ramaṇamiti na jānīmaḥ /
children.translated_text: Whether the lover entered the beloved or the beloved entered the lover — we do not know;
the awareness of their own limbs — it vanished skillfully for those two at that moment. // 387 //
With eyes closed, body motionless — at the end of lovemaking, for her,
the sign of inferring the existence of life was but the shadow of <s>Anaṅga</s> (Love). // 388 //
Covered with droplets of exertion's moisture, bashful from the recollection of what had passed,

children.text: sā śuśubhe rativiratau paryākulakeśabhūṣaṇā nitarām // DKuṭṭ_389 //
children.translated_text: she shone exceedingly in the aftermath of love, with her hair and ornaments in disarray. // 389 //
For those two who had surrendered their bodies without pretense, who counted the entire world as nothing but bliss,
the night ended — though their desire remained undiminished. // 390 //
Wearied by the exhausting combat of love, yawning, walking unsteadily and slowly,
her eyes heavy with sleep, <s>Hāralatā</s> emerged from the bedchamber. // 391 //
'I, staying close to his side, having eaten and drunk together with him,

children.text: nītā niśā kathābhirmohanakāryaṃ tu yatkiṃ cit // DKuṭṭ_392 //
children.translated_text: passed the night in conversation — though there was some task of enchantment [left undone].' // 392 //
'An unsophisticated man, hardened by labor, a rare-to-find young <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, dull —
he departed in the guise of a lover, [bringing] untimely death to me [by boredom] at night.' // 393 //
'Desire never ceased, not even for a moment, yet neither was there capacity — with efforts at love devoid of substance,
I was merely tormented today by an old man!' // 394 //
'Since the assailant, overcome by drink, was practically dead [from intoxication], and I lay buried in my portion of the bed

children.text: anirodhitanidrāyāḥ sukhena me yāminī yātā // DKuṭṭ_395 //
children.translated_text: with my sleep unobstructed, the night passed pleasantly for me.' // 395 //
'Of delicate lovemaking, of charming speech, with witty jesting —

children.text: śakunavaśenopanato mama sakhi ramaṇo manoharākāraḥ // DKuṭṭ_396 //
children.translated_text: a lover of captivating appearance has come to me by the fortune of birds [auspicious omen], my friend!' // 396 //
'Concealed at the edge of the bed, facing away, releasing slow, soft sighs,
even more motionless at my urging, drenched in perspiration — // 397 //
'his love having been poured out and gone, his sleep departed, longing for the end of night,

children.text: grāmoṣitaḥ prahīṇo niṣpratipattiḥ sthito 'dya sakhi manujaḥ // DKuṭṭ_398 //
children.translated_text: a village-dweller, cast off — the man stands today without any plan, O friend.' // 398 //

children.text: śṛṇu sakhi kautukamekaṃ grāmīṇakakāminā yadadya kṛtam /
children.translated_text: 'Listen, friend, to one amusing thing done today by a rustic lover:
seeing my eyes closed in the bliss of love, the frightened man released me, thinking I was dead!' // 399 //
'From a deceitful one, ignorant of local customs, an ill-bred pretender —
we have suffered the misery of farcical ridicule from a prince!' // 400 //
'Dear friend, I was taken by force by the city governor in public view;
when one who enslaves demands double the price, how can there be injustice?' // 401 //

children.text: ākarṣantī jaghanaṃ vrajasi yathā vikṣatā nakhaistilaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Dragging your hips as you walk, scratched to bits by nails —

children.text: manye tathopabhuktā tvaṃ Kerali dākṣiṇātyena // DKuṭṭ_402 //
children.translated_text: I think, <s>Keralī</s>, you have been enjoyed by a man from the South.' // 402 //

children.text: adhare binduḥ kaṇṭhe maṇimālā kucayuge śaśaplutakam /
children.translated_text: 'A dot on the lip, a pearl necklace on the throat, a rabbit-mark on the pair of breasts —

children.text: tava sūcayanti Ketaki Kusumāyudhaśāstrapaṇḍitaṃ ramaṇam // DKuṭṭ_403 //
children.translated_text: these indicate, <s>Ketakī</s>, that your lover is learned in the <s>Kāmaśāstra</s>.' // 403 //
Hearing such morning talk of the courtesans whose night's engagements had ended,

children.text: so 'pi yathākriyamāṇaṃ pravidhātuṃ nirjagāma kartavyam // DKuṭṭ_404 //
children.translated_text: he too went out to attend to his duties as they were to be performed. // 404 //
With love's accumulation well-established, her mind won over, together with her,
enjoying the pleasures of youth, a year and a half passed for him. // 405 //
While having intimate conversations, strolling on the terrace of the garden,
<s>Sundarasena</s>, with his hand clasped by his companion's hand, once // 406 //
saw coming from a distance a letter-carrier walking swiftly,
wearing a covering of various garments stitched from thick, coarse threads,
his body soiled, with worn shoes on feet that had broken straps, the ointment cracked and flaking,
As [the messenger] gradually drew near, <s>Paurandari</s> (<s>Sundarasena</s>), recognizing him,

children.text: sākūtamanā ūce vayasya hanumānayaṃ prāptaḥ // DKuṭṭ_409 //
children.translated_text: spoke with a meaningful mind: 'Friend, <s>Hanumān</s> has arrived!' // 409 //
With his head bowed to the ground, having made obeisance, [the messenger] placed upon the earth

children.text: utkṣipya jhaṭiti lekhaṃ Sundara iti vācayāmāsa // DKuṭṭ_410 //
children.translated_text: snatching up the letter, [the friend] read aloud: '<s>Sundara</s>!' // DKuṭṭ_410 //
'Greetings! From the illustrious city of <s>Kusumapura</s>, <s>Purandara</s> addresses <s>Sundara</s>,
seized by grief bursting forth within, with indistinct syllables and words.' // DKuṭṭ_411 //
'The unblemished [honor of the] family has not been regarded; what is proper for those of high birth has been scorned;
censure has not been heeded — as you have fallen onto the path trodden by rogues.' // DKuṭṭ_412 //
'In a lineage of those whose conduct is straight, free from the fault of double-dealing,
devoted to the destruction of others' enemies — how have you been born a serpent?' // DKuṭṭ_413 //
'Where is your face, which should hold the recitation of <s>Vedic</s> verses purified by the sacrificial cake?
And where is this savoring of the mouth of a harlot, fragrant with wine and liquor?' // DKuṭṭ_414 //
'Where is the astonishment at the sudden pain born from the splitting of <s>kuśa</s> (sacred grass)?
And where is the delight in cruel scratch-wounds from the battle of love with slave-girls?' // DKuṭṭ_415 //
'Where is the face washed by tears from eyes irritated by the smoke of the three sacred fires?
And where is the flood of tears that comes from the weight of grief at a courtesan's scolding?' // DKuṭṭ_416 //
'Where is the sound of <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> (sacrificial exclamation), the ear-ornament that adorns one who performs the six duties?
And where is the eagerness to hear the moaning of a public woman in lovemaking?' // DKuṭṭ_417 //
'Where is the trembling born from the agitation of being struck with a slender creeper by the teacher?
And where is the endurance of a cruel kick from the foot of an angered courtesan?' // DKuṭṭ_418 //
'Where is the covering of deer-skin, the vow prescribed by the <s>Smṛti</s> texts for one observing austerities?
And where is the reverence for wearing garments that have touched the body of a woman for sale?' // DKuṭṭ_419 //
'The cutting of sacrificial fuel-sticks alone was practiced from boyhood;

children.text: śaṭhavanitādharakhaṇḍana utpannaṃ kauśalaṃ kuto bhavataḥ // DKuṭṭ_420 //
children.translated_text: whence has your skill arisen in biting the lip of a deceitful woman?' // DKuṭṭ_420 //
'Only the service of the <s>guru</s> (teacher) was always practiced with a steadfast mind;

children.text: kuṭilamatayo bhujiṣyāḥ kathaṃ tvayārādhitā nipuṇam // DKuṭṭ_421 //
children.translated_text: how have crooked-minded slave-girls been skillfully served by you?' // DKuṭṭ_421 //
'Your fame for clear and well-articulated pronunciation belongs to <s>Vedic</s> recitation alone;
where was this verbal cleverness in appeasing an angry courtesan learned?' // DKuṭṭ_422 //
'Or rather, what can be done? Even those born in a spotless family
become celebrated among the wicked, due to the faults of previously accumulated <s>karma</s>.' // DKuṭṭ_423 //
'Having entrusted the household affairs to you, with my mind solely devoted to acquiring merit for the next world,
I intended to remain [in retirement] — but day after day, that hope has been betrayed.' // DKuṭṭ_424 //
When <s>Sundarasena</s> had grasped the contents of the letter, bewildered and compliant,
another [person] sang, at his own opportunity, a verse set to melody: // DKuṭṭ_425 //
'For men whose eyes are covered by the darkness of sensual pleasures, who fall into the pit without seeing the path,
the words of elders are the collyrium-stick that clears their vision.' // DKuṭṭ_426 //
'The application of bitter medicine and the harsh words of a <s>guru</s>'s prescribed duty
cause distress at the moment but produce the prosperity of happiness in the outcome.' // DKuṭṭ_427 //
Then, finding an opportunity to speak, the friend addressed the son of <s>Purandara</s>;

children.text: punarapi na hi khidyante priyajanahitabhāṣaṇe santaḥ // DKuṭṭ_428 //
children.translated_text: for good people never tire of speaking for the benefit of those dear to them. // DKuṭṭ_428 //
'You have disregarded the words of your companions; your body is submerged in the great ocean of wicked addiction;
if the words of your father, anguished with grief, are the last support [you have left] —' // DKuṭṭ_429 //
'Your father, who was the lamp of his lineage, adorned by his conduct, a man of great fortitude —

children.text: Sundara samprati tātaḥ spṛṣṭo duṣputradoṣeṇa // DKuṭṭ_430 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Sundara</s>, he has now been touched by the fault of having a bad son.' // DKuṭṭ_430 //
'The absence of a son is preferable; the state of having a bad son, for a man of noble family who has sons,
burns him deeply within on occasions when the topic of good conduct arises.' // DKuṭṭ_431 //

children.text: sāṃvyavahārika eva prāyo loke guṇonnatā niyatāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Generally in the world, those elevated by virtues are fixed in worldly affairs [alone];

children.text: yena tu sutena jananī vandhyātvaṃ ślāghate sa pāpīyān // DKuṭṭ_432 //
children.translated_text: but he is the worst son on account of whom a mother praises barrenness.' // DKuṭṭ_432 //
'Knowledge of the scriptures is fruitless, and service at the teacher's house is of no benefit
for one who has abandoned the righteous path, his mind enslaved by sensual objects.' // DKuṭṭ_433 //

children.text: jīvanneva mṛto 'sau yasya jano vīkṣya vadanamanyonyam /
children.translated_text: 'He is dead even while alive, at whose face people look at one another,
make grimaces, and from a distance point their fingers.' // DKuṭṭ_434 //

children.text: no parihartuṃ viṣayāḥ śakyāḥ satyaṃ tathāpi nipuṇadhiyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Sensual objects cannot be given up — that is true; nevertheless, those of keen intellect
do not become the subject of talk distinguished by the particular appellation of scandal.' // DKuṭṭ_435 //
'Service of the teacher, a wife born of good family, the company of affectionate kinsmen,
devotion to Brahmanical duties — these are the means of achieving both worlds for the wise.' // DKuṭṭ_436 //

children.text: sulabhā tasya vibhūtistasya guṇā yānti jagati vistāram /
children.translated_text: 'Prosperity comes easily to him; his virtues spread throughout the world;

children.text: bahu manute taṃ sujanastasmai spṛhayanti bāndhavāḥ satatam // DKuṭṭ_437 //
children.translated_text: good people esteem him highly; his kinsmen always envy him.' // DKuṭṭ_437 //
'He alone does not stumble from the path trodden by the virtuous;

children.text: maṇḍayati so 'nvavāyaṃ sa nivāsaḥ śarmaṇāmaśeṣāṇām // DKuṭṭ_438 //
children.translated_text: he adorns his lineage; he is the abode of all joys.' // DKuṭṭ_438 //

children.text: sa bhavati vinayādhāro yuktāyukte vivekitā tasya /
children.translated_text: 'He becomes the repository of good conduct; he has discernment between what is proper and improper;
the instructive words of the elderly are always a feast for his ears and stomach [i.e. heart].' // DKuṭṭ_439 //
'When embodied beings are attached to base women, it is the ripening of past <s>karma</s>;

children.text: āyatanaṃ tu sukhānāṃ saṃsārabhuvāṃ kulodgatā rāmā // DKuṭṭ_440 //
children.translated_text: but a wife born of good family is the abode of happiness in the stages of worldly life.' // DKuṭṭ_440 //
'Saddened when [her husband] is saddened, joyful when he is joyful, agitated when he is agitated,

children.text: pratibimbasamā kāntā saṃkruddhe kevalaṃ bhītā // DKuṭṭ_441 //
children.translated_text: a wife is like a reflection — only when he is angry, she is merely afraid.' // DKuṭṭ_441 //
'A wife whose conversation is compatible, who is an enduring companion in the desired sports of love,
and who is skilled in following the mind — such a wife is born only to the meritorious.' // DKuṭṭ_442 //
'Offering the genuine flavor of true love, softly, afraid of the sound of her bangles,
surrendering her body — her intentions revealed like the blossoming of the Flower-god's designs.' // DKuṭṭ_443 //

children.text: hā hā kimuddhatatvaṃ śroṣyati kaścidgatatrapa svairam /
children.translated_text: 'Ah, ah! Such impudence! Someone will hear, you shameless one! Freely!

children.text: nikaṭe parivārajano vismṛta eva smarāturasya tava // DKuṭṭ_444 //
children.translated_text: The attendants nearby — have you completely forgotten them, you who are agitated with desire?' // DKuṭṭ_444 //
Thus, with words whose meanings convey exertion, mixed with soft exclamations of rebuke,
a well-born woman doubles the hero's deeds when the flow of passion spreads. // DKuṭṭ_445 //
To his friend who had spoken thus, the son of <s>Purandara</s> replied,
trembling with the fear of imminent separation from his beloved: // DKuṭṭ_446 //
'Father's command is not to be transgressed; the fire of separation from <s>Hāralatā</s> is intense;

children.text: vidhivaśavartini maraṇe no vidmaḥ kāryapariṇāmam // DKuṭṭ_447 //
children.translated_text: death is subject to the will of Fate — we know not how things will turn out.' // DKuṭṭ_447 //
'Dragged away by destiny, one abandons a beloved who was indifferent to gaining wealth, whose mind was bound by love alone —

children.text: daivākṛṣṭo muñcati ghaṭito vā lohavajrakaṇikābhiḥ // DKuṭṭ_448 //
children.translated_text: as even [an object] bound with iron and adamantine particles [is pulled away].' // DKuṭṭ_448 //
Then, having resolved to depart, he made his beloved aware of the matter;
and she, distressed with grief, followed him as he set out on the journey. // DKuṭṭ_449 //
Reaching the foot of a banyan tree, her eyelash-tips dotted with drops of tears,
her steps faltering, he addressed <s>Hāralatā</s>: // DKuṭṭ_450 //

children.text: ā kṣīravato vṛkṣādā salilādvā priye priyaṃ yāntam /
children.translated_text: 'A [wife] should follow her departing beloved up to the milk-bearing tree or up to the water' —

children.text: anuyāyāditi vacanaṃ tena tvamito nivartasva // DKuṭṭ_451 //
children.translated_text: this is the saying; therefore, turn back from here.' // DKuṭṭ_451 //

children.text: kiṃ kurmo daivahatāḥ prabhavati yasmin kṛśodari prasabham /
children.translated_text: 'What shall we do, struck by fate? For in this matter, O slender-waisted one,
the arrow of the <s>guru</s>'s command, which cuts the knot of love, prevails irresistibly, without obstruction.' // DKuṭṭ_452 //
'Neither the acquisition of accumulated wealth, nor the intimacy of familiar company, nor the quality of flattery,

children.text: na svāmisamādeśo nākāravilobhanaṃ na ca khyātiḥ // DKuṭṭ_453 //
children.translated_text: nor a master's command, nor the enticement of gestures, nor fame —' // DKuṭṭ_453 //
'was the cause of your attachment to us; yet by the force of fate,
there is this connection, however improbable, whose consequence is beyond remedy.' // DKuṭṭ_454 //

children.text: paruṣaṃ yadabhihitāsi praṇayaruṣā śaṅkitaṃ ca narmaṇi vā /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever harsh thing was said to you in a lover's quarrel, or doubtfully in jest —
O beautiful-teethed one, that is not to be remembered, at this moment when harsh words are recalled.' // DKuṭṭ_455 //

children.text: tava hṛdaye hṛdayamidaṃ vinyastaṃ nyāsapālanaṃ kaṣṭam /
children.translated_text: 'This heart has been deposited in your heart; guarding a trust is difficult;

children.text: yatnāttathā vidheyaṃ sthānabhraṃśo yathā na syāt // DKuṭṭ_456 //
children.translated_text: strive carefully so that it does not fall from its place.' // DKuṭṭ_456 //
Then, when the beloved had finished speaking, <s>Hāralatā</s>, the composition of her words afflicted by the weight of tears,
spoke with difficulty, her voice nearly drowned by the substance of her emotion: // DKuṭṭ_457 //
'Born of an impure family, living by selling my body, cunning in conduct —

children.text: kvāhaṃ rūpājīvā kva bhavantaḥ ślāghanīyajanmaguṇāḥ // DKuṭṭ_458 //
children.translated_text: who am I, a woman living by her beauty? And who are you, possessing praiseworthy qualities of birth?' // DKuṭṭ_458 //
'But that you, having come out of curiosity to see the pleasures [of the city], have rested

children.text: iyato divasānasmin tanme parajanmakṛtaśubhasya phalam // DKuṭṭ_459 //
children.translated_text: for these many days here — that is the fruit of my merit from a previous birth.' // DKuṭṭ_459 //
'Service of the <s>guru</s>, one's kinsmen, residence in one's homeland, a compatible wife —

children.text: anuṣaṅgadṛṣṭaparicita āsthāṃ pravidhāya kaḥ parityajati // DKuṭṭ_460 //
children.translated_text: who, having established attachments through continued familiarity, would abandon them?' // DKuṭṭ_460 //
'This is the fickleness of youth, that you have found amusement in one such as me;

children.text: yattu sukhamanavagītaṃ tasya sthānaṃ nijā dārāḥ // DKuṭṭ_461 //
children.translated_text: but as for the happiness that is free from censure — its place is with one's own wife.' // DKuṭṭ_461 //

children.text: te madhurāḥ parihāsāstā vakragiraḥ sa vāmatāsamayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Those sweet jests, those indirect words, those moments of feigned displeasure —

children.text: no hṛdaye kartavyā rahasi kṣemārthinā bhavatā // DKuṭṭ_462 //
children.translated_text: should not be kept in your heart by you, who seek your own welfare, in private.' // DKuṭṭ_462 //
'Whatever I have done that was contrary [to propriety], whether from levity of mind or from affection,

children.text: pratikūlaṃ tatra mayā nāthāñjalireṣa viracito mūrdhni // DKuṭṭ_463 //
children.translated_text: for that, my lord, this <s>añjali</s> (salute of joined palms) is offered on my head.' // DKuṭṭ_463 //
'The paths are difficult to travel, the dwelling is far away, the heart is unsteady;
O <s>Guṇapālita</s>, you, the friend, must be vigilant.' // DKuṭṭ_464 //
'When the two hearts have become one, the suffering born of separation
for the lovers who experience it — another may well prescribe the remedy from the sidelines.' // DKuṭṭ_465 //
'For those bound by the bonds of genuine affection and firmly established mutual devotion —
the separator is death, or the resolution of the steadfast.' // DKuṭṭ_466 //
Then, after hearing this, saying 'Stay well, dear one — I go,'

children.text: abhidhāya yāti mandaṃ Sundarasene vivartitagrīvam // DKuṭṭ_467 //
children.translated_text: <s>Sundarasena</s> departs slowly, his neck turned back [to look at her]. // DKuṭṭ_467 //
Her arm clinging to the branch of the banyan tree, her face and lips drying from the hot breath of sighs,
overturned [with grief], bearing an unblinking gaze directed at the path he took, // DKuṭṭ_468 //
her braid swaying, her neck-ornaments gone askew,
filled with flowing tears, her limbs too weak for the portion of garment that had slipped — // DKuṭṭ_469 //
as if she were clutching her heart with her other hand resting upon her pair of breasts,
forsaken of all coquetry, abandoned by the obligations of the world of the living, // DKuṭṭ_470 //
embraced by calamity, subdued by the cruel blows to her vital points —
<s>Hāralatā</s>, her voice barely articulate, being drawn inward, // DKuṭṭ_471 //

children.text: mā mā tāvadyāta kṣaṇamekaṃ yāvadeṣa niṣkaruṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: saying 'Don't, don't go yet — until this merciless one

children.text: vanagulmairna tirohita ityabhidadhatīṃ jahuḥ prāṇāḥ // DKuṭṭ_472 //
children.translated_text: is not hidden by the thickets of the forest' — [with these words] her life departed. // DKuṭṭ_472 //
Then, meeting a traveler who had come from behind, the son of <s>Purandara</s> asked:
'Did you see a grief-stricken woman turning back?' // DKuṭṭ_473 //

children.text: sa uvāca vaṭataroradha urvyāṃ patitā viniścalāvayavā /
children.translated_text: He replied: 'Beneath the banyan tree, fallen upon the ground, her limbs motionless,

children.text: tiṣṭhati vanitā nānyā nayanāvasaraṃ gatāsmākam // DKuṭṭ_474 //
children.translated_text: a woman lies — no other [sight] has come within the range of our eyes.' // DKuṭṭ_474 //
Struck by that word as by a stone, his form trembling, he fell upon the ground;

children.text: utthāpitaśca suhṛdā so 'bhidadhe tena śokadīnena // DKuṭṭ_475 //
children.translated_text: raised up by his friend, he — broken by grief — spoke thus: // DKuṭṭ_475 //
'Let father be fulfilled; may you too, O good friend, be happy now;

children.text: samakālameva muktā pāpena mayāsubhiśca Hāralatā // DKuṭṭ_476 //
children.translated_text: simultaneously, <s>Hāralatā</s> has been released by sin, and I by life.' // DKuṭṭ_476 //

children.text: hā hā hāva hato 'si dhvastā līlā vilāsa kiṃ kuruṣe /
children.translated_text: 'Alas, alas! O grace, you are slain! O playfulness, destroyed! O coquetry, what are you doing?

children.text: uccchinnā vicchittirbhrama vibhrama daśa diśo nirādhāraḥ // DKuṭṭ_477 //
children.translated_text: O elegance, you are cut off! O allure, O charm — directionless in the ten quarters, without support!' // DKuṭṭ_477 //
'O <s>kilakiñcita</s> (feigned reluctance), go to the forest! O <s>moṭṭāyita</s> (pouting), you have reached a state of shelterlessness!'

children.text: kuṭṭamita pravrajyāṃ gṛhāṇa bibboka viśa bhuvo vivaram // DKuṭṭ_478 //
children.translated_text: "O rogue, take up the wandering ascetic's life! O dandy, enter a hole in the earth!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 478 //

children.text: lalitamanāthībhūtaṃ vihṛtasya na vidyate gatiḥ kvāpi /
children.translated_text: "There is no recourse anywhere for the graceful one left without a protector;
she whose radiance robbed the orb of the moon has gone to the presence of Death." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 479 //
"Let me turn back and go to burn her who in my absence has released her beloved life;
let at least the gift of the seven-flamed (funeral fire) be some service to the poor girl." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 480 //
Then, going to that very place where she had attained the five-fold state (death),

children.text: vilalāpa muktanādaṃ viluṭhan bhuvi sahacareṇa dhṛtamūrtiḥ // DKuṭṭ_481 //
children.translated_text: he lamented aloud, rolling on the ground, his body supported by his companion. // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 481 //

children.text: ete vayaṃ nivṛttā muñca ruṣaṃ dehi kopane vācam /
children.translated_text: "Here we have returned! Let go of your anger, O wrathful one, speak a word!

children.text: uttiṣṭha kimiti tiṣṭhasi bhūmitale reṇurūṣitaśarīrā // DKuṭṭ_482 //
children.translated_text: Arise! Why do you lie upon the ground, your body soiled with dust?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 482 //
"Why have you closed your eyes and remain motionless, O fair-faced one?
The fault of not preventing my departure does not belong to me." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 483 //
"The ladies of the lord of heaven (<s>Indra</s>) cannot rival you now that you have gone to heaven;

children.text: satsvapi śareṣu pañcasu nirāyudhaḥ sāmprataṃ madanaḥ // DKuṭṭ_484 //
children.translated_text: even with his five arrows intact, <s>Madana</s> (Love) is now disarmed." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 484 //

children.text: vañcakavṛttā veśyā ityapavādo janeṣu yo rūḍhaḥ /
children.translated_text: "The reproach current among people that courtesans are deceitful in their ways —

children.text: apanīto 'sau nipuṇaṃ tvayā priye jīvamokṣeṇa // DKuṭṭ_485 //
children.translated_text: that has been skillfully refuted by you, dear one, by the surrender of your life." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 485 //
"Only one is worthy of praise for his vow of chastity — <s>Mahāsena</s> (<s>Kārttikeya</s>), the son of the Destroyer of <s>Tripura</s> (<s>Śiva</s>),

children.text: hṛdayaṃ yasya spṛṣṭaṃ na manāgapi vāmalocanāpremṇā // DKuṭṭ_486 //
children.translated_text: whose heart was never touched even slightly by the love of a lovely-eyed woman." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 486 //
"I think that, realizing that separation from the beloved is unbearable even for a moment,

children.text: Hariṇā vakṣasi Lakṣmīrvidhṛtā Gaurī Hareṇa dehārdhe // DKuṭṭ_487 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) holds <s>Lakṣmī</s> upon his chest, and <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) holds <s>Gaurī</s> in half of his body." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 487 //

children.text: ayi Lokapāla sā bhuvi lalāmabhūtā tayā vinā śūnyam /
children.translated_text: "O Guardian of the World (<s>Lokapāla</s>), she was the ornament of the earth! Without her, the universe is empty —

children.text: viśvamiti kiṃ na cintitamātmasthānaṃ priyāṃ nayatā // DKuṭṭ_488 //
children.translated_text: was this not considered by you when you took my beloved to your own abode?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 488 //
"O lord <s>Hutavaha</s> (Fire), do not, do not — having extracted the essence of the ocean of beauty,

children.text: kathamapi vihitāṃ dhātrā dhakṣyasyenāṃ jagadbhūṣām // DKuṭṭ_489 //
children.translated_text: will you somehow burn this ornament of the world, fashioned with such difficulty by the Creator?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 489 //

children.text: iti vilapantaṃ bahuvidhamavadhīrya suhṛt purandarasya sutam /
children.translated_text: Thus, disregarding the son of <s>Purandara</s> (<s>Indra</s>) as he lamented in many ways, his friend
constructed a pyre with logs and made the courtesan fuel for the fire. // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 490 //
When his mind, agitated with grief, was resolved upon plunging into the blazing fire,
someone recited by chance an <s>āryā</s> verse that flashed into his consciousness: // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 491 //

children.text: anumaraṇe vyavasāyaṃ strīdharme kaḥ karoti savivekaḥ /
children.translated_text: "What discerning person would resolve to follow a woman in death (<s>anumaraṇa</s>) as woman's duty,
abandoning the vow of taking the staff (<s>daṇḍa</s>) — the means of liberation from <s>saṃsāra</s>?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 492 //
Hearing this, <s>Sundarasena</s>, his distress dispelled, said to his minister:

children.text: pratibodhitaṃ mano me dhīreṇānena yuktamupadiśatā // DKuṭṭ_493 //
children.translated_text: "My mind has been awakened by this wise person who teaches what is proper." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 493 //
"In this revolving <s>saṃsāra</s>, tormented by birth, old age, disease, and death, where the beloved once glimpsed is quickly lost —

children.text: āvartini saṃsāre kaḥ kuryādāgrahaṃ sumatiḥ // DKuṭṭ_494 //
children.translated_text: what sensible person would form attachments?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 494 //
"Let your honour proceed to <s>Kusumapura</s> (Pāṭaliputra); we shall take refuge
in the last <s>āśrama</s> (the order of renunciation), prescribed for the destruction of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance)." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 495 //

children.text: so 'vadadabhijātajano bālyātprabhṛti tvayā ca na viyuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: He replied: "A man of noble birth, never separated from you since childhood —
how can your resolve to renounce now abandon a friend who is indifferent to worldly pleasures?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 496 //
Having spoken thus, <s>Sundarasena</s>, together with <s>Guṇapālita</s>,

children.text: Guṇapālitena sahitaḥ Sundaraseno jagāma vanam // DKuṭṭ_497 //
children.translated_text: went to the forest, frequented by ascetics of firm vows and austere discipline. // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 497 //
"Let courtesans be so — focused solely on self-interest, devoid of genuine feeling;
what loss is that to you in obtaining your desired pleasure?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 498 //
"The discussion of ultimate truth does not touch the sophisticated minds

children.text: na spṛśati tattvacarcā paṇyavadhūnāṃ vidagdhacetāṃsi // DKuṭṭ_499 //
children.translated_text: of courtesans skilled in the sixty-four arts, adept at following the hearts of their lovers." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 499 //
"Through turns, leaps, variegated gaits, postures, speed, urging and compliance,

children.text: rāgasparśena vinā viśati manaḥ sādināṃ turagaḥ // DKuṭṭ_500 //
children.translated_text: a horse enters the minds of riders even without the touch of passion." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 500 //
"Where is even the scent of love in cuckoos, parrots, and house-pigeons?
Yet with their special songs they inflame the unequal-arrowed (<s>Kāma</s>) in young men." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 501 //
"Equipped with the natural, the conventional, and the artificial modes, through the perfect execution of all techniques,
even an actor devoid of real emotion produces delight in the hearts of the audience." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 502 //
"Those fools who see the fault of loss of wealth in the embrace of a courtesan —
they should be asked by you: 'Are wives maintained without the expense of bed and provisions?'" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 503 //

children.text: na ca lābha eka eva pravartane kāraṇaṃ manuṣyeṣu /
children.translated_text: "Nor is profit the only motive driving human actions;
passion and other motives also exist, as stated by the authors of the <s>Vaiśika</s> treatises." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 504 //
"What wealth, indeed, was gained from <s>Sundarasena</s> by that ascetic woman

children.text: tadvirahakuliśabhinnā mumoca yā jīvitaṃ kṣaṇārdhena // DKuṭṭ_505 //
children.translated_text: who, shattered by the thunderbolt of separation from him, gave up her life in half a moment?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 505 //
"The erotic sentiment, whose nature is that of a noble youth, whose attachment to another's body is indicated by horripilation and the like,
whose splendor is clearly manifest — who can restrain it?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 506 //
"Even amid the constraints of elders and household servants, those experienced in the matter
perceive the inner transformation of unchaste women through the sweet glance of furrowed brows and sidelong looks." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 507 //
"Others, abandoning their husband's house, heedless of the stain upon their family and the censure of people,

children.text: rāgoparaktahṛdayā yānti digantaṃ manuṣya āsajya // DKuṭṭ_508 //
children.translated_text: with hearts dyed by passion, attach themselves to a man and go to the ends of the earth." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 508 //
"Insults inflicted by husbands, the severity of the elder's retinue, even destitution at home —
for those women whose chastity is already destroyed, attachment to another man arises from sheer passion." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 509 //
"Even those women of steadfast conduct who are devoted to serving their husbands —
even they, though free from passion, remain so only through propriety alone." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 510 //
"Therefore, let there be sexual union, arising from various causes — who can prevent it?
The governance of the heart in one's own women, other men's women, and courtesans alike is subject to passion." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 511 //
With such examples supported by reasoning, with such words as these,
and also with other flattering phrases, the mind of the client is to be won over. // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 512 //
Having feigned sleep and then awakening, with a slight display of weary languor,
producing a yawn, embracing him tightly as the night departs — // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 513 //
looking at the quarters with eyes whose lids are half-opened, with a long deep sigh,

children.text: vaktavyamiti bhavatyā rajani khale kiṃ prayātāsi // DKuṭṭ_514 //
children.translated_text: you should say: 'O night, O wicked one, why have you departed (so soon)?' // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 514 //
"How could a weak woman endure the flood of the pleasure of love with a man of firm strength,
if the passion born of <s>Madana</s> (Love) did not provide a foundation of strength?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 515 //
"Blessed is the <s>cakravāka</s>-bird's wife, who attains the time of union with her beloved!
O <s>Kumudvatī</s> (night-lotus), separated from the moon, your merit is exhausted!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 516 //
"A juicy flower in full bloom, fragrant and beautiful in form, that has not been obtained

children.text: na karoti tathā pīḍāmāsvāditavicyutaṃ yathā bhṛṅgyāḥ // DKuṭṭ_517 //
children.translated_text: does not cause as much pain to the bee as one that was tasted and then lost." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 517 //
"I therefore petition you, bowing down with hands joined above my head:
by your grace, let me be counted among your attendant servants." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 518 //
Then, through attentions that kindle the hues of passion, that dispel all thought of gain in sequence,
that are gentle and follow the heart — having thus brought the man to trust — // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 519 //

children.text: avalokito 'si lampaṭa kimapi vadan karṇasaṃnidhau nibhṛtam /
children.translated_text: "You were spotted, O rake, whispering something privately near the ear of
<s>Śaṅkarasenā</s>'s nurse, today, by me, through a secret opening. // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 520 //

children.text: mālatyā saha keliṃ vidadhāsi sakhī mameti na virodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: You are sporting with <s>Mālatī</s>; she is my friend, so there is no objection;

children.text: yattu ciraṃ snigdhadṛśā paśyasi tāṃ tatra me śaṅkā // DKuṭṭ_521 //
children.translated_text: but the fact that you gaze at her for a long time with affectionate eyes — in that lies my suspicion." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 521 //

children.text: tvāmāgatā na vīkṣitumanubadhya na yācitaḥ prayatnena /
children.translated_text: "She came but did not look at you; she followed you but did not earnestly petition you;

children.text: āhūya vada kimarthaṃ tāmbūlaṃ grāhitā kamaladevī // DKuṭṭ_522 //
children.translated_text: tell me, having called you, for what purpose did <s>Kamaladevī</s> offer you betel?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 522 //
"When <s>Kundamālā</s> was removing her bodice, revealing the side of her shoulder, armpit, and breast —

children.text: sābhiniveśaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ bhavatā kiṃ kundamālāyāḥ // DKuṭṭ_523 //
children.translated_text: did you look with interest at that, sir?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 523 //
"If you grasped <s>Hīrā</s> in jest by the edge of her garment,

children.text: ācchoṭyāpakrāntā kiṃ māmavalokya pṛṣṭhataḥ sahasā // DKuṭṭ_524 //
children.translated_text: why did she, snapping her fingers, suddenly depart looking back at me?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 524 //

children.text: vijñānena khyātāṃ Kusumalatāṃ tvaṃ tu varṇayasyaniśam /
children.translated_text: "You constantly praise <s>Kusumalatā</s>, famous for her knowledge,
watching <s>Mṛgadevī</s> dance with wide-open eyes." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 525 //
"I do not understand the reason why, abandoning the well-known straight path,
you always go by the crooked way past the house of <s>Mādhavasenā</s>." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 526 //
Thus, through jealous accusations and other light angers that pierce the vital points,
born of love — once the depth of passion is ascertained, O slender-waisted one — // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 527 //
remaining within earshot, hidden from sight, O long-eyed one, together with the mother,

children.text: paruṣagirā tvaṃ kuryā itthaṃ mithyāvacaḥkalaham // DKuṭṭ_528 //
children.translated_text: you should create such a quarrel of false words with harsh speech. // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 528 //
"Wealth came to him without effort; he was humble with love, unrestrainedly generous —

children.text: bhaṭṭānandasya suto nidhibhūto 'bhavyayā tvayā tyaktaḥ // DKuṭṭ_529 //
children.translated_text: the son of <s>Bhaṭṭānanda</s>, a veritable treasure, has been discarded by you, unworthy one!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 529 //
"His judgment impaired by vice, dependent solely on fate, hostile to his own wife —

children.text: māmavigaṇayya mūḍhe nirbhartsita eva keśavasvāmī // DKuṭṭ_530 //
children.translated_text: yet you, fool, have only rebuked <s>Keśavasvāmin</s>, disregarding me!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 530 //
"Heedless of the king's displeasure, with uninterrupted income, generous by nature —
why was the devoted Superintendent of Tolls neglected by you, O perverse-minded one?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 531 //
"The only son of his father, who is in his fourth age of life and afflicted by disease,
a wealthy lord who was obtained — even he was rejected by you who do not desire prosperity!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 532 //

children.text: svakareṇa parityaktā tvayā vibhūtiḥ karomi kiṃ pāpā /
children.translated_text: "You have thrown away prosperity with your own hand — what am I to do, wretched one?
You who look with contempt upon <s>Vasudeva</s> who approached with his entire fortune!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 533 //
"The one whose inclination is excited by rivalry with other men and who

children.text: vasu visṛjati yo rabhasāttasya na vārtā tvayā pṛṣṭā // DKuṭṭ_534 //
children.translated_text: lavishes wealth impetuously and without reserve — you have not even inquired after him!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 534 //
"Skilled in painting and other arts, expert in the science of love, virile by nature —

children.text: upakurvannapi sarvo vidveṣigaṇe tvayā kṣiptaḥ // DKuṭṭ_535 //
children.translated_text: every such man, though he renders service, has been cast by you into the camp of enemies!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 535 //
"An ornament was given by the son of <s>Madhusūdana</s> to <s>Candravatī</s> —

children.text: paśyantī bibhrāṇāmayi rāgiṇi kiṃ na jihreṣi // DKuṭṭ_536 //
children.translated_text: seeing her wear it, O passionate girl, are you not ashamed?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 536 //
"The entire revenue of a village, entering by the command of <s>Siṃharāja</s>
into the house of <s>Manmathasenā</s>, diminishes the glory of your beauty!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 537 //
"Never mind other gains — the service that <s>Ukanandisena</s>'s son

children.text: Śivadevyā upacāraḥ kriyate yastena paryāptam // DKuṭṭ_538 //
children.translated_text: renders to <s>Śivadevī</s> in mere contempt — that alone is enough!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 538 //
"Look at this white mansion, built by <s>Anaṅgadevī</s> with the purity befitting
a <s>Pāśupata</s> preceptor — an ornament to the entire city!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 539 //

children.text: āpaṇikārthasya kuto rājā labhate caturthamapi bhāgam /
children.translated_text: "How could the king obtain even a fourth share of a shopkeeper's wealth?
The market-master <s>Rāmasena</s> — <s>Narmadā</s> enjoys him by his grace!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 540 //

children.text: puṃstvakhyāpanakāmo na strī na pumān kila prabhusvāmī /
children.translated_text: "The master <s>Prabhusvāmin</s> — neither woman nor man, so they say — seeking to prove his manhood
by pursuing you, was laughed at by you, O fool, without considering your own advantage!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 541 //
"Renowned by the king's favour, with his mind set solely on aphrodisiacs —

children.text: pratyākhyātaḥ sa tathā Ravidevaḥ kiṅkaratvamākāṅkṣan // DKuṭṭ_542 //
children.translated_text: that <s>Ravideva</s>, desiring to be your servant, was thus rejected!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 542 //
"Was he born into <s>Kandarpa</s>'s (Love's) own family? Or does he know some proven

children.text: jānāti kamapi siddhaṃ yenākṛṣṭāsi sarvabhāvena // DKuṭṭ_543 //
children.translated_text: spell of enchantment, by which you have been drawn with your whole being?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 543 //
"In childhood she is unfit; later she is degraded by old age;

children.text: tāruṇye rāgahṛtā yadi gaṇikā bhramatu tadbhikṣām // DKuṭṭ_544 //
children.translated_text: if in youth the courtesan's passion has stolen her wits — then let her go begging!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 544 //
"Bring here this merchandise, which was earned by my body;

children.text: vidadhāmi tīrthayātrāmāssva sukhaṃ preyasā sārdham // DKuṭṭ_545 //
children.translated_text: I will go on a pilgrimage — you stay happily with your lover!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 545 //
"Of those wicked women, scorned by respectable people, whose nature manifests only sin —
This alone is the reward — that union with the beloved is unobstructed.

children.text: no dhanalābho lābho lābhaḥ khalu vallabhena saṃsargaḥ /
children.translated_text: Gain of wealth is not true gain; true gain is indeed the company of one's beloved.
The acquisition of wealth before one's eyes does not bring delight to the heart.
Pierced by intense passion and sprinkled with the nectar-essence of youth,

children.text: na bhajati sahṛdayahṛdayaṃ vibhavārjanasambhavā cintā // DKuṭṭ_548 //
children.translated_text: the heart of a sensitive person does not entertain anxiety born of the pursuit of wealth.

children.text: lābhaḥ sa eva paramaḥ paryāptaṃ tena tena tṛptāsmi /
children.translated_text: That alone is the supreme gain — I am satisfied with him, that is enough —

children.text: viniveśya yadutsaṅge nikṣipati mukhe mukhena tāmbūlam // DKuṭṭ_549 //
children.translated_text: when, having seated me on his lap, he places <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel) in my mouth with his own mouth.
He wipes the drops of perspiration from lovemaking off my limbs with his own garment;

children.text: yadurasi nidhāya vihasaṃstasya na mūlyaṃ vasundharā sakalā // DKuṭṭ_550 //
children.translated_text: when he lays me upon his chest and laughs — the entire earth is not a fair price for that.
He whose passion for his own wife has slackened, whose mind is attached to me, who has no other concern,
he who has conquered the beauty of fire itself — by him the ways of the <s>gaṇikā</s> (courtesan's trade) have been put to shame.
A bee, by the ordinance of fate, tastes the nectar of many flowers,

children.text: īdṛkprasavaviśeṣaṃ labhate khalu yena bhavati kṛtakṛtyā // DKuṭṭ_552 //
children.translated_text: yet she finds that one special blossom by which she becomes truly fulfilled.

children.text: ayi sarale tāvadimā upadeśagiro viśanti karṇāntaḥ /
children.translated_text: O innocent girl, these words of instruction enter only as far as the ear,
so long as my heart has not entered into yours.

children.text: śrīrastu durgatirvā veśmani vāso mahatyaraṇye vā /
children.translated_text: Whether there be prosperity or destitution, dwelling in a mansion or in a great forest,

children.text: svarloke narake vā kiṃ bahunā tena me sārdham // DKuṭṭ_554 //
children.translated_text: in heaven or in hell — in short, let it be with him.
'Here lies this jewelry, O wicked mother — take it, what use is it to me?
I am adorned by him alone, that treasury of virtues, <s>Bhaṭṭaputra</s>.'
Having hastily removed the ornaments placed on their proper parts of the body,

children.text: evamabhidhāya yāsyasi mātuḥ purataḥ samutsṛjya // DKuṭṭ_556 //
children.translated_text: speaking thus, you shall cast them before your mother and depart.

children.text: iti rāgāndhaḥ śrutvā cetasi kurute kadā cidevamidam /
children.translated_text: Thus hearing this, the one blinded by passion sometimes thinks in his heart:
'For women whose minds are governed by affection, there is nothing they will not do.'

children.text: jananīṃ janmasthānaṃ bāndhavalokaṃ vasūni jīvaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Their mother, their birthplace, the circle of their kinsmen, their possessions, and their very lives —
women attached to a particular man consider these as worthless as straw.
When <s>Vajra</s> was slain on the battlefield by a stone hurled from a catapult hard as a thunderbolt,

children.text: prāṇānmumoca dayitā na mantravidhinā hṛtā nāma // DKuṭṭ_559 //
children.translated_text: his beloved gave up her life — not taken away by any magical rite, mind you.
When <s>Maṇikaṇṭha</s>, the southerner, met his death by the force of time,

children.text: premopagatā veśyā tenaiva samaṃ jagāma bhasmatvam // DKuṭṭ_560 //
children.translated_text: a courtesan, overcome by love, turned to ashes together with him.
When <s>Bhāskaravarman</s> departed to the abode of the gods, though restrained by the king,
a <s>vilāsinī</s> (courtesan), unable to bear that grief, entered the fire.
When the <s>Nagna</s> (Jain) teacher <s>Narasiṃha</s> fell into the blazing fire with its terrible flames,
a slave-woman, tormented by grief, offered her own body in that very fire.
Her mind overwhelmed by the weight of affection, <s>Jīhallā</s> accepted

children.text: aṅgīcakāra muktvā Jīhallā Bhaṭṭaviṣṇumā mṛtyoḥ // DKuṭṭ_563 //
children.translated_text: the livelihood of serving in the abode of the gods, which came to her in due course, releasing <s>Bhaṭṭaviṣṇu</s> from death.
When her beloved returned from a foreign land, upon merely catching a gracious glimpse of him,

children.text: pādayugaṃ tatyajaturna Vāmadevasya samiti nihatasya // DKuṭṭ_564 //
children.translated_text: two women did not let go of the feet of <s>Vāmadeva</s>, who had been slain in battle.
When the son of <s>Bhaṭṭakadambaka</s> departed to the abode of the lord of the dead,

children.text: cakre dehatyāgaṃ raṇadevī vārayoṣitāṃ mukhyā // DKuṭṭ_565 //
children.translated_text: <s>Raṇadevī</s>, foremost among courtesans, gave up her body.
In this very city, a <s>gaṇikā</s> (courtesan), drawn by love,
gave away all her wealth accumulated over a lifetime to <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s>, the son of a <s>Bhaṭṭa</s>.

children.text: iyamapi mayi vihitāsthā mātṛvacaḥśravaṇakaluṣitā kva gatā /
children.translated_text: 'And this one too, who had placed her trust in me — where has she gone, her mind polluted by listening to her mother's words,
having cast off all her ornaments, her anger and agitation fully displayed?'
'I shall now gratify the doe-eyed one with all my possessions —
her who has cast away her ornaments, whose retinue has been abandoned save for what her mother released.'
'What need have I for a house, or for other kinsmen, wife, and household?

children.text: saṃsāragrahakāraṇamekā khalu Mālatī mama hi // DKuṭṭ_569 //
children.translated_text: Indeed, <s>Mālatī</s> alone is the reason for my remaining in this cycle of existence.'
She, embraced ever more tightly, as if fashioned from the limbs of the moon,

children.text: ceto nayati samatvaṃ brahmaṇa ānandarūpasya // DKuṭṭ_570 //
children.translated_text: leads his mind to the equanimity of <s>Brahman</s> (the Absolute), whose nature is bliss.
Her composure shattered by the agitation of passion arising within her, impetuously,
her garment slipping from her pair of breasts, <s>Mālatī</s> embraces the fortunate one.
During lovemaking, the merciless biting of her lips accompanied by pained moaning sounds —

children.text: ahaheti vacastasyā apuṇyabhājo na śṛṇvanti // DKuṭṭ_572 //
children.translated_text: the 'aha!' cries from her — the unfortunate ones do not get to hear them.
Agitated by the tumult and clashing of vigorous lovemaking, the beloved
renders the cycle of existence hidden, covered by the observance of transformations born of remembered births.
When her body is tightly embraced, the beloved experiences the rapturous swoon of delight;

children.text: śithilīkṛtā tu kiṃ cidvividhavikāraṃ samucchvasiti // DKuṭṭ_574 //
children.translated_text: but when slightly released, she breathes deeply with various tremors.
There are indeed other women skilled in the acts befitting a man,

children.text: sṛṣṭā tu tayā niyataṃ viparītaratikriyāgoṣṭhī // DKuṭṭ_575 //
children.translated_text: but the art of <s>viparītarati</s> (inverted lovemaking) was surely created by her alone.
Her mastery in producing <s>kuharita</s> (cooing), <s>recita</s> (moaning), and <s>kampita</s> (trembling)
renders the extraordinary arts of playing stringed instruments, which others have from past births, seem dull by comparison.
Seeing the graceful movements, gestures, yawning, bending, smiling, and trembling of <s>Mālatī</s>,
<s>Kāma</s> (the god of love) abandons his admiration for the amorous gestures of <s>Rati</s>.
Her laughter is never vulgar, her sidelong glances never lack playful charm,
she never resists the exertion of love, nor denies the longings of <s>Puṣpabāṇa</s> (the Flower-Arrowed one, Kāma).
Her talk never aims at wealth, she is never unskilled in discerning others' minds,
and in her speech there is never crudeness when incidentally praising outstanding qualities.
She never praises other men, never abandons propriety of time, place, and dress —
she who moves slowly under the heavy burden of her ample hips, the very birthplace of refinement.
She performs the <s>cakrāhva</s> (cakravāka-style) embrace, the <s>haṃsa</s> (swan-style) clasp, the <s>nakula</s> (mongoose-style) hold,
and the <s>pārāvata</s> (pigeon-style) enfolding, the slender-waisted one, each as the occasion demands.
For him whose mind is captivated by her oblique words, laughter, and conduct,

children.text: anukūlasundarā api bharaṇīyabharāya kevalaṃ dārāḥ // DKuṭṭ_582 //
children.translated_text: even his own agreeable and beautiful wife becomes merely a burden to maintain.
She hints at the need for a separate household, speaks of her brothers' difficult temperaments,
reveals the disarray of the home, and praises the virtues of her father's family.
She speaks of the mother's favoritism toward another daughter, disparages the husband —

children.text: pārśvanimagnā jāyā mā yātu vimucya kārmukaṃ Madanaḥ // DKuṭṭ_584 //
children.translated_text: let <s>Madana</s> (the god of love) not release his bow while his wife is sunk at his side!

children.text: evaṃ kṛte 'pi sundari yadi tiṣṭhati nāyakaḥ prakṛtyaiva /
children.translated_text: O beautiful one, even when all this has been done, if the lover remains steadfast by nature,

children.text: itthaṃ pathi parimoṣastvatsakhyā naipuṇena vaktavyaḥ // DKuṭṭ_585 //
children.translated_text: then a robbery on the road must be arranged by your friend with this cunning:
On account of being busy with household duties, or in order to win the hearts of respectable women,

children.text: nāyāte bhavati sakhī prāvṛḍghanakaluṣite diśāṃ cakre // DKuṭṭ_586 //
children.translated_text: when the friend does not come, on a night when the quarters of the sky are darkened by monsoon clouds,
lying on a raised couch, with the agitation of her own passion swelling,
her eyes fixed upon the path to you, she heard a song sung by another as if it were meant for her.

children.text: yadi jīvitena kṛtyaṃ saṃbhāvaya virahiṇi priyaṃ tūrṇam /
children.translated_text: 'If you value your life, O beloved, hasten to comfort the one suffering in separation,

children.text: ghanarasitasya hi purataḥ kadalīdalakomalaḥ kuliśapātaḥ // DKuṭṭ_588 //
children.translated_text: for before the roar of the thundercloud, the fall of the thunderbolt is as soft as a plantain leaf.'
Hearing this, she spoke to me: 'Blessed are those women, O friend, who are hard-hearted,
who can endure the prolonged burning fire of separation from their dearest beloved.'

children.text: mama tu dināntarite 'pi preyasi labdhvā sahāyasāmagrīm /
children.translated_text: 'But for me, even when my beloved is absent just for a day, having found full cause,
<s>Makaraketana</s> (the Banner-of-Makara, Kāma) makes my heart tremble with surging longing.'
'The breeze, rich with the fragrance of <s>bakula</s> flowers, intensely fills me with yearning;
the <s>kalāpabhṛt</s> (peacocks) shake my resolve with their sweet cries.'
'She who had incessantly embraced her beloved

children.text: utsahate sā vīkṣitumaviralamāliṅgito yayā kāntaḥ // DKuṭṭ_592 //
children.translated_text: could barely bring herself to gaze upon the rising mass of dark clouds accompanied by lightning flashes and rows of cranes.'
Women, eager for union with their most desired one, do not consider
the impropriety of going on their own, the many dangers, or the roads at night.

children.text: kriyatāṃ bhūṣaṇaśobhā tvarayati me mānasaṃ Manojanmā /
children.translated_text: 'Let my adornment be made beautiful — <s>Manojanmā</s> (the Mind-born one, Kāma) urges my heart;

children.text: rañjayati mano nitarāṃ kaladhautaniveśitaṃ ratnam // DKuṭṭ_594 //
children.translated_text: a gem set in gold delights the mind exceedingly.'
When the horizons are covered with dense rain-clouds, at the hour of dusk, as she prepares
to go out at nightfall — O you who are blinded by passion, what is this foolish plan you have begun?
A new <s>abhisārikā</s> (woman who goes out to meet her lover) has been seen —
she who desires to go to a man staying in another place, relying on the essence of elaborate speech concerning his wife.
Her <s>tilaka</s> (forehead mark) half-washed away, the tips of her hair disheveled by falling drops of water,
her thin garment clinging in the darkness, her body bristling from the fierce wind and rain,
stumbling with her feet on uneven ground she cannot see, clinging to the hand of her companion,

children.text: purato 'dhvanaḥ pramāṇaṃ muhurmuhuḥ sādhvasena pṛcchantīm // DKuṭṭ_598 //
children.translated_text: asking again and again in trepidation about the distance of the road ahead —

children.text: anyasmin pretapatau vyagre kṛcchreṇa kathamapi prāptām /
children.translated_text: when the other man, the lord of the household, was busy with something else, she arrived with great difficulty;
she was announced by servants appropriate for the occasion — thus deliberating with his ministers:
'Is this the greatness of love? Or is it the limitlessness of the lure of wealth?

children.text: kiṃ vānyataḥ pravṛttā praveśitā vātavarṣeṇa // DKuṭṭ_600 //
children.translated_text: Or has she come from elsewhere and been driven inside by the wind and rain?'
Since it is improper when one's wives are present — on the pretext of public propriety —
she was dismissed by the lover of <s>Mālatī</s> to stay in another dwelling.
Laughed at by the people, wearing garments soaked with water,
her pride in her beauty abandoned, her face downcast with embarrassed shame,
seized by remorse, her soles cut by thorns and tips of <s>darbha</s> grass,
remembering our words — the virtuous ones shall see such an <s>abhisārikā</s> (woman who ventures out to meet her lover).
Thus, disregarding the mother who spoke harshly, as she set out toward your presence,

children.text: caurahatakā vrajantīṃ vidrāvitarakṣiṇaḥ sakhīṃ mumuṣuḥ // DKuṭṭ_604 //
children.translated_text: the guards who had been driven off tried to seize your friend, who was attacked by thieves on the way.

children.text: eṣā prapañcaracanā yadi bhavati vṛthā punaḥ purastasya /
children.translated_text: If this elaborate stratagem proves futile, then in his presence
a merchant, prompted by an accomplice, will come and say this to you:
'In addition to the pearl necklace given earlier, thirty <s>kedāras</s> (fields of land),

children.text: paricārikayānītā anyānapi mṛgayate vyayasya kṛte // DKuṭṭ_606 //
children.translated_text: brought through a maidservant — and he seeks still more for his expenditures.'
'As for the gifts of camphor, saffron, sandalwood, incense, and the like given freely,

children.text: tatsampuṭake likhitaṃ śṛṇu piṇḍanikāṃ karomi te purataḥ // DKuṭṭ_607 //
children.translated_text: those are recorded in the casket — listen, I shall make you an itemized account right here.'
'For all this time you were not pressed with demands,

children.text: riktaṃ bhāṇḍasthānaṃ sāmpratamiti yācanā kriyate // DKuṭṭ_608 //
children.translated_text: but now the treasury is empty — therefore this request is being made.'
When he speaks thus, you should stand for a moment with a show of slight embarrassment,
and then address him in a humble voice, with an air of bashfulness:
'Let your pearl necklace remain with you, at the price determined by a neutral assessor;
as for the rest, whatever else remains, I shall arrange it within a few days.'
If even this woven deception proves as fruitless as a eunuch, then the following must be said:

children.text: āśaṅkante 'niṣṭaṃ kātarahṛdayā hi yoṣitaḥ prāyaḥ // DKuṭṭ_611 //
children.translated_text: 'Women are generally faint of heart and apprehend misfortune.'

children.text: apaṭuśarīre svāmini vijñaptā bhagavatī mayā gatvā /
children.translated_text: 'When my lord was unwell in body, I went and made a petition to the goddess:
"By your grace, may the lord of my life be restored to a healthy body."'
'Having had my wish fulfilled, I shall worship her with offerings and oblations,

children.text: sāmagrīviraheṇa tu na vitīrṇā tatra me manasi śūkā // DKuṭṭ_613 //
children.translated_text: but for want of the necessary supplies, I have not yet discharged the vow — this pricks my conscience.'
If this too proves futile, then from his house that has been emptied and is falling apart,
O slow-witted one, you must cause a fire, and the total ruin must be made to appear accidental.
'Having perceived sufficient intimacy through the signs of shared meals, shared bed, and shared garments,
by these means he should be made to vomit and purge [i.e., drain of wealth]. // 615 //
'By the method of tormenting him with moneylenders' [demands], by the loss of possessions, or by the words of associates —
even when he is [already] despised — skillfully, O one of beautiful limbs, when his substance has been drained: // 616 //
'The determination [expressed] through harsh words: "He is a future saboteur of [our] interests" —
these methods of releasing a patron should be carefully employed.' // 617 //
'Directing him to a separate seat; slackening in rising to greet him and such courtesies;
conversations tinged with envy and mockery; jesting that pierces the vital spots; // 618 //
'praising his rival; repeatedly publicizing his rival's superior qualities and one's attachment to them;
when he speaks affectionately, denouncing him as excessively talkative; // 619 //
'interrupting his words with obstructions; rejecting the topic of conversation he has introduced;
expressing disgust at his dealings; leaving his side with some pretext; // 620 //
'killing time with some excuse; turning away in bed at the time for sleep;
announcing that one is overcome by drowsiness; showing distress at being face-to-face; // 621 //
'preventing the touch of intimate parts; maintaining a natural posture during sexual advances;
distorting the face when he kisses; stiffening the body rigidly when he embraces; // 622 //
'showing intolerance at the occasions of being struck, or scratched by nails, or bitten;

children.text: dīrgharate nirvedaḥ svapihīti vaco 'bhiyojake bhūyaḥ // DKuṭṭ_623 //
children.translated_text: expressing weariness during prolonged love-play; saying "go away" to one who approaches again; // 623 //
'persisting even when he is incapable; similarly, laughing at his attempts to display skill;
with desire for the night to end, repeatedly asking the night-watchman [for the time]; // 624 //
'hastily leaving the bedchamber at dawn, rising from the bed in a rush,
exclaiming eagerly: "The night is over! It is dawn!" — // 625 //

children.text: ubhayecchayā pravṛttaṃ nirupādhi prema bhavati ramaṇīyam /
children.translated_text: 'Love that arises from mutual desire, unconditional, is truly delightful,
when the two are deeply attached to each other — like the natural setting of a fine gem in gold. // 626 //
'But love that is one-sided is without doubt the cause

children.text: sa nidānamasaṃdigdhaṃ sītāṃ prati daśamukhasyeva // DKuṭṭ_627 //
children.translated_text: of humiliation, weakness, wretchedness, and ruin — as [was the case of] <s>Rāvaṇa</s> toward <s>Sītā</s>. // 627 //
'The very smiles, glances, and sweet talk of those who are enamored
appear reversed, as it were, to those who have fallen out of love. // 628 //
'Where women think in their minds: "Let him do whatever he wants — I shall endure it for a moment" —

children.text: iti yatra manaḥ strīṇāṃ tatrāpi rate ramanti paśutulyāḥ // DKuṭṭ_629 //
children.translated_text: even in that lovemaking, those who are like cattle take delight. // 629 //

children.text: yatra na madanavikārāḥ sadbhāvasamarpaṇaṃ na gātrāṇām /
children.translated_text: 'Where there are no transformations of love, no genuine surrender of the body,

children.text: tasminnujjhitabhāve paśukarmaṇi paśava eva rajyante // DKuṭṭ_630 //
children.translated_text: in that joyless, animal act, only animals take pleasure. // 630 //
'A man of self-respect, wounded by contempt, his genuine feeling diminishing day by day,
will abandon even a foolish woman. // 631 //
'The man whom a woman mocks by clapping her palm against her friend's palm as a witness —

children.text: yaṃ naramupahasati strī dadātu tasmai mahī randhram // DKuṭṭ_632 //
children.translated_text: let the earth open a hole for him! // 632 //
'A man who hears the praise of another man's qualities, and criticism of himself directed at someone else,

children.text: śṛṇvannapi yaḥ svasthaḥ svastho 'sau kālapāśabaddho 'pi // DKuṭṭ_633 //
children.translated_text: and yet remains unperturbed — he is indeed unperturbed, even when bound by the noose of Death! // 633 //
'A man whom even the servants treat with contempt, having understood their mistress's intentions —

children.text: vyavaharati tiraskurvaṃstasya na mūlyaṃ varāṭikāḥ pañca // DKuṭṭ_634 //
children.translated_text: his worth is not even five <s>varāṭikā</s> (cowrie shells). // 634 //
'He who does not know the difference between genuine and feigned behavior
becomes, without doubt, a suitable candidate for <s>Paśupati</s> [<s>Śiva</s>] — for obtaining the half-moon [i.e., becoming a renunciant]. // 635 //
'Having gradually lost his portion of dignity, fallen into lightness through his emptiness,
unable to reach the bank of discernment — that wretched man floats in the lake of women. // 636 //
'The displays of affection (<s>anubhāvas</s>) carefully fabricated to convey the appearance of passion (<s>śṛṅgāra</s>) —
those who make their living by the craft of love (<s>ratiśilpa</s>), the foolish take them as genuine. // 637 //
'Women who are won by money, who are without moral limits, whose purpose is self-interest —

children.text: tābhirapi samīhante bata mandāḥ saṃgatamajaryam // DKuṭṭ_638 //
children.translated_text: alas, even with them, fools desire imperishable union! // 638 //
'"A patron is acceptable [only] when his wealth is visibly present; even a wealthy man is not otherwise" — thus it has been stated
by the authors of the <s>Kāmaśāstra</s>; how then can there be any question regarding those who have lost their wealth? // 639 //

children.text: vyāsamunināpi gītaṃ dvāveva narādhamau mano dahataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Even the sage <s>Vyāsa</s> sang: "Two lowest of men burn the mind:
he who desires without being rich, and he who becomes angry though without power." // 640 //

children.text: kṣīṇadravye dehini dārā api nādareṇa vartante /
children.translated_text: 'When wealth is exhausted in an embodied being, even his own wives do not treat him with respect;
how much less so slave-women, whose sole relish is taking, whose livelihood is the commerce of their bodies! // 641 //
'Even animals, who do not know what is to be rejected and what accepted, abandon a flower whose juice has been drunk;

children.text: kusumaṃ kimu kāryavido veśyā naramāttasarvasvam // DKuṭṭ_642 //
children.translated_text: how much more so courtesans, who know their purpose, toward a man whose entire substance has been consumed! // 642 //
'Just as a man who always gives arouses increasing passion because he is of passionate nature,

children.text: nirdāno 'pi sadā no niḥsaṃdehaṃ tathaiva manujanmā // DKuṭṭ_643 //
children.translated_text: so too, without doubt, does one who never gives, by his human birth [ironically — i.e., he produces only aversion]. // 643 //
'What is past is past; even in future gain there should be no excessive regard;
the wealth that falls into the hand at the present moment is the delight of women whose men are not fixed. // 644 //
'The honey that has been squeezed out, the love-sick drained bee-mass rendered hollow —
both the petty ones and the openly wanton courtesans abandon the residue of love. // 645 //

children.text: ekaḥ krīṇātyadya prāto bhavitā tathāparaḥ kretā /
children.translated_text: 'One buys today; tomorrow another buyer will come;

children.text: anyavaśe kṣaṇamekaṃ na vikrayaḥ śāśvato 'sti veśyānām // DKuṭṭ_646 //
children.translated_text: in another's power for only a moment — the sale of courtesans is not permanent. // 646 //
'Let those who have ears hear: the arch of the brow, the sidelong glance, the glimpsed smile, and such —
shown as if conveying deep truth, when done, are transferred to another. // 647 //

children.text: yadi nāma nirākaraṇe na samarthā chinnakāryabandhe 'pi /
children.translated_text: 'Even if a woman of great dignity is unable to refuse [a patron], though the bond of business is severed,

children.text: kā cinmahānubhāvā boddhavyaṃ tadapi cetanāvadbhiḥ // DKuṭṭ_648 //
