children.translated_text: that too should be understood by those who have discernment. // 648 //
'He served her with his wealth, and she too served him with the gift of her body;
that is now past — henceforth, dry romance is purposeless. // 649 //
'A man for whom contempt is a tonic, and insult a source of satisfaction —
that donkey among men deserves the cudgel of even harsher rebukes and harsh words! // 650 //

children.text: dīpajvālālalane vrajataḥ khalu nirvṛtiṃ tayostviyān bhedaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'One who goes toward a lamp-flame [i.e., both a moth and a lover drawn to a courtesan] certainly reaches destruction — the difference between the two is this:

children.text: prathamā snehena vinā tathāparā snehayogena // DKuṭṭ_651 //
children.translated_text: the first [perishes] without love (<s>sneha</s>, also "oil"), while the other through the presence of love (<s>sneha</s>). // 651 //
'<s>Dharma</s> (merit) comes from love for a man adorned with new qualities who is lovesick;
<s>artha</s> (wealth) from the approach of a wealthy man; <s>kāma</s> (pleasure) from the sexual enjoyment of a man skilled in lovemaking. // 652 //

children.text: yastu na dharmaprāptyai nārthāya na kāmasādhanopāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'But a man who is neither a means to <s>dharma</s>, nor to <s>artha</s>, nor a device for obtaining <s>kāma</s> —
when questioned by those whose wealth is good conduct, what does he say? // 653 //
'The youth of fools — seized by the agitation of desire, its romance mocked by rogues,
stricken by poverty — is only for their ruin. // 654 //
'When a passionate man's coffers are empty, it is the petty bee, gratified by obtaining mere drink,

children.text: kṣudrā madhukarikābje na tu gaṇikā cintitasvārthā // DKuṭṭ_655 //
children.translated_text: that merges [with the flower], not the courtesan, who has her own interests in mind. // 655 //
'Those courtesans who have a purposeful concern even in a glance cast with sidelong eyes —
how are they to be deceived by men who are agitated merely by being seen? // 656 //
'The four performances of a courtesan — mind, praise, body, and flattering gestures —
are for the attraction of those fattened with inherited wealth, and for the torment of the destitute. // 657 //

children.text: kiṃ dhakṣyati bhūyo 'pi jvalanastaṃ tādṛśaṃ kulāṅgāram /
children.translated_text: 'What further burning can fire do to such a charcoal of a family
that burns ceaselessly from the contemptuous dismissals of a disaffected slave-woman? // 658 //
'This house is for the wealthy; it is an impenetrable forest for others;
"Shoo!" said <s>Mālatī</s> with upraised arm — she is not one devoted to giving away love as charity.' // 659 //
Thus, hearing the words — piercing his vital points —

children.text: ākarṇayato vāco daivopahatasya tasya marmabhidaḥ // DKuṭṭ_660 //
children.translated_text: of the house-servant, prompted [by her mistress], speaking harsh syllables, directed at nobody in particular, of him who was struck by fate: // 660 //
'If even so addressed, this brute in human form does not understand,

children.text: tadidaṃ sundari vācyaḥ praśritavacasā tvayā kāmī // DKuṭṭ_661 //
children.translated_text: then, O beautiful one, this lover should be told by you in humble words: // 661 //

children.text: prīyata eva tavopari hṛdayaṃ me kiṃ tu gurujanādhīnā /
children.translated_text: '"My heart is indeed devoted to you, but I am under the authority of my elders;
I am not able to transgress my mother's words. // 662 //
'"So please go from here for a few days;

children.text: punarapi bhavataiva samaṃ bhoktavyaṃ jīvalokasukham // DKuṭṭ_663 //
children.translated_text: then once again, the pleasures of this mortal world shall be enjoyed together with you." // 663 //

children.text: nirvāsite tu tasmin yaḥ kāmī pūrvamujjhito bhuktvā /
children.translated_text: 'But when he has been expelled, the former lover who was rejected, having consumed [his wealth] — when he has acquired new wealth,
this is the strategy for reconciliation with him: // 664 //
'The narration of past events — the garden excursions, the sports, the brilliant and lovely jesting — together with him;
and displaying the symptoms of love's fever when gazing upon him: // 665 //
'"This supremely blessed garden, tightly embraced by fragrant beauty —
my lord of life wandered here, with his hand resting on my shoulder. // 666 //

children.text: sakhya ito bhramarakulatrāsitayā priyatamo mayā sahasā /
children.translated_text: '"O friend, right here, when I was startled by a swarm of bees, my beloved suddenly
embraced me as my breasts arched forward, breathing a slow, deep sigh. // 667 //
'"In this bower of <s>atimukta</s> (jasmine), lovely with the sound of buzzing bees and cooing cuckoos,
covered with blossoms scattered by the stirring of the wind — // 668 //
'"when passionate love had grown strong in me, and <s>Kāma</s> (Love) was powerful, with all his allied forces,
my beloved, on a bed of leaves, was never satisfied in our secluded acts. // 669 //
'"The rogue, on the pretext of giving me a push on the swing, scratching my sides with his nails,

children.text: cakre māṃ madanamayīṃ vratatipreṅkhāmimāṃ samārūḍhām // DKuṭṭ_670 //
children.translated_text: made me — mounted on this very swing of creepers — entirely suffused with love. // 670 //
'"This <s>aśoka</s> tree is to be envied, having been touched by my beloved's hand
as he was examining its fresh young leaves and shoots to make a garland for me. // 671 //
'"Sitting playfully on his lap beneath this mango tree,

children.text: aśṛṇavamahamiti vācaḥ paśyantī vilasitāni taruṇānām // DKuṭṭ_672 //
children.translated_text: I heard these words while watching the dalliances of young lovers: // 672 //
'"'Lift up your beloved who has fallen at your feet at once, O <s>Mānarasā</s>!

children.text: atyākṛṣṭaṃ truṭyati sudṛḍhamapi premabandhanaṃ mūḍhe // DKuṭṭ_673 //
children.translated_text: If pulled too hard, even a firm bond of love breaks, O foolish one!' // 673 //

children.text: tiṣṭhannapi yātasamaḥ kiṃ tena nivāritena sakhi paśunā /
children.translated_text: '"'Even while staying, he is as good as gone — what use, O friend, in restraining that brute,

children.text: yāmīti niṣprakampaṃ viniḥsṛtā yasya Mādhave vāṇī // DKuṭṭ_674 //
children.translated_text: from whose mouth during <s>Mādhava</s> (spring) the word "I am going" issued forth without a tremor?' // 674 //
'"'Youth is the essence of life; spring is the essence of seasons; the Flower-arrowed one (<s>Kāma</s>) is the companion [of spring];
O beautiful one, the tasting of the nectar of love's pleasures is the essence of life.' // 675 //

children.text: ramyaṃ kusumastabakaṃ kuru me priya kaiṅkirātamavataṃsam /
children.translated_text: '"'Make for me, dear, a cluster of flowers as an ear-ornament from the <s>kiṅkirāta</s> [shrub];

children.text: tiṣṭhatu vā kimanena pratyagramaśokakisalayaṃ cāru // DKuṭṭ_676 //
children.translated_text: or let it be — what use is that? — a fresh <s>aśoka</s> shoot is beautiful.' // 676 //
'"'Never mind, never mind that — bring me the lovely <s>sinduvāra</s> (vitex);

children.text: nahi nahi rājati sutarāṃ cūtadrumamañjarī karṇe // DKuṭṭ_677 //
children.translated_text: no, no — a <s>cūta</s> (mango) blossom-spray looks far better on the ear.' // 677 //
'"'Fie on youth without a beloved! Fie on a beloved deprived of youth!
And fie on both together, when blossoming with the power of <s>Manmatha</s>, without lovemaking!' // 678 //
'"'Though provocation arose from a hundred offenses, and though anger took deep root in that perverse one,

children.text: avagatamadhunā sakhyo na vasantamatītya vartate mānaḥ // DKuṭṭ_679 //
children.translated_text: now it is understood, O friends — a fit of pique (<s>māna</s>) does not last beyond spring.' // 679 //
'"'The essence of a hundred years is that tiny moment of the first meeting place,

children.text: sacakitamāgacchantī sotkalikā yatra dṛśyate ramaṇī // DKuṭṭ_680 //
children.translated_text: where the beloved is seen approaching timidly, with rising excitement.' // 680 //

children.text: kiṃ nirmito 'si dhātrā navo 'paraḥ kimu vasantaguṇa eṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: '"'Has the Creator fashioned some new [marvel]? Or is this a special quality of spring?
Has <s>Kandarpa</s> [<s>Kāma</s>] filled his quiver with arrows? Or has some entirely different Love-god come into being?' // 681 //
'"'If you do not see the <s>kakubha</s> trees, lovely with abundantly blazing, fragrant blossoms,
if you do not hear the humming of bees mingled with the songs of cuckoos — // 682 //'

children.text: gandhaṃ yadi no labhase vāsitadigvyoma sumanasāṃ hṛdyam /
children.translated_text: If you cannot obtain the delightful fragrance of flowers that perfumes the sky in every direction,

children.text: anubhavasi yadi sparśaṃ no śītaladākṣiṇātyapavanasya // DKuṭṭ_683 //
children.translated_text: if you cannot experience the touch of the cool southern breeze, // 683 //
you who are reduced to the sense of taste alone, passed around by people, despised —

children.text: nārhasi tato 'pi muktvā nijāśrayaṃ gantumanyato nitarām // DKuṭṭ_684 //
children.translated_text: you ought not, abandoning your own abode, to go elsewhere all the more on that account. // 684 //
In this pool, playfully, with streams of water shooting from hand-pumps,
I was struck by my beloved, and he in turn was struck by me with a lotus stalk. // 685 //
Then, having dived beneath the water and approaching me undetected, he suddenly
lifted me up with a laugh, making the assembled retinue burst into laughter. // 686 //
As he gazed at my hips, clinging wet garments pressed against them,
<s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic sentiment) in its consummation took on the character of first longing and desire. // 687 //
For even passion long established among young lovers is brought to freshness

children.text: cirarūḍho 'pi hi yūnāṃ navatvamupanīyate rāgaḥ // DKuṭṭ_688 //
children.translated_text: through particular conjunctions of time, place, dress, activity, and situation. // 688 //
Friends, I suddenly recall the embarrassment of him who, while respectfully offering a lotus,

children.text: sakhyaḥ smarāmi sahasā vilakṣatāṃ kliṣṭahasitasya // DKuṭṭ_689 //
children.translated_text: had committed the offence of a slip of the name, and smiled with strained laughter. // 689 //
When my beloved cast his eyes with longing upon the space between my breasts, freshly scratched with nail-marks,
I, bashful, made a lotus leaf into a covering. // 690 //
When water was unexpectedly thrown at me, concealed within a cupped lotus leaf, from nearby,

children.text: āhatayā yadvikṛtaṃ svasthadhiyā tanna śakyate kartum // DKuṭṭ_691 //
children.translated_text: the distortion of expression produced by being struck — that cannot be reproduced by one of composed mind. // 691 //
A well-executed display of <s>hāva</s> (coquetry), a graceful languid stretching of limbs heavy with passion,
the revealing of intimate places, the snapping of fingers, a charming smile, // 692 //
the repeated loosening and tying of the girdle, the disheveling of the mass of hair,
the biting of one's own lip, the kissing of the child, the eagerness for love — // 693 //
casting her restless, wide eyes again and again with longing toward the desired one,
addressing his companion — thus she spoke in words choked with grief. // 694 //
Just as swans have the power to separate water and milk that have become one,
so too do wicked people have the power to sever those whose hearts are united as friends. // 695 //
The scoundrel speaks words that are exceedingly smooth, excessively measured in tone, and lighter than air,

children.text: paramārthataḥ sa hṛdayaṃ vahati punaḥ kālakūṭaghaṭitamiva // DKuṭṭ_696 //
children.translated_text: but in truth he carries a heart as if compounded with <s>kālakūṭa</s> (deadly poison). // 696 //
That is why he, having dismissed the attendants, with anger openly displayed like an actor's,
assuming the appearance of a well-wisher, the rogue skilled in causing harm to others, spoke thus to me: // 697 //
'What fault is it of those dwelling on the frontiers, who do not know the differences in quality,

children.text: svādhīnakuṅkumā api yadvidadhati bahumatiṃ nīle // DKuṭṭ_698 //
children.translated_text: that even those who have <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron) at their disposal hold indigo in high regard?' // 698 //
'Where are you, a <s>Rambhā</s> (celestial nymph) upon the earth, whose bodily radiance puts the moon's light to shame —

children.text: Citralatā kva varākī nīcairupasevitā voṭā // DKuṭṭ_699 //
children.translated_text: and where is that wretched <s>Citralatā</s>, a lowly <s>voṭā</s> (courtesan) patronized by base men?' // 699 //

children.text: yasyārthe na vigaṇitāḥ prahvātmāno mahādhanāḥ kulajāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He for whose sake those of great wealth, noble birth, and humble bearing were disregarded —

children.text: so 'dya hṛdayena tasyāṃ tvayi tiṣṭhati bāhyavṛttena // DKuṭṭ_700 //
children.translated_text: that very man now stands with his heart turned outward toward her, while remaining with you only in outward conduct.' // 700 //
'That same behavior, set in motion by the skillful through true and false appearances,
the clever ones discern there, distinguishing between affection and indifference.' // 701 //
'But for you, whose love has grown deep, the mind's faculty does not rise
to the discernment of such conduct' — thus it was reported to me through familiarity. // 702 //
Thus, my entire body poisoned by the venom of words issuing from the serpent of that wicked person,
the pangs of jealousy grew intense, born from the shattering of long-established love. // 703 //
Because of the fickleness of their hearts, the minds of women, shattered by the thunderbolt of harsh words,

children.text: vaktṛviśeṣavitarko na spṛśati prāyaśo manaḥ strīṇām // DKuṭṭ_704 //
children.translated_text: for the most part do not engage in deliberation about the particular speaker. // 704 //

children.text: priyamapi vadan durātmā kṣipati vipatsāgare duruttare /
children.translated_text: A wicked person, even while speaking pleasant things, casts one into the impassable ocean of calamity;

children.text: āsādya prāṇabhṛto mṛtaye parileḍhi jihvayā khaḍgaḥ // DKuṭṭ_705 //
children.translated_text: a sword, upon reaching living beings, licks them with its tongue unto death. // 705 //
Entering into the practice of speech composed of kind and sweet syllables, becoming absorbed in it,

children.text: saralā durāśayānāmupaghātaṃ phalata eva vindanti // DKuṭṭ_706 //
children.translated_text: the guileless find from the ill-intentioned only injury as the fruit. // 706 //
On a day when the amusement of tormenting others does not reach completion,

children.text: antarmanā asādhurna gaṇayati tadāyuṣo madhye // DKuṭṭ_707 //
children.translated_text: the wicked person, troubled within, does not count that day among the days of his life. // 707 //

children.text: divasāntānabhinandati bahu manute teṣu janmano lābham /
children.translated_text: He celebrates the ends of days, he greatly esteems the gain of being born on those days
which pass in the application of causing suffering to others, the evil-minded one. // 708 //
As the rogue goes about with beaming face and wide-open eyes,

children.text: manye tathā na jātaḥ sadahitakaraṇaśramo vandhyaḥ // DKuṭṭ_709 //
children.translated_text: I think such a one has never been born for whom the labor of harming the good has been fruitless. // 709 //
The deceitful hunter, with arrows of cunning, striking the good who are like deer unaware of countermeasures,
practiced in hitting the mark, does not feel any exertion in slaying them. // 710 //
Among men whose deep-rooted passion is directed toward faithful and excellent wives,

children.text: nayati mano duḥśīlaḥ kusumāstro hīnapātreṣu // DKuṭṭ_711 //
children.translated_text: the wicked <s>Kusumāstra</s> (<s>Madana</s>, the god of love) leads the mind toward unworthy objects. // 711 //
When the beloved goes to another with concealment, out of curiosity, through casual association,
clever-minded women, even knowing this, conduct themselves according to the rules of drama. // 712 //

children.text: satyaṃ premaṇi vṛddhe vyathayati hṛdayaṃ manāgapi skhalitam /
children.translated_text: Truly, when love has grown great, even a slight stumble wounds the heart;
yet the steadfast, who have recognized their own greatness, do not lose their composure even then. // 713 //

children.text: svacchandaṃ pibatu rasaṃ bhrāntvā bhrāntvā vanāni kusumeṣu /
children.translated_text: Let the bee drink nectar freely, wandering from forest to forest among the blossoms;
having experienced the special qualities, it will return again to the <s>mālatī</s> (jasmine). // 714 //
The bee does not properly know the excellence of the <s>mālatī</s>
until it experiences the taste of intimacy with other flowers. // 715 //
Love, when subjected to the torment of gentle jealousy, shines with increased brilliance,

children.text: saṃcālyamānadāruḥ pāvaka iva suprabhaḥ snehaḥ // DKuṭṭ_716 //
children.translated_text: like fire that blazes brightly when the wood is stirred, through affection. // 716 //
But he who is drawn far away by the heat of the fire of excessive anger —

children.text: kācamaṇiḥ sa khalu yathā pariṇāme khaṇḍakhaṇḍamupayāti // DKuṭṭ_717 //
children.translated_text: he is indeed like a glass gem, which in the end breaks into pieces. // 717 //
Many men are served with propriety out of greed for wages,

children.text: viśrāmyati yatra manaḥ sa tu duṣprāpaḥ sahasreṣu // DKuṭṭ_718 //
children.translated_text: but he in whom the heart finds rest — such a one is hard to find among thousands. // 718 //
That <s>sukṛta</s> (merit) is truly difficult to comprehend even by the foremost sages beginning with <s>Manu</s>, who know the three times,
the fruit of which is the embrace of a beloved who comes rushing eagerly. // 719 //
She whose memory arises in times of distress even when the beloved has passed from the range of sight —

children.text: manye tāṃ prati niyataṃ kuṇṭhitaśarapañcakaḥ Madanaḥ // DKuṭṭ_720 //
children.translated_text: toward her, I believe, <s>Madana</s> (the god of love) surely has his five arrows blunted. // 720 //
One somehow lives on — alas for this conduct, censured by the great —
which a <s>gaṇikā</s> (courtesan) does not abandon out of greed for obtaining the lover she desires. // 721 //
A she-camel, feeding on thorny, bitter-sapped shrubs and bushes such as <s>karīra</s> and <s>khadira</s>,
by fortune obtains a sweet stream of honey. // 722 //
What is beauty when subject to an unloving man? What are graceful sports devoid of passion?

children.text: ko dharmo nirupaśamaḥ kiṃ saukhyaṃ vallabhena rahitānām // DKuṭṭ_723 //
children.translated_text: What is <s>dharma</s> without tranquility? What is happiness for those bereft of a beloved? // 723 //
Childhood has freedom as its fruit; youth has the enjoyment of pleasing love-play as its fruit;
old age has tranquility as its fruit; and the accomplishment of others' welfare is the fruit of birth itself. // 724 //
Upon hearing the <s>ālī</s> (female friend) speak thus, as if seized by a spirit,

children.text: yauvanasukhena sārdhaṃ mayaiva yūyaṃ paricchinnāḥ // DKuṭṭ_725 //
children.translated_text: 'Along with the pleasures of youth, it is I who have been cut off from you all. // 725 //
Now, placed in the midst of the fire of remorse, my every limb being scorched,
having attained a fruitless birth, I live by mere breathing alone. // 726 //

children.text: sthāneṣu yeṣu yuṣmatsaṃgatayā krīḍitaṃ ciraṃ dhṛtyā /
children.translated_text: Those very places where, through steadfastness, I long sported in your company —

children.text: tāni khalu vīkṣamāṇā bhavāmi kaṇṭhasthitaprāṇā // DKuṭṭ_727 //
children.translated_text: gazing upon them now, my life-breath stands at my throat. // 727 //
Subject to another's will, bereft of consciousness, adorned yet moving like a puppet on strings,

children.text: dārumayīva pratimā vidadhāmi viḍambanā bahvīḥ // DKuṭṭ_728 //
children.translated_text: like a wooden image, I perform many a mockery. // 728 //
Even if a bee-woman, for the sake of obtaining sustenance for her belly, embraces other flowers,

children.text: tadapi na puṣṭirbhṛṅgyā apibantyā āravindamakarandam // DKuṭṭ_729 //
children.translated_text: still there is no nourishment for her if she does not drink the nectar of the lotus. // 729 //
Let alone the next world — one who seeks pleasure, who delights in another's misfortune,

children.text: vyasanārṇave patantī na vāritā parijanenāsmi // DKuṭṭ_730 //
children.translated_text: I was not prevented by my attendants as I was falling into the ocean of calamity. // 730 //

children.text: kiṃ vā bahubhiḥ kathitaiḥ samprati niyame tu niyamitā buddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: But what use are many words? Now my mind is firmly resolved upon restraint;
I shall remain stationed in your household, assigned to the duties of a servant.' // 731 //
Thus, one brought under control through the transformations of eyes and other gestures, his body drained of firmness,
overcome by the grip of <s>Māra</s> (the god of desire), the memory of his former rejection wiped clean — // 732 //
his desire for love-play having arisen, his gaze falling moment by moment to the region of the collarbone,

children.text: pakvāmramiva vimokṣyasi pūrvavadācūṣya subhru niḥśeṣam // DKuṭṭ_733 //
children.translated_text: you shall release him like a ripe mango, O fair-browed one, having sucked him completely dry as before. // 733 //
Casting the hook of crooked smiles, glances, and words, baited with the flesh of your own body,

children.text: prakṣipyākṛśya jaḍaṃ sphuraṇena vivarjitaṃ suparipuṣṭam // DKuṭṭ_734 //
children.translated_text: and having pulled in the dull one, devoid of any struggle, well-fattened — // 734 //
having drawn him between your two hands and prepared him with the expenditure of attentions,

children.text: bhuktvā yāvanmāṃsaṃ tyakṣyasi carmāsthiśeṣitaṃ matsyam // DKuṭṭ_735 //
children.translated_text: having consumed all the flesh, you shall discard the fish, reduced to skin and bones. // 735 //
Listen, O fair-hipped one, how in this very place, by <s>Mañjarī</s>, daughter of the chief <s>ācārya</s> (teacher), at the foot of the <s>Kalaśeśvara</s> (temple),
a prince was chewed up and spat out. // 736 //
There was a king named <s>Śrī Siṃhabhaṭa</s>, foremost among the mighty;
his son took up residence in the quarter connected with <s>Devarāṣṭra</s>. // 737 //
He once, out of a desire to see the temple of <s>Vṛṣabhadhvaja</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), with a limited retinue of trusted attendants,
came along, following the manners and conduct stirred up by youth. // 738 //
His hair was bound with a large cloth strip positioned at the top third of his head;
his body-paint was slight and transparent, the tips of his hair by the ears thickly smeared with <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron). // 739 //
He had a forehead <s>tilaka</s> (mark) of white mustard seeds, and was chewing <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel),
with earrings set in his ears, and ornaments on his neck mostly of the <s>ṭīṭibhaka</s> type. // 740 //
At the place of the armlet he wore a gold-covered amulet containing a <s>mantra</s> (sacred formula) embedded in lac,
and on his wrists were strung garlands of gems and gold with dangling sprout-shaped pendants. // 741 //
He carried a cane staff, his hip wrapped in wool with a sword-hilt at his side,
covered in a soft fine cloth, with shoes on his feet that made a loud crunching sound. // 742 //

children.text: Gambhīreśvaradāsyāṃ lagnaḥ kila tava vayasyako vīraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Your friend <s>Vīra</s> is attached to <s>Gambhīreśvaradāsī</s>, it seems;

children.text: prāpsyati sāpi durāśāvarṣatritayena yanmayā prāptam // DKuṭṭ_743 //
children.translated_text: she too will obtain through vain hopes in three years what I have obtained.' // 743 //
'<s>Candravarmā</s> shows the directions their fruit, brings the moon down into his hand —
O <s>Suradevi</s>, all with an elaborate display of empty words!' // 744 //
'I see <s>Vasuṣeṇa</s> now following you, O <s>Kuraṅgī</s> (Doe-eyed one);

children.text: sunirūpitā bhaviṣyasi viṣamā guḍajihvikā tasya // DKuṭṭ_745 //
children.translated_text: you will be well examined — you will prove a bitter pill for him.' // 745 //

children.text: carvayati jalaṃ yo 'sau Hariṇi Haro dhūrtatābhimānena /
children.translated_text: 'That <s>Hara</s> who, O <s>Hariṇī</s> (Deer-girl), chews water out of pride in his roguery —

children.text: likhati śataṃ daśavṛddhyā sa nimagnastaralikāvarte // DKuṭṭ_746 //
children.translated_text: he writes a hundred at ten percent interest; he is sunk in the whirlpool of a <s>taralikā</s> (courtesan).' // 746 //

children.text: gṛhṇāsi yatpaṭānte mama paśyata eva Nanda Madirākhyām /
children.translated_text: 'The fact that you seize the edge of the garment of the one named <s>Madirā</s> right before my eyes, O <s>Nanda</s> —

children.text: ata āvayoravaśyaṃ mā vakṣyasi noktamantaraṃ bhavati // DKuṭṭ_747 //
children.translated_text: from this, do not say there will be no rift between us two, for it inevitably arises.' // 747 //
'This <s>Kuśakarṇa</s>, who has taken up a cushion, who holds a staff and wears ochre robes,
fearing contact with the world, having withdrawn apart, looking to both sides, // 748 //
performing the vow of silence, having produced in all a faith in his <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> devotion,
has resorted to the doctrine of <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu) under the pretext of visiting the temple of <s>Tripurāntaka</s> (<s>Śiva</s>); // 749 //
he gazes at women with artful longing, avoiding the sight of other people.'

children.text: Kumudini mama hṛdayagataṃ bhavitavyaṃ vyājaliṅginānena // DKuṭṭ_750 //
children.translated_text: "<s>Kumudinī</s>, what is in my heart must be — this one is embracing me falsely!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 750 //
"He watches when unseen; when observed, he gazes at another direction;

children.text: brūte kiṃ citsaspṛhamabhiyukto bhavati kīlitadhvānaḥ // DKuṭṭ_751 //
children.translated_text: he speaks something with longing when addressed, but his voice becomes choked." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 751 //

children.text: na jahāti samāsannaṃ notsahate sparśagocare sthātum /
children.translated_text: "He does not leave the vicinity, nor dares to remain within reach of touch;

children.text: eṣa manuṣyo manye niṣpratibhaḥ sābhilāṣaśca // DKuṭṭ_752 //
children.translated_text: this man, I think, is both abashed and full of desire." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 752 //

children.text: te 'tītāḥ khalu divasāḥ kriyate narma tvayā samaṃ yeṣu /
children.translated_text: "Those days are past indeed when you sported merrily together with him;
now you are an 'ācāryānī' (preceptor's wife) by virtue of your connection with a pure-conduct preceptor!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 753 //
"Wander as you please, seizing young women like tender shoots,
O <s>Lolikadāsa</s>, until you enter the snare of the queen!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 754 //
Filled with gallants and maidservants engaged in such manner of talk,
with the path cleared by an advance retinue skilled in attendance — such was the temple precinct. // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 755 //
Having completed the worship of <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), while the crowd was restrained by the stern staff-bearers,
<s>Samarabhaṭa</s> sat upon a seat swiftly placed by an appointed attendant. // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 756 //
Surrounded by a group of dancers, flautists, singers, and conspicuous young women seated in front,
with betel, flowers, and garments proffered by merchant-folk led by the chief merchant, // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 757 //
attended by various perfume-bearers, men carrying disk-weapons, swords, and maces,
with trusted guards behind him, swords drawn, and bodyguards — // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 758 //
a betel-box bearer, holding the prepared betel-leaf with tongs,
gently touching it with the left hand in the <s>khaṭakāmukha</s> gesture — // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 759 //
with the front part of his body leaning upon the minister and jesting companion stationed at his side,
he inquired about the well-being of the merchants, dancers, and others. // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 760 //
Then the bard, a steadfast man, when the hubbub of the crowd had been silenced, loudly
praised him thus, with a voice that was clear and resonant: // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 761 //
"Victory to the lord, destroyer of enemy forces, whose mind is fixed solely on serving the feet of his guru!
O thou seated on the hips of enemy women! O fierce web of rays dispelling the darkness of poverty!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 762 //
"O ornament of a lineage of warriors brave in battle! O thou bowing in worship of the great god of the earth!
O granter of fearlessness to those who seek refuge! O noonday sun to the lives of friendly kinsmen!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 763 //
"Such a fire of valor as yours, pervading the circles of the sky and the quarters —
is seen quenched only upon the forehead-ornaments of enemy women (i.e., in their tears)." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 764 //
"There is this clear distinction between ordinary fire and the fire of your valor:

children.text: aṅkurati tena dagdhaṃ dagdhasyānena nodbhavo bhūyaḥ // DKuṭṭ_765 //
children.translated_text: what is burned by that sprouts again; what is burned by this has no further rebirth." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 765 //
"Your band of adversaries — eating <s>śrīphala</s> fruits, wrapped in leaves, fond of strife, renouncing the pleasure of sacrificial sessions —

children.text: rājyasthitiṃ na muñcati hṛtalakṣmīko 'pi tava vipakṣagaṇaḥ // DKuṭṭ_766 //
children.translated_text: does not relinquish its claim to sovereignty, even though its <s>Lakṣmī</s> (fortune/beauty) has been seized." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 766 //

children.text: dadato vāñchitamarthaṃ sadānuraktasya tava gṛhaṃ tyaktvā /
children.translated_text: "Having left the house of you who always give the desired wealth and are ever devoted,
Fame — naked and attached — has gone to the quarters through the fickleness of a woman!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 767 //

children.text: bhavataḥ bhavato dhairyaṃ tena hi bhinno 'ndhakaḥ praṇataḥ /
children.translated_text: "Your firmness is such that <s>Andhaka</s> was split by it and bowed in submission;

children.text: muktāstvayā tu bahavo ripavo 'pi prekṣakāḥ samare // DKuṭṭ_768 //
children.translated_text: yet many enemies released by you have become mere spectators in battle." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 768 //
"Wandering over the entire earth, I have witnessed this wonder, O delight of the eyes:
that you, even being a giver of wealth, shun the company of the fierce!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 769 //
"This is another most wondrous thing — though plundered by thousands of young women,
the treasury of your charm only increases, never diminishes!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 770 //
"Another thing to marvel at: your whiteness (purity/fame) does not depart,
even when streaked by the blue-lotus-petal lustre of the eyes of beautiful women!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 771 //
"You, who alone dwell in the hearts of many women,

children.text: janaka kusumāstrapāṇeḥ puruṣottama tena viśvarūpo 'si // DKuṭṭ_772 //
children.translated_text: O father of the Flower-arrowed one (<s>Kāma</s>), O <s>Puruṣottama</s>, are therefore of universal form!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 772 //

children.text: kiṃ vahasi vṛthā garvaṃ priyo 'hamiti yoṣitāṃ narādhīśa /
children.translated_text: "Why do you bear pride in vain, saying 'I am the beloved of women,' O lord of men?
Sixteen thousand <s>Gopīs</s> yearned for <s>Murāri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>)!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 773 //

children.text: brāhmaṇyena yayāce makhasamaye yaḥ Baliṃ Hṛṣīkeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: "<s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), who at the time of sacrifice begged <s>Bali</s> through Brahminical guise —

children.text: na sa bhavati samo bhavatā dānaikaniṣaṇṇahṛdayena // DKuṭṭ_774 //
children.translated_text: he is not equal to you, whose heart is wholly devoted to giving!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 774 //
"Situated above the mountain-kings, relieving the heat of thirst of all living beings, with your loftiness —

children.text: tṛṣṇāsaṃtāpaharo megha iva kadā na dakṣastvam // DKuṭṭ_775 //
children.translated_text: when are you not capable, like a rain-cloud?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 775 //
"The flow of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>'s water — running in many channels, full of twists, given to bad courses, skilled at splitting banks —

children.text: Gaṅgājalapravāhaḥ puṇyadiśā kevalaṃ tava samānaḥ // DKuṭṭ_776 //
children.translated_text: is equal to you only in bestowing merit!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 776 //
"The birthplace of bad dealings, the origin of foolishness, the abode of indiscrimination —

children.text: ekastvaṃ doṣajñaḥ kṛtīkṛto yena kalikālaḥ // DKuṭṭ_777 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Kali</s> age has been made illustrious by you alone, who know its faults!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 777 //
"Though 'well-gone' (<s>Sugata</s>/Buddha), you are not averse to life; though bearing the bull-banner (<s>Śiva</s>), you are not yoked to sorrow;

children.text: udyataśastro 'pi ripau kathamasi sannāsiko jātaḥ // DKuṭṭ_778 //
children.translated_text: though you raise your weapon against the enemy, how is it that you are 'noseless' (i.e., lacking in pride)?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 778 //
"A precious jewel, of many enjoyments, bearing great burdens, the abode of steadfast soul —
O lord of men, it is wondrous that you are embraced by all good qualities!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 779 //
"<s>Piṅgala</s>, by whom a person light by nature was raised to gravity from the lowest station,

children.text: jaghanacapalā tathāryā sa Piṅgalaste kathaṃ tulyaḥ // DKuṭṭ_780 //
children.translated_text: yet who was herself fickle-hipped and noble — how can he compare to you?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 780 //

children.text: yasya na jātirnātmā nārthajñānaṃ na mānase praśamaḥ /
children.translated_text: "He for whom there is no caste, no self, no knowledge of wealth, no tranquility of mind —

children.text: bhavasi bhavasāra na tvaṃ tenādvayavādināsadṛśaḥ // DKuṭṭ_781 //
children.translated_text: O essence of existence, you are therefore not comparable to the Advaitin (non-dualist)!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 781 //
"In that too there is growth; in him too is the fame of manly virtues;
in that too are technical terms — therefore you do not surpass grammar!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 782 //
"Even when praised without flattery, even when free from reproach, even when beyond comparison —
O lord, with your true dramatic type, class, and qualities, you adorn the earth!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 783 //

children.text: anyaiva varṇanaiṣā bhavatsu lokottarā sthitā kāpi /
children.translated_text: "This description of your kind is something other, something extraordinary established in the world;

children.text: vāmo yathaiva śatruṣu mitreṣu tathaiva vāmo 'si // DKuṭṭ_784 //
children.translated_text: just as you are 'crooked' (formidable) toward enemies, so too you are 'crooked' (gracious) toward friends!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 784 //
"By that with which you honor elders, by that with which you celebrate virtuous deeds,

children.text: prīṇayasi yena viprānnṛpanandana tena vṛṣalastvam // DKuṭṭ_785 //
children.translated_text: by that with which you please <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> — by that, O prince, you are a <s>Vṛṣala</s> (a bull among men)!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 785 //

children.text: dainyamidaṃ yacchlāghā kriyate tava rakṣasāpi na samasya /
children.translated_text: "It is a pity that praise is offered to you as an equal of even that <s>Rākṣasa</s> (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>);

children.text: na sa haṭhamakarodyoṣiti bhavāṃstu bhuṅkte prasahya ripulakṣmīm // DKuṭṭ_786 //
children.translated_text: he did not take 'women' (<s>Sītā</s>) by force, whereas you enjoy the fortune of enemies by force!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 786 //
"This praise of charming flattering words, which is the source of our livelihood,

children.text: tatpatati te svarūpe yāmi namaḥ santu saukhyāni // DKuṭṭ_787 //
children.translated_text: falls upon your true nature! I depart — salutations — may there be pleasures!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 787 //
Hearing this, he afterwards spoke, commending the panegyrist with applause:

children.text: āssva kimākulatā te yāsyasi tuṣṭo mayā prahitaḥ // DKuṭṭ_788 //
children.translated_text: "Sit down — what is your anxiety? You shall go away pleased, sent by me." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 788 //

children.text: punarapi paṭha tadyugalaṃ gītikayoryattvayā purā paṭhitam /
children.translated_text: "Recite once more that pair of songs which you recited before,
while I stood screened behind a partition at the house of the well-born girl." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 789 //
"When you recite, this speech is unsealed in the assembly of the learned" —
having said this, he recited with a voice pure in the three registers: // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 790 //
"One woman is angry from a lover's quarrel; another is listless from the frustration of broken affection;
yet another, not having obtained a seat close enough, harbors weariness in her heart." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 791 //
"Another is separated by a quarrel; another is inhibited by the shyness of a new marriage;

children.text: ramaṇīgaṇamadhyagataḥ smarāturaḥ kiṃ karotu bahujāniḥ // DKuṭṭ_792 //
children.translated_text: in the midst of this group of women, what is the love-afflicted man of many wives to do?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 792 //
Then, making a nod of the head signaling comprehension, with raised eyebrows,
he addressed the dance-master: 'What good music is there in this (performance)?' // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 793 //

children.text: sa uvāca tato vaṇijo netāro yatra yatra pātrāṇi /
children.translated_text: He replied: 'Wherever merchants are the patrons of the performers,

children.text: śāṭhyāyatanaṃ dāsyastatra kutaḥ sauṣṭhavaṃ nāṭye // DKuṭṭ_794 //
children.translated_text: and slave-girls the abode of deceit — whence can there be elegance in dramatic art?' // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 794 //

children.text: kā cidbalinākrāntā kā cinna jahāti kāminaṃ ruciram /
children.translated_text: One girl is overpowered by a strong man; another does not leave her charming lover;

children.text: anyā pānakagoṣṭhyāṃ nayati dinaṃ prītakaiḥ sārdham // DKuṭṭ_795 //
children.translated_text: yet another spends the day in a drinking party with her lovers. // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 795 //
One constantly does not leave the doorway of the house, hoping for a man's arrival;
a bribed gateman tells another, who is menstruating, (that she is unavailable). // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 796 //

children.text: raṅgagatāpi kṣudrā śṛṇoti yadi paricitaṃ gṛhāyātam /
children.translated_text: A base girl, even when at the theatre, if she hears that a familiar patron has come to her house,

children.text: uddiśya vārikāryaṃ vrajati tataḥ prakṛtamutsṛjya // DKuṭṭ_797 //
children.translated_text: citing a need for water, leaves the performance and goes. // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 797 //
"She whose gaze has been trained on her beloved from the very onset of youth —

children.text: sāmājikamadhyasthā sā kathamanyāsu yāti parabhāgam // DKuṭṭ_798 //
children.translated_text: how does she, standing amid the audience, yield precedence to other women?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 798 //

children.text: cetovaśitā sattvaṃ sattve sati cārutā prayogasya /
children.translated_text: "Mastery over the mind is <s>sattva</s> (innate talent); when <s>sattva</s> is present, there is beauty of performance;

children.text: na bhavati sā veśyānāṃ madyāmiṣapuruṣanihitahṛdayānām // DKuṭṭ_799 //
children.translated_text: but that is not found in courtesans whose hearts are fixed on liquor, meat, and men." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 799 //
"We too, having no alternative, have taken refuge in this temple
now that <s>Anaṅgaharṣa</s> has gone to the world of the gods, occupying the sacred site." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 800 //

children.text: iha tu kadā citkiṃ cidvṛttinirodhābhiśaṅkayā nirutsāhāḥ /
children.translated_text: "But here, sometimes somewhat discouraged by the fear of livelihood being obstructed,
these women of <s>Ratnāvalī</s>'s (troupe) perform their hand-and-foot movements." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 801 //
"This one performs the role of the King of <s>Vatsa</s> (<s>Udayana</s>); that one imitates the king's companion;
this one parodies the staging of the story of <s>Vāsavadattā</s>." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 802 //
"Through effort, literary skill, extraordinary beauty, and sustained passion,
this one has gained fame in the imitation of the <s>Siṃhala</s> king's daughter." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 803 //
"The varied arrangement of postures (<s>sthānaka</s>), the movement, the grace of bodily undulation,
the emotional inflection of speech, the nourishment of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment), the firmness of disposition," // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 804 //
"the unfolding of <s>sāttvika</s> (involuntary psychophysical) states, acting that is adorned with appropriate behavior,

children.text: miśrāmiśre vādye layācyutiṃ varṇayanti Mañjaryāḥ // DKuṭṭ_805 //
children.translated_text: the beat-deviation in mixed and unmixed musical accompaniment — all these they describe as <s>Mañjarī</s>'s." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 805 //
"She, whose awareness of the Flower-arrowed one (<s>Kāma</s>) along with his body has been destroyed by the mere utterance of his name,
with a glance that suddenly manifests the state of aroused love, through a gap in the <s>sinduvāra</s> (vitex) hedge —" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 806 //
"watching the King of <s>Vatsa</s>, concealing the distinction between the model and the imitation,
she produces 'Bravo!' cries in the mouths of the audience-members' minds." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 807 //
"While painting the lord of <s>Vatsa</s>, gradually entering into the state of <s>Kāma</s>,
she makes her hand tremble uncontrollably with shivering, goosebumps, and perspiration." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 808 //
"With a similar set of <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequent physical expressions), she shows the <s>karuṇa rasa</s> (pathetic sentiment) as distinct from <s>vipralambha</s> (love in separation),
unsolicited, when she arrives at the point of attempted suicide." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 809 //
While the dance-master was thus describing <s>Mañjarikā</s>, the prince, gazing at her with longing,
touched her with his staff, asking 'Who is she?' // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 810 //
Then, understanding the prince's inclination, extending the playful conversation about the young woman,
while disparaging courtesans, the minister praised the benefits of association with a <s>bandhakī</s> (concubine). // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 811 //
"Love with a wife is for progeny; the embrace of a slave-girl is for curing illness;

children.text: tatkhalu surataṃ surataṃ kṛcchraprāpyaṃ yadanyanārīṣu // DKuṭṭ_812 //
children.translated_text: but that is truly <s>surata</s> (love-making) which is obtained with difficulty from other women." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 812 //

children.text: svavyāpāraikamateḥ paracintā nāsti me kadā cidapi /
children.translated_text: "I, being intent solely on my own affairs, have never had concern for others' matters;

children.text: paśyantyāstvāmīdṛśamadya tu me mānasaṃ vyathitam // DKuṭṭ_813 //
children.translated_text: but seeing you thus today, my heart is pained." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 813 //

children.text: yadi vedmi tasya vasatiṃ sāmarthyaṃ yadi bhavettato 'bhyadhikam /
children.translated_text: "If I knew his dwelling-place, and if my power were even greater,
I would go and crush that accursed fate to powder with clubs!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 814 //
"If this incomparable body of yours was fashioned thus by the wretched Creator, O slender girl,
why was the fruit of your birth made barren by the absence of a suitable lover?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 815 //

children.text: śaiśavamastu jarā vā vyādhirvā kṣetriyaḥ praṇāśo vā /
children.translated_text: "Let there be childhood, or old age, or disease, or hereditary illness, or destruction;

children.text: svākāraṃ tāruṇyaṃ na tu kupatikadarthanāgrastam // DKuṭṭ_816 //
children.translated_text: but one's own beautiful youth should not be swallowed up by a wretched husband's contempt!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 816 //

children.text: keliḥ pradahati majjāṃ śṛṅgāro 'sthīni cāṭavaḥ kaṭukāḥ /
children.translated_text: "His love-play burns the marrow, his romantic gestures pierce the bones, his sweet words are bitter;

children.text: na karoti manastuṣṭiṃ dānamabhavyasya gṛhabhartuḥ // DKuṭṭ_817 //
children.translated_text: the gift of an unworthy householder does not produce satisfaction in the heart." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 817 //
"'Where have you come from? Where did you stay for so long? For what purpose?' —
asking thus with an uneasy mind, the householder produces a headache." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 818 //
If by fate's arrangement a radiant youth comes within the range of sight,

children.text: tatrātmānaṃ kṣapayati jāyāṃ ca raṭan gṛhasvāmī // DKuṭṭ_819 //
children.translated_text: the husband wastes himself there, lamenting over his wife. [DKuṭṭ 819]
With the afterlife in dispute, with people's censure in this variegated world,

children.text: daivādhīne pralaye na vidagdhā hārayanti tāruṇyam // DKuṭṭ_820 //
children.translated_text: with dissolution dependent on fate, clever women do not let their youth go to waste. [DKuṭṭ 820]
O woman with beautiful breasts, your pair of bosoms, whose splendor is daily sullied by the slapping of a bad husband's hands,

children.text: tuṅgamapi patitakalpaṃ stanaśālini tava payodharadvandvam // DKuṭṭ_821 //
children.translated_text: though lofty, is rendered almost fallen. [DKuṭṭ 821]
A couch with fine coverings, an agreeable husband, a charming dwelling—
these do not equal even a fraction of stolen lovemaking in a hasty moment. [DKuṭṭ 822]
Suddenly, in a narrow path, by one who has come face-to-face unexpectedly, by the desired one,
what is obtained through a passionate encounter is the fruit of no small good <s>karma</s>. [DKuṭṭ 823]
Unsurpassed pleasure, they say, is what thinkers of the afterlife have called heaven;
may the attainment of that birth come from union with the man desired by one's heart. [DKuṭṭ 824]
Those who are determined to grasp the sweet fruit from an inaccessible precipice—

children.text: te śokakleśarujāṃ kevalamupayānti pātratāṃ mandāḥ // DKuṭṭ_825 //
children.translated_text: only the dull ones among them attain nothing but eligibility for grief, suffering, and pain. [DKuṭṭ 825]
Is the course of the planets unfavorable, or has the bad conduct of another birth ripened,
or is it the habitual practice of that wretch who is self-destroyed? [DKuṭṭ 826]

children.text: yena tapasvī sa yuvā stauti samīraṃ tvadaṅgasaṃspṛṣṭam /
children.translated_text: That wretched youth praises the wind that has touched your body,

children.text: tvatpādākrāntabhuve spṛhayati kakubhaṃ tvadāśritāṃ namati // DKuṭṭ_827 //
children.translated_text: he longs for the ground trodden by your feet, he bows to the quarter of the sky that shelters you. [DKuṭṭ 827]
He meditates upon your form, he recites a garland of syllables forming your name,
with mind made one-pointed, longing for the attainment of the bliss of union with you. [DKuṭṭ 828]
Having abandoned all his affairs, gazing at you with neck turned sideways,
he makes the street before your house into a path of a hundred turnings by his comings and goings. [DKuṭṭ 829]
You have been seen by her for a long time, wandering near her house with longing;

children.text: saṃdeśa eṣa dattaḥ prābhṛtametattava prahitam // DKuṭṭ_830 //
children.translated_text: this message has been given, this gift has been sent to you. [DKuṭṭ 830]
She withers away, watching for an opportunity to leave the house, on your account—
thus is he robbed by clever, deceitful women using you as a pretext. [DKuṭṭ 831]
But what use are further words to one whose mind is seized by groundless delusion?

children.text: anutiṣṭha yathāyuktaṃ tvatto nāśaśca jīvarakṣā ca // DKuṭṭ_832 //
children.translated_text: Act as is fitting—from you come both his destruction and the saving of his life. [DKuṭṭ 832]
Fall from family honor, public censure, passage to hell, uncertainty of survival—
a helpless woman accepts all these in an instant when she goes to another man. [DKuṭṭ 833]

children.text: sa tu likhati dāsapatraṃ tyajati kuṭumbaṃ dadāti sarvasvam /
children.translated_text: But he writes a deed of servitude, abandons his family, gives away all his possessions,

children.text: yāvanna bhavati purataḥ parayuvatiḥ projjhitāvaraṇā // DKuṭṭ_834 //
children.translated_text: until the other man's wife appears before him with her veil cast off. [DKuṭṭ 834]
'What was to be seen has been seen, curiosity has departed, the secret is known'—

children.text: iti yāti manasi kṛtvā vihitavidheyastatastūrṇam // DKuṭṭ_835 //
children.translated_text: thinking thus in his mind, he who has accomplished his purpose then leaves quickly. [DKuṭṭ 835]
And she, cut off, released from the grip of anxiety, looking in all directions,

children.text: viśati gṛhaṃ saṃtrastā sarvata āśaṅkitā savailakṣyā // DKuṭṭ_836 //
children.translated_text: enters the house, frightened, suspicious of everything, embarrassed. [DKuṭṭ 836]
Being new to this fallen conduct and not skilled in the well-composed answers of an experienced adulteress,

children.text: pṛṣṭā kva gatāsi tvaṃ na kva ciditi sambhramād brūte // DKuṭṭ_837 //
children.translated_text: when asked 'Where did you go?', she says in confusion 'Nowhere.' [DKuṭṭ 837]

children.text: ete doṣā bahavaḥ puruṣā api capalakautukāḥ prāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: These faults are many, and men too are mostly of fickle curiosity;

children.text: tvaṃ ca graheṇa lagnā kāryavimūḍhātra tiṣṭhāmi // DKuṭṭ_838 //
children.translated_text: and you are caught by a planet's influence, deluded about what to do—here I stand helpless. [DKuṭṭ 838]
Thus with her heart swinging like a pendulum, steadied by the <s>dūtī</s> (go-between) who is practiced in her craft,

children.text: dṛṣṭeti śaṅkamānā pade pade calati parṇe 'pi // DKuṭṭ_839 //
children.translated_text: suspecting that she has been seen, she trembles at every step, even at a falling leaf. [DKuṭṭ 839]
Casting her eyes everywhere, her startled, trembling gaze darting again and again,
she reaches the place of assignation, drawn by desires multiplied a hundredfold. [DKuṭṭ 840]
Producing a flood of <s>anubhāvas</s> (involuntary expressions) mixed with fear, passion, and modesty,
with breasts, navel, and limbs now seen, now hidden by her shifting garment— [DKuṭṭ 841]

children.text: nīvīślathanārambhaṃ nirundhatī na na na yāmi yāmīti /
children.translated_text: Resisting the beginning of the loosening of her girdle-knot, saying 'No, no, no, I won't go—I'll go,'
she elaborates the repertoire of <s>Smara</s> (the god of love) with her hushed, indistinct utterances. [DKuṭṭ 842]
She seems to lead him into inner dissolution, swallowing all his limbs as she embraces him;

children.text: yaṃ śliṣyate 'nyayoṣā tiktaṃ tasyāmṛtaṃ purataḥ // DKuṭṭ_843 //
children.translated_text: for the man whom another woman embraces, what was bitter becomes nectar in her presence. [DKuṭṭ 843]

children.text: na kṛtaṃ tava rahasi puro bāṣpāvṛtakaṇṭhakuṇṭhayā vācā /
children.translated_text: 'You did not perform in secret before me, with a voice choked and stammering with tears held back,
the release of the flood of grief caused by the husband's contempt.' [DKuṭṭ 844]
'Making pillows of each other's arms, without any apprehension, by us two,

children.text: saṃvalitoru na suptaṃ śithilāṅgaṃ rativimardakhinnābhyām // DKuṭṭ_845 //
children.translated_text: with thighs intertwined, we did not sleep with limbs relaxed, exhausted by the exertion of love.' [DKuṭṭ 845]
'Delicious food brought secretly from my own house, in a private place,

children.text: svakareṇa mayā dattaṃ nirvṛtahṛdayena nāśitaṃ bhavatā // DKuṭṭ_846 //
children.translated_text: was given by my own hand and eaten by you with a contented heart.' [DKuṭṭ 846]

children.text: na kṛtā caritrarakṣā na ca bhuktaṃ tvaccharīramapayantram /
children.translated_text: 'No care was taken to protect my reputation, nor was your body enjoyed as an instrument of pleasure;

children.text: dṛṣṭādṛṣṭabhraṣṭā kva yāmi kiṃ vā karomi durjātā // DKuṭṭ_847 //
children.translated_text: ruined in this world and the next—where shall I go, what shall I do, wretched as I am?' [DKuṭṭ 847]
'The delight in wearing the veil modestly, free and leisurely conversation, gentle and slow movements—

children.text: samprati mama pāpāyāḥ karapihitamukhā hasanti bhūmijñāḥ // DKuṭṭ_848 //
children.translated_text: now the worldly-wise women laugh at me, the sinful one, covering their mouths with their hands.' [DKuṭṭ 848]
'Those women of equal age and family who were my friends—

children.text: tā vārayanti mattaḥ kusaṅga iti tanniyantāraḥ // DKuṭṭ_849 //
children.translated_text: they now keep their kin away from me, saying "She is bad company."' [DKuṭṭ 849]
'Enduring the reproaches from my household servants, my face suppressing anger,
I stand without pride, due to the weakness born of faults I myself created.' [DKuṭṭ 850]
'When good people incidentally recite praises of faithful wives,

children.text: hṛdayena dūyamānā mūḍhā sīdāmi śṛṇvantī // DKuṭṭ_851 //
children.translated_text: I, the foolish one, sink down with a burning heart as I listen.' [DKuṭṭ 851]
'When I sit down nearby, unable to forbid me with averted glances,
my kinswomen shrink from one another while eating, exchanging looks among themselves.' [DKuṭṭ 852]
'I was exposed by you yourself, who for even a moment would not leave the vicinity of my house,
and would not withdraw your gaze, sunk in love-softened tenderness, from us.' [DKuṭṭ 853]
'Betraying the ruin of another's household, vain in thinking themselves handsome, arrogant from their good looks,
men of your kind have passion like a chameleon's.' [DKuṭṭ 854]
With syllables pained by grief arising from an unwanted situation, thus,

children.text: sopālambhā vijane dhanyāḥ śṛṇvanti bandhakīvācaḥ // DKuṭṭ_855 //
children.translated_text: with reproaches, in private, the fortunate ones hear the words of the <s>bandhakī</s> (kept woman). [DKuṭṭ 855]
For one whose gaze has been captured, with eyes offered in genuine affection to another young woman,
the artful displays arranged by a <s>veśyā</s> (courtesan) are recounted before him as equal to old straw. [DKuṭṭ 856]
To those whose particular deities have been propitiated, a great festival of <s>rati</s> (love) approaches;

children.text: vacanamapi premārdraṃ svairiṇyāḥ śravaṇameti puṇyavatām // DKuṭṭ_857 //
children.translated_text: even the love-softened words of a <s>svairiṇī</s> (independent woman) reach the ears of the meritorious. [DKuṭṭ 857]

children.text: kā gaṇanā viṣayarate puṃsi varāke parāṅganā spṛhayā /
children.translated_text: What account is to be made of a wretched man addicted to sensual pleasures? A married woman, with longing,

children.text: vyājena vīkṣamāṇā dhyānadhiyāṃ spṛśati majjānam // DKuṭṭ_858 //
children.translated_text: gazing at him under some pretext, touches the very marrow of the meditative-minded. [DKuṭṭ 858]

children.text: śirasā racitāñjalayo dadhati nideśaṃ triviṣṭape gaṇikāḥ /
children.translated_text: In heaven, <s>gaṇikās</s> (courtesans) stand with joined palms raised above their heads, carrying out orders;
yet <s>Indra</s>, lord of <s>Śacī</s>, drawn by the taste of another's wife, took <s>Ahalyā</s>. [DKuṭṭ 859]

children.text: apsarasaḥ kiṃ na vaśā vaidagdhyavatāṃ ca kiṃ na dhaureyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Were not the <s>Apsarases</s> at his command? And were there not champions among the accomplished?
Yet <s>Govinda</s> (Kṛṣṇa) developed attachment to the wives of the cowherds. [DKuṭṭ 860]
Courtesans of all three worlds were at the disposal of the lord of the <s>Rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: tadapi jahāra kalatraṃ daśarathatanayasya Rāmasya // DKuṭṭ_861 //
children.translated_text: yet he carried off the wife of <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>. [DKuṭṭ 861]
Then <s>Mañjarī</s>'s mother, mustering enthusiasm to argue for her own side,
began to refute the speech favoring the prince's minister. [DKuṭṭ 862]
'Bold with village women, your manhood destroyed by never seeing sophisticated city women,
a village-dweller, unsophisticated—one like you inevitably disparages the <s>gaṇikā</s> (courtesan). [DKuṭṭ 863]
The lovemaking of a <s>bandhakī</s> (kept woman) whose husband is still living, devoid of nail and tooth marks,
does not moisten the hearts of men who have immersed themselves in the treatises of <s>Kāmadeva</s>. [DKuṭṭ 864]

children.text: sthāpaya ghaṭakaṃ tāvatkuru bhūmitale tṛṇaiḥ samāstaraṇam /
children.translated_text: Set aside the water pot, spread straw on the ground for bedding—
such is generally the prelude to lovemaking for village youth couples. [DKuṭṭ 865]
Smeared thickly with <s>uśīra</s> (vetiver) paste, wearing a matted topknot and a wilted <s>mallikā</s> (jasmine) garland,

children.text: pāmaranāryā dṛṣṭaḥ smaro 'hamiti manyate viṭo grāmyaḥ // DKuṭṭ_866 //
children.translated_text: a vulgar village gallant thinks himself <s>Smara</s> (the god of love) when seen by a common woman. [DKuṭṭ 866]
Sweating from the exertion of household work, having gone out on an errand to fetch water,

children.text: upapatirupaiti harṣaṃ niśāgame pāmarīṃ prāpya // DKuṭṭ_867 //
children.translated_text: the paramour is delighted at nightfall upon obtaining this common woman. [DKuṭṭ 867]
When a woman who has lowered a pot into a well, with her foot placed on a wooden plank,
glances with her neck turned—that uplifts the spirit of the young man. [DKuṭṭ 868]

children.text: lagno 'si yatra gātre kathamapi daivena devayātrāyām /
children.translated_text: 'That spot on her body where you happened to touch by fate during a temple festival—

children.text: adyāpi tanna muñcati pulakodgamakaṇṭakaṃ tasyāḥ // DKuṭṭ_869 //
children.translated_text: even today the goosebumps have not left that place on her skin.' [DKuṭṭ 869]
'When she entered the deserted thicket-garden to pick cotton,

children.text: khaṅkāritena saṃjñā kṛtā tayā tvaṃ tu vetsi no mūrkhaḥ // DKuṭṭ_870 //
children.translated_text: she made a signal by coughing—but you, fool, did not understand.' [DKuṭṭ 870]
'That woman, whose gaze was fixed only on you while she embraced a pestle,

children.text: āvṛttyā bhramati puro jātaḥ khalu śālikhaṇḍane vighnaḥ // DKuṭṭ_871 //
children.translated_text: has been going back and forth before you—surely an obstacle has arisen in the rice field!' [DKuṭṭ 871]
'She watched you throwing <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple) fruits, with your skill praised by bystanders,
abandoning her household duties, peeping through the crack in the door.' [DKuṭṭ 872]
'When you were passing near the road, O handsome one, she, without discerning her own fatigue,

children.text: pratyāsannagṛheṣvapi kṛtaḥ prasahya smarāturo lokaḥ // DKuṭṭ_873 //
children.translated_text: forcibly created love-sickness in the people of even the neighboring houses.' [DKuṭṭ 873]
Thus, of the village fool whose pride in his good fortune has been inflated by the words of the clever <s>dūtī</s> (go-between),
the mind becomes agitated with a thousand waves of emotion. [DKuṭṭ 874]
Restraining that one whose speech had blossomed forth, with a bow of his head,

children.text: śrīsiṃhabhaṭasya sutaṃ samuvāca vaco 'tha nartakācāryaḥ // DKuṭṭ_875 //
children.translated_text: the <s>nartakācārya</s> (dancing master) then addressed the son of <s>Śrī Siṃhabhaṭa</s>. [DKuṭṭ 875]
'In the domain of the <s>nāyaka</s> (hero), <s>Bharata</s> is the authority; the <s>kuśīlavas</s> (performers) include sages like <s>Kohala</s> and others;
in women's dramatic art, the <s>Apsarases</s>; in <s>Gāndharva</s> (music), the son of the Lotus-born (<s>Brahmā</s>). [DKuṭṭ 876]
The sage <s>Mataṅga</s> is learned in the application of wind instruments and vocal techniques;

children.text: yadi rañjayanti hṛdayaṃ bhavato bhūmispṛśāṃ kutaḥ śaktiḥ // DKuṭṭ_877 //
children.translated_text: if these delight your heart, what capacity have mere mortals? [DKuṭṭ 877]

children.text: abhyadhikaṃ dhṛṣṭatvaṃ prāyeṇa hi śilpajīvināṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: Generally, excessive boldness is found among those who live by their craft,
and especially in one who has adopted the profession of a dancer and has conquered the stage. [DKuṭṭ 878]
Therefore I petition you: just as <s>Prajāpati</s> (the Creator) fashioned <s>Nāṭya</s> (drama),

children.text: avalokayāṅkamekaṃ mā bhavatu mama śramo vandhyaḥ // DKuṭṭ_879 //
children.translated_text: watch one act—let not my labor be in vain.' [DKuṭṭ 879]

children.text: iti kathayannarabhartuḥ putreṇa sa codito bhruvonnatayā /
children.translated_text: Thus speaking, urged by a raise of the eyebrow from the king's son,
with all the instruments assembled, he set the <s>sūtradhāra</s> (stage manager) into action. [DKuṭṭ 880]
With the position given by the flutist, having properly taken up the distinct fifth note,
during the interval of the <s>dvipadī</s> (two-line verse) recitation, the <s>sūtradhāra</s> entered with the <s>prāveśikī dhruvā</s> (entrance song). [DKuṭṭ 881]
Endowed with the <s>rasa</s> (sentiment) of <s>utsāha</s> (heroic energy), delighting the hearts of the audience,
through the mastery and skill of the poet's composition concerning the deeds of the lord— [DKuṭṭ 882]
Having circled through the <s>dhruvā</s> (song) measured in eight <s>kalās</s> (beats), set to proper <s>tāla</s> (rhythm) and <s>laya</s> (tempo),

children.text: āhūya naṭīṃ kṛtvā tayā samaṃ svagṛhakāryasaṃlāpam // DKuṭṭ_883 //
children.translated_text: having called the <s>naṭī</s> (actress) and conducted with her the domestic dialogue— [DKuṭṭ 883]
Having indicated the arrival of a character, performing some graceful steps,
he exited along with the <s>gṛhiṇī</s> (wife/female lead) to the accompaniment of the exit song. [DKuṭṭ 884]
Then, following the <s>kathodghāta</s> (opening of the story), the minister entered with wonder,
and delighted by the bringing together of unlikely elements and by the rise of the king. [DKuṭṭ 885]
Indicating <s>Vatsanātha</s> (the lord of <s>Vatsa</s>) ascending the palace to watch the spring festival dance of <s>Kusumāyudha</s> (Kāmadeva),
he exited to accomplish the immediately following task. [DKuṭṭ 886]

children.text: atha viśati sma narendraḥ prāsādagataḥ samaṃ vayasyena /
children.translated_text: Then the king, having ascended the palace, entered together with his companion,
observing the festivities with a delighted heart, on account of his own prosperity and happiness. // DKuṭṭ_887 //
Drawn by a feeling of wonder, casting wide-open eyes

children.text: nṛtyati paurajanaughe provāca vayasya paśya paśyeti // DKuṭṭ_888 //
children.translated_text: upon the throng of townspeople dancing, he said to his companion: 'Look, look!' // DKuṭṭ_888 //
Children, youths, and elders all alike, with the movements of both sheltered and unsheltered young women,
heedless of what is proper or improper to say — the populace sports about, the flow of their delight swelling. // DKuṭṭ_889 //
Yellowed with ground flour, having constructed extravagant garlands of various flowers,
their songs at each step scattered by the many deep breaths arising from physical exertion, // DKuṭṭ_890 //
with arms raised, dancing vigorously to the sound of hand-clapping mingled with the noise of musical instruments,
stumbling now and again yet displaying firmness and grace — [such was] the elder. // DKuṭṭ_891 //
'May spring endure forever, with the embrace of one's beloved always within one's power!' —
singing thus, a young woman impetuously embraces [her beloved], overcome by passion. // DKuṭṭ_892 //
While she plays, struck by water from a syringe without any [hostile] intent,
a young man — the wicked soul — considers himself fortunate because of the married woman. // DKuṭṭ_893 //
When the dam of modesty is broken on the occasion of the festival, from the mouth of a respectable woman,

children.text: aślīloktijalaughe niryāte kena vāryate prasaraḥ // DKuṭṭ_894 //
children.translated_text: when the flood of indecent words has poured forth — who can stop its flow? // DKuṭṭ_894 //
Among women engaged in gambling, whose speech carries the same activities,
the face-veil serves to conceal whether they are noble or ignoble. // DKuṭṭ_895 //
Then, at the place indicated by the companion, with gestures disrupted by steps faltering from intoxication,
the two servant-girls, sent by <s>Vāsavadattā</s>, entered dancing. // DKuṭṭ_896 //
Performing a gesture that merely suggested the turning of a lotus, when the arrow [scene] was to be enacted,
they enacted it with heroic glances, relying on the weapon alone. // DKuṭṭ_897 //
The king, his mind captivated by curiosity, following the movement of their glances,
declared: 'Wonderful indeed — the playful performance of these two graceful women!' // DKuṭṭ_898 //
'In the contest of crushing, pressing, and intermingling of hands, though I am being pushed aside,

children.text: stanamaṇḍale sthito 'haṃ tvaṃ punarākṛṣya kutra citkṣiptaḥ // DKuṭṭ_899 //
children.translated_text: I remain fixed on the breast-region — while you have been pulled away and cast elsewhere.' // DKuṭṭ_899 //
'Now you obstruct me!' — as if in anger, the charming pearl necklace,
leaping up, strikes the one who dances with many picturesque footsteps. // DKuṭṭ_900 //
The mango vine held splendidly the crest-jewel that had fallen from its place in the coiffure,

children.text: adhṛta patanniryūhāṃ na tveṣā madanikā veṇīm // DKuṭṭ_901 //
children.translated_text: but this dancing girl did not [hold] the braid whose garlands were falling unsupported. // DKuṭṭ_901 //
'You have no concern for the slender waist, bowed by the weight of the breasts' —

children.text: itthamiva pādalagnau krīḍantyā nūpurau rasataḥ // DKuṭṭ_902 //
children.translated_text: thus, as it were, the anklets attached to her feet jingle as she plays. // DKuṭṭ_902 //

children.text: vahati sma yaṃ nitambaṃ kathamapi kṛcchreṇa mandasaṃcārā /
children.translated_text: The hip that she bore somehow, with difficulty, moving slowly —

children.text: kalayati taṃ tūlalaghuṃ jayati manojanmano mahimā // DKuṭṭ_903 //
children.translated_text: she makes it seem light as cotton; the glory of <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love) triumphs! // DKuṭṭ_903 //
With <s>Udayana</s>'s permission, <s>Vasantaka</s> too dances with a joyful spirit
in their midst, with a comic <s>carcaritāla</s> (clapping rhythm), charming with humor and modesty. // DKuṭṭ_904 //
After those two had performed for a long time with steps that were bold, agitated, and graceful, approaching the king,
they delivered a message from the daughter of <s>Pradyota</s>. // DKuṭṭ_905 //
'The queen commands, my lord —' but having said only half, they bashfully

children.text: avalokya mukhaṃ na hi na hi vijñāpayati praṇamya vinayena // DKuṭṭ_906 //
children.translated_text: looked at each other's faces, and 'No, no!' — they conveyed their message with a bow, respectfully. // DKuṭṭ_906 //
'To perform the worship of <s>Makaradhvaja</s> (Kāma, the Love-god) in the presence of your lotus-feet,
O ornament of the earth's surface — such is the inclination of my mind.' // DKuṭṭ_907 //

children.text: priyaratibhogo madano dayitavasanto janasya manasi vasan /
children.translated_text: '<s>Madana</s> (Love), whose enjoyment is the delight of the beloved, whose dear [companion] is spring, dwelling in the hearts of people —

children.text: bhāvena bhavān pūjyo lokasthityā tu kusumaśarapāṇiḥ // DKuṭṭ_908 //
children.translated_text: he is worshipped in spirit as you, my lord; but for the sake of worldly convention, it is the bow-armed god of flowers.' // DKuṭṭ_908 //
Having delivered the message, and having wandered about in a manner fitting their nature, age, and the occasion,
those two, possessed by intoxication and love, disappeared behind the curtain. // DKuṭṭ_909 //
Then, when the curtain was removed, the princess appeared together with the servant-girls,
followed by attendants bearing in their hands the articles suitable for worship, the jeweled necklace unnoticed. // DKuṭṭ_910 //

children.text: atha dṛṣṭvā sāgarikāṃ pramāditāṃ parijanasya ninditvā /
children.translated_text: Then, seeing <s>Sāgarikā</s> distracted, the chief queen, having rebuked the attendants and grown agitated,
addressed <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>: // DKuṭṭ_911 //
'Send this girl away to the inner apartments; you take the flowers and other offerings,
before she comes within the range of the king's sight.' // DKuṭṭ_912 //
Approaching then, the servant-girl said to her: 'You — for what purpose have you come?

children.text: medhāvinīṃ vimucya vraja tasminmā vilambasva // DKuṭṭ_913 //
children.translated_text: Release <s>Medhāvinī</s> and go. Do not delay there.' // DKuṭṭ_913 //

children.text: vihite devyādeśe manasīdaṃ sannidhāya sā tasthau /
children.translated_text: When the queen's command had been carried out, keeping this in her mind, she stood still —

children.text: vihagī Susaṅgatāyā haste nihitā manobhavasaparyām // DKuṭṭ_914 //
children.translated_text: the bird placed in the hand of <s>Susaṅgatā</s> for the worship of <s>Manobhava</s> (Love). // DKuṭṭ_914 //
'Let me watch, concealed behind a <s>sinduvāra</s> (vitex) bush,

children.text: tātāntaḥpurikābhiryathārcyate kiṃ tatheha no veti // DKuṭṭ_915 //
children.translated_text: whether father's harem women worship [the god] here in the same manner [as elsewhere] or not.' // DKuṭṭ_915 //
Approaching King <s>Vatsa</s>, who seemed like passion condensed, like heart's desire that had attained the excellence of embodied form,

children.text: samupetya Vatsarājaṃ jagāda sā jayatu deva iti // DKuṭṭ_916 //
children.translated_text: she said: 'Victory to the lord!' // DKuṭṭ_916 //
Though already enjoyed, the romantic sentiment had been renewed by the festival of <s>Madana</s> (Love);
he, returning her affection as she showed hers, having welcomed her with words of greeting, said: // DKuṭṭ_917 //
'I think <s>Manobhava</s> (Kāma) shall suffer a torment
greater than the burning by the fire of <s>Śarva</s>'s (Śiva's) eye — the anguish born of separation from the pleasure of touching your hand.' // DKuṭṭ_918 //

children.text: atha Manmathamabhyarcya kṣitināthaṃ tadanu samadhikaṃ tasyām /
children.translated_text: Then, after worshipping <s>Manmatha</s>, and thereupon [paying homage] to the king even more,

children.text: paramāṃ mudaṃ vahantyāṃ vigrahavanmadanamanasi kanyāyām // DKuṭṭ_919 //
children.translated_text: while the princess, bearing supreme joy, [stood with] <s>Madana</s> embodied in her mind — // DKuṭṭ_919 //
when the king, an ocean of the <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) sentiment, fell thus into the grip of passionate longing,
the <s>nagna</s>-preceptor (naked ascetic / stage director) recited behind the scenes, with words that were loud, sweet, and of clear meaning: // DKuṭṭ_920 //
'Like the nectar-rayed moon, with an unbroken disk, delightful, a feast for the eyes —
at the evening assembly, the kings stood to behold <s>Udayana</s>.' // DKuṭṭ_921 //
Now, when his name was pronounced, and the regard for the king of gods had instantly departed,
the princess, with wonder and delight born [in her heart], placed [his image] within her heart: // DKuṭṭ_922 //

children.text: ayamudayanaḥ sa rājā tātaḥ satkṛtya māṃ dadau yasmai /
children.translated_text: 'This is that King <s>Udayana</s> — my father, having honored me, gave me to him!

children.text: hanta parapreṣaṇamapi na niṣphalaṃ sāmprataṃ jātam // DKuṭṭ_923 //
children.translated_text: Alas, even being sent as a gift to another has not proved fruitless now.' // DKuṭṭ_923 //
'Before anyone finds out — come, I shall quickly depart from here!' —

children.text: iti kathamapi nāyakataḥ kṛṣṭvā dṛśamutsasarja raṅgabhuvam // DKuṭṭ_924 //
children.translated_text: thus, somehow tearing her gaze from the hero, she left the theater. // DKuṭṭ_924 //
'Our hearts stolen by the great festival of <s>Kandarpa</s> (Love), we did not notice

children.text: saṃdhyātikramakālaḥ paśya tvaṃ priyavayasyaka tathā hi // DKuṭṭ_925 //
children.translated_text: that the twilight hour has passed — look, dear companion, for indeed: // DKuṭṭ_925 //
'The eastern quarter, the lord of night hidden behind the mountain of sunrise,

children.text: paripāṇḍunā mukhena priyamiva hṛdayasthitaṃ ramaṇī // DKuṭṭ_926 //
children.translated_text: reveals [him] with a pale face, like a woman [revealing] a beloved held in her heart.' // DKuṭṭ_926 //

children.text: devi tvanmukhapadmaḥ padmān vidadhāti paśya vicchāyān /
children.translated_text: 'Queen, your lotus-face makes the lotuses look pale, see!

children.text: alayo 'pi lajjitā iva śanaiḥ śanaistadudareṣu līyante // DKuṭṭ_927 //
children.translated_text: Even the bees, as if ashamed, slowly hide within their centers.' // DKuṭṭ_927 //
Having spoken thus, after performing the concluding circling with elaborate footsteps,

children.text: naiṣkrāmikyā dhruvayā viniryayau nāyako 'pi saha sarvaiḥ // DKuṭṭ_928 //
children.translated_text: the hero too exited with a concluding <s>dhruva</s> (exit song), together with all. // DKuṭṭ_928 //
When the act had reached completion and the sounds of singing and instruments had ceased,
the prince began to evaluate the merits of the spectacle. // DKuṭṭ_929 //

children.text: nāṭyaprayogatattvaṃ matayo na viśanti mādṛśāṃ prāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The essence of dramatic staging does not generally enter the minds of those like us,
whose hearts are given over to the affairs of cavalry, sacrifices, infantry, and villages.' // DKuṭṭ_930 //

children.text: āste likhito grāmo gṛhāṇa taṃ satpradeśabahubhūmim /
children.translated_text: 'A village has been inscribed [in the grant]; take that one, with its many fertile lands in fine locations;

children.text: vāsaya tatrāvāsaṃ bhavasi tataḥ ṭhakkuro divasaiḥ // DKuṭṭ_931 //
children.translated_text: settle a dwelling there — and in a few days you will become a <s>ṭhakkura</s> (lord).' // DKuṭṭ_931 //
'Even though your livelihood has been established, why do you keep making petitions?

children.text: arpaya vā yadi necchasi kuru sthitiṃ hastadānena // DKuṭṭ_932 //
children.translated_text: Either bestow [your wealth upon others], or if you don't wish to, maintain your position through hand-grants.' // DKuṭṭ_932 //

children.text: na ca pattayo na saptirna ca poṣyajanastathāpyasaṃtuṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He has neither royal decrees, nor horses, nor dependents — yet he is dissatisfied,
though receiving his share, out of the pride of long-standing [service].' // DKuṭṭ_933 //
'The tendency toward making petitions was discerned by us from afar;
be silent — you shall hear the matter from the chamberlain.' // DKuṭṭ_934 //
'You people of the household — where will you go? Taking the common share of the clan,

children.text: ādāya saṃvibhāgaṃ svagṛha iva sthīyatāṃ yathāsaukhyam // DKuṭṭ_935 //
children.translated_text: stay in your own home as if at ease, as you please.' // DKuṭṭ_935 //

children.text: abhyantaravyayārthaṃ na vilabdho yo mayā mahodraṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The great revenue grant that I did not obtain for internal expenses —

children.text: tatrāpi te 'nubandho no jāne kiṃ karomīti // DKuṭṭ_936 //
children.translated_text: even in that matter you have a claim! I do not know what to do.' // DKuṭṭ_936 //
'A provincial posting with substantial revenue was arranged for you at the very outset;

children.text: adyāpi te na jātaṃ niyogināṃ paśya mantharatām // DKuṭṭ_937 //
children.translated_text: see the sluggishness of the officials — it has still not materialized for you.' // DKuṭṭ_937 //
With such words — creating illusions of daily profit and income,
devoid of any fruit — for how long can a dependent be deceived? // DKuṭṭ_938 //
On this subject, relying upon our expertise and familiarity with the terrain,

children.text: mukharatayā kathayāmo jaḍamatisāmājikocitaṃ kiṃ cit // DKuṭṭ_939 //
children.translated_text: we shall speak with loquacity something suitable for a dull-witted audience. // DKuṭṭ_939 //
Having seven bases, six constituents, three measures of physical extent,
the highest through predominance of <s>sattva</s>, to be accomplished through the three [registers] separately and combined — // DKuṭṭ_940 //
of delicate and vigorous action, adorned by subsidiary coloring, of varied styles,
accomplished through emotions that are to be adopted, rejected, or are middling — this is the dramatic performance. // DKuṭṭ_941 //
Of deep and sweet sound, with various modulations preserving the melodic structure,

children.text: darśayato vaicitryaṃ na bhraṣṭo vādakasya layakālaḥ // DKuṭṭ_942 //
children.translated_text: displaying variety — the instrumentalist has not missed the rhythm and tempo. // DKuṭṭ_942 //
With clear meaningful words embellished by proper placement, <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic flavor), <s>kāku</s> (intonation), without abandoning these,
the recitation was faultless in all languages — charmingly sustained. // DKuṭṭ_943 //
With controlled <s>dīpana</s> (intensification) and <s>gamana</s> (progression), combined with fast, medium, and slow tempos,
endowed with melody suited to each <s>rasa</s>, properly harmonized — the song was well-sung by the singers. // DKuṭṭ_944 //
With the full array of costuming that conveys nature, particular states, and conditions,
the imitation has been surpassed — founded upon the wealth of both types of <s>siddhi</s> (success). // DKuṭṭ_945 //
Instructed by the sons of <s>Bharata</s>, I think even the harem-women of kings

children.text: manye tā api nāṭye śobhāsaṃdohamīdṛśaṃ nāpuḥ // DKuṭṭ_946 //
children.translated_text: such as <s>Nahuṣa</s> did not achieve such a wealth of beauty in drama. // DKuṭṭ_946 //
With tightly woven <s>sandhi</s> (junctures), excellently composed with worthy characters,
examined by discerning critics — the jewel of the <s>Ratnāvalī</s> shines! // DKuṭṭ_947 //
As the prince, having demonstrated his refinement, was thus engaged in the narration of such qualities,
another person recited a verse that had come to mind in connection with the occasion: // DKuṭṭ_948 //
'Not retreating from battle, connoisseurship of spectacles, delight in eloquent speech,
zealous prosecution [of cases], and hereditary learning — these are the [virtues] of princes.' // DKuṭṭ_949 //
When this topic had reached his ears, the prince, with relish,
began a description of hunting, interrupting the [current] conversation: // DKuṭṭ_950 //
'Skill in hitting a moving target, practice of firm seating on a swift horse,
knowledge of terrain — these come through the pursuit of hunting. // DKuṭṭ_951 //
'Riding a horse at full speed, with the tips of his feet firmly placed in the stirrups,
his body leaning forward, watching the uneven ground ahead — // DKuṭṭ_952 //
'as long as the creature runs with all its breath, when the world is thrown into confusion by fear of the hunters,

children.text: gocarapatite jīve laghukriyaḥ kṣipati mārgaṇaṃ dhanyaḥ // DKuṭṭ_953 //
children.translated_text: when the quarry falls within range — the fortunate one, acting swiftly, shoots the arrow. // DKuṭṭ_953 //

children.text: mūle sthitasya nibhṛtaṃ mṛgayubhiruccāṭya ḍhaukitaṃ nikaṭe /
children.translated_text: Of [the animal] standing still at the base [of a tree], driven out quietly by the hunters and brought near,
of the hunter who brings down the leaping deer — there is an indescribable, special pleasure. // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 954 //
A deer, ears pricked at the sound of a song, motionless, with grass and fodder in its mouth —
seated still — only the enviable ones (skilled hunters) capture it. // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 955 //
The one who blocks a wild boar charging straight toward him, fleeing from the blaze of a forest fire,

children.text: yo niruṇaddhi sa vandyaḥ sūkaramekaprahāreṇa // DKuṭṭ_956 //
children.translated_text: and stops it with a single blow — he is worthy of praise. // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 956 //
Approaching quietly without making footfall sounds a hare sleeping in the belly of a dense thicket,

children.text: vyādhavara eva kurute nirjīvaṃ helayā śaśakam // DKuṭṭ_957 //
