children.translated_text: only the best of hunters dispatches it effortlessly. // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 957 //
While <s>Saiṃhabhaṭa</s> was thus celebrating the skill and dexterity of hunting,
another person, in the course of the conversation, sang a song that had come to mind: // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 958 //
"Let alone the enjoyment of the activity itself — even a conversation begun about the hunt
encroaches upon the time proper for meals and other duties of those whose minds are absorbed in it." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 959 //
Having grasped the meaning of the song, and having given instructions to the treasurer regarding a gift,
<s>Samarabhaṭa</s> rose, gazing lovingly at <s>Mañjarikā</s>. // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 960 //
Then, having gone to his own residence and completed his meal and other duties,
with his mind drawn by <s>Mañjarikā</s>, he spoke thus in the presence of his minister: // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 961 //
"In the furrowing of brows, in smiles, in glances, in gentle, artful words, in gestures, in gait —

children.text: kusumapraharaṇa eko yugapadvihitāśrayaḥ kathaṃ tasyāḥ // DKuṭṭ_962 //
children.translated_text: O Flower-armed one (<s>Kāma</s>), how has one person alone simultaneously found refuge in all of hers?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 962 //
"The destruction of <s>Sunda</s> and <s>Upasunda</s> was the fruit of the Self-born's (<s>Brahmā</s>'s) creation of <s>Tilottamā</s>;

children.text: janamṛtaye tāṃ sṛjatā kiṃ dṛṣṭaṃ surahitaṃ tena // DKuṭṭ_963 //
children.translated_text: in creating her for the death of mortals, what concern for the gods' welfare did he show?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 963 //
"Adorned with flowers, her braid is a canal bestowing the fruits appropriate to <s>Kāma</s>
upon embodied beings, with her eyes tremulous as a fawn's." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 964 //
"Her lotus-face — like a lotus — is drunk by bees fallen from the triple heaven,
with its collyrium-adorned, faultless, coquettish, honey-maddened coppery glow." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 965 //
"An ascetic devoted to austerities who frequents the slopes of the mountain-king for the attainment of bliss —

children.text: spṛhayati so 'pi nitambaṃ suratāptyai samavalokya tanvaṅgyāḥ // DKuṭṭ_966 //
children.translated_text: even he, upon beholding the hips of the slender-limbed one, covets those hips for the attainment of (erotic) bliss." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 966 //
"The middle portion of her body, divisible into three hand-spans, the pair of arms equipped with two hands —

children.text: janayati tadapi mṛgākṣī sahasrakarato 'dhikaṃ tāpam // DKuṭṭ_967 //
children.translated_text: even so, the doe-eyed one produces more heat than the thousand-rayed sun." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 967 //

children.text: sā sragdharā suvadanā praharṣiṇī saiva saiva tanumadhyā /
children.translated_text: "She is <s>Sragdharā</s> (a garland-bearer/a metre); she is fair-faced, she is <s>Praharṣiṇī</s> (a delighter/a metre); she herself is slender-waisted;

children.text: na karoti kasya vismayamiti rucirā mañjubhāṣiṇī saiva // DKuṭṭ_968 //
children.translated_text: who does she not astonish? For she is lovely, she is sweet-voiced — she herself." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 968 //

children.text: anukurvatyā kanyāṃ tathā tathā nāyakastayā dṛṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: "As she was imitating the maiden, the hero was so gazed upon by her

children.text: yena jaratsvapyaṭanī dhanuṣaḥ spṛṣṭā daśārdhabāṇena // DKuṭṭ_969 //
children.translated_text: that even as an old traveler, the five-arrowed one (<s>Kāma</s>) touched the bow's string." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 969 //
"Her beauty, variegated by youth, her gestures transformed by <s>Anaṅga</s> (Love), blazing through dramatic art —
these rob even the tranquil of their pride of serenity, effortlessly." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 970 //

children.text: dagdhe 'pi vapuṣi bhītiṃ na vimuñcati nīlalohitasamutthām /
children.translated_text: "Even when his body has been burned, he does not release the fear arising from <s>Nīlalohita</s> (<s>Śiva</s>);

children.text: tatkṣetre vasati yataḥ pramadārūpeṇa śambaradhvaṃsī // DKuṭṭ_971 //
children.translated_text: for the Destroyer of <s>Śambara</s> (<s>Kāma</s>) dwells in that domain in the form of a beautiful woman." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 971 //

children.text: yadi vaḥ paralokamatiḥ śṛṇuta śreyastapodhanā mattaḥ /
children.translated_text: "If you are intent on the next world, hear from me what is beneficial, O ascetics:

children.text: utsṛjya yāta tūrṇaṃ vāravadhūdūṣitaṃ sthānam // DKuṭṭ_972 //
children.translated_text: quickly leave this place, polluted by courtesans!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 972 //

children.text: ciramapi vikalpya niścitiriyameva sthāpyate na gatiranyā /
children.translated_text: "Even after long deliberation, this alone is the established conclusion — there is no other course;

children.text: tannirmāṇe jātā lāvaṇyamayāḥ kaṇā vidheraṇavaḥ // DKuṭṭ_973 //
children.translated_text: the Creator's atoms in her creation became particles of pure grace." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 973 //
"Her pair of breasts, having reached their full height, spread forth unopposed;

children.text: kṣapayati yajjanamevaṃ kaḥ sprakṣyati tadvivekavān patitam // DKuṭṭ_974 //
children.translated_text: whoever thus wastes his life — what discerning person would touch him once fallen?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 974 //
"How could the arrangement of those hips not be coveted by those devoted to sensual pleasure,

children.text: śāntātmanāpi vihitaṃ viśvasṛjā gauravaṃ yasya // DKuṭṭ_975 //
children.translated_text: when even by the tranquil-souled Creator, gravity was bestowed upon them?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 975 //
"He (<s>Kāma</s>) whose origin is from remembrance, whose arrows are flowers, whose power relies on women,

children.text: so 'pi vyaṅgaḥ praharati dhāturaho citramācaritam // DKuṭṭ_976 //
children.translated_text: he too, though limbless, strikes — ah, wondrous is the conduct of the Creator!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 976 //
"Let others stand aside — having seen that jewel among women, the essence of the world,
<s>Brahmā</s> himself loses attention to his recitation and becomes filled with disillusionment!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 977 //
"If <s>Śarva</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) were to see her, then, turning away from the company of the other <s>Rāmā</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>),

children.text: nindati mūrdhani somaṃ smarāgnisaṃdhukṣaṇaṃ śarīraṃ ca // DKuṭṭ_978 //
children.translated_text: he would curse the moon on his head, and his own body which kindles the fire of Love." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 978 //
"<s>Keśava</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) is present here, and she too is endowed with a beauty that captivates the heart;
then why does she not leave his chest — is it out of suspicion regarding <s>Saindhavī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>'s rival)?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 979 //

children.text: udayati na paṇḍitānāṃ kathamātmani kautukaṃ gajendragatiḥ /
children.translated_text: "How does astonishment not arise in the learned at the gait of a lordly elephant (in her walk)?
For it afflicts young men in the bloom of youth even without any deliberate effort." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 980 //
"The ear-lotus might attain the nature of an eye, or the eye might attain the nature of a blue lotus,

children.text: hariṇadṛśo yadi na syātkanakojjvalakesaraṃ madhye // DKuṭṭ_981 //
children.translated_text: were it not for the golden-bright pistil in the center of the fawn-eyed one's face." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 981 //
"Women, because of her incomparability, and men too, because of deprivation of her enjoyment,
wither away constantly — only those devoid of both natures (the neuter) remain at ease." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 982 //
"The ill-behaved do not attain praiseworthy roundness — except her breasts,

children.text: yau dattvāmalamūrtiṃ madhye hāraṃ janakṣayaṃ kurutaḥ // DKuṭṭ_983 //
children.translated_text: which, though having given a spotless form in the middle, produce a necklace that destroys people." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 983 //

children.text: bhūmaṇḍale 'tra sakale nātaḥ paramaparamadbhutaṃ kiṃ cit /
children.translated_text: "In this entire globe, there is nothing more supremely wonderful than this:

children.text: no jātā yadapārthā kṛśodarī dhārtarāṣṭrayātāpi // DKuṭṭ_984 //
children.translated_text: that the slender-waisted one has not become destitute even though she has undergone the <s>Dhārtarāṣṭra</s>-expedition (i.e., been 'gambled away' through the dice-game)." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 984 //
"The middle region of the slender girl is too narrow to bear artificial ornaments;

children.text: śakta iti kṛtaṃ vidhinā romāvalibhūṣaṇaṃ sahajam // DKuṭṭ_985 //
children.translated_text: therefore the Creator fashioned the natural ornament of the line of hair (<s>romāvalī</s>)." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 985 //
"A trembling lip, the unsteadiness of her pair of eyes, the furrow of her brows —
such is the power of the slender-limbed girl: it conquers the entire world without remainder." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 986 //

children.text: vahatu nitambaḥ sthūlo raśanāṃ hāraṃ ca kucayugaṃ pīnam /
children.translated_text: "Let her broad hips bear the girdle, and her full pair of breasts the necklace;
but the fastening of bracelets on her lotus-stalk-like arms would be perilous." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 987 //
"Skilled in many strategies, constantly devoted to matters of virtue,

children.text: balinaḥ sthāpayati vaśe karabhorurvigraheṇa mṛdunaiva // DKuṭṭ_988 //
children.translated_text: she brings the powerful under her sway, with her soft body alone, O she of elephant-calf thighs." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 988 //
While the prince's mouth was thus eloquent with praises of her, agitated by the Makara-bannered one (<s>Kāma</s>),
a bold go-between, sent by <s>Mañjarikā</s>, arrived. // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 989 //
She respectfully placed before him a tray of flowers and betel,
and then, at the right moment, conveyed the errand of her mistress: // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 990 //
"The foolish girl longs to pluck the lotus born from the navel of the Slayer of <s>Mura</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) as an ear-ornament;
she wishes to take down the orb of the moon-king from the sky!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 991 //
"The senseless one craves the <s>amṛta</s> (nectar), the food of the gods of the triple heaven;
she desires to lie upon a bed strewn with fresh sandalwood leaves in the hot season!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 992 //
"She puts her trust in wearing a garland plucked from the <s>Pārijāta</s> tree's blossoms;
the ill-resolved one seeks to seize the jewel from the breast of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 993 //
"We are sinful women, touched by men without discrimination; where are we, lowborn ones,

children.text: kva ca yūyamindrakalpā analpamanaso guṇābharaṇāḥ // DKuṭṭ_994 //
children.translated_text: and where are you, equal to <s>Indra</s>, great-souled, adorned with virtues?" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 994 //

children.text: duṣprakṛteḥ prakṛtiriyaṃ tasya tu dagdhātmajanmanaḥ kāpi /
children.translated_text: "This is the nature of one of evil disposition — but hers, of one whose own birth is accursed, is something else entirely:
heedless of what is proper and improper, she fixes her heart where it should not be." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 995 //
"She who laughs at the lotus-pond, saying 'I am juicier, dyed with natural passion' —

children.text: dhyānadhiya ātmavṛttiṃ nindatyekatra puruṣa āsaktām // DKuṭṭ_996 //
children.translated_text: with the eye of contemplation, she condemns her own fixation on a single man." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 996 //
"Saying 'it is too smooth,' she takes no pleasure even in a century's flow of ghee;
she praises the course of the five dice — declaring it a companionship not barren of results." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 997 //
"She does not praise the sandalwood creeper encircled by serpents, saying 'it is too moist with juice';

children.text: na śṛṇoti kīrtyamānāṃ svapneṣvapi madanamūrchitāṃ matsīm // DKuṭṭ_998 //
children.translated_text: she does not hear of even in dreams the <s>matsī</s> (fish) swooning in love." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 998 //
"She hates the tongue among the sense organs, saying 'it is stained with betel-redness';
she declares the understanding of one desiring liberation to be undiscriminating among hares, bulls, horses, and men." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 999 //

children.text: no bahu manute Rambhāṃ Nalakūbaramabhisṛteti kāmārtā /
children.translated_text: "Love-sick, she does not esteem <s>Rambhā</s>, saying 'she went to <s>Nalakūbara</s>';
and she censures <s>Urvaśī</s>, the celestial courtesan, for being devoted to <s>Purūravas</s>." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 1000 //

children.text: harati mano no hriyate rañjayati na rajyate kadā cidapi /
children.translated_text: "She steals hearts but is never herself robbed; she delights others but is never herself delighted;
she captivates with wonderful deeds and favors, but is not herself captured by many." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 1001 //

children.text: premamayīvābhāti prema tu nāmnaiva kevalaṃ vetti /
children.translated_text: "She appears as though made of love, yet knows love only by name;

children.text: kaṇṭakitā bhavati rate ratabhogasukhaṃ śṛṇoti lokāttu // DKuṭṭ_1002 //
children.translated_text: she bristles with goosebumps during lovemaking, but learns of love's bliss only from common report." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 1002 //
"She performs intimate flattery through special artistry, not through the impulse of passion;
ignorant of love's disease, she produces pain only to the point of pretense." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 1003 //
"Young as she is, devoid of sincerity, she glimmers like a crescent moon having reached the Lord (<s>Śiva</s>);
like the exploits of the Lord of <s>Rākṣasas</s> (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>), she strips the lord of wealth (<s>Kubera</s>) of his glory." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 1004 //
"O lord of men, what shall I say? Even <s>Kāma</s>, the wicked Flower-arrowed one, though his body was burned by the fire of <s>Tripurāntaka</s>'s (<s>Śiva</s>'s) eye,
does not abandon his grasp on that which is hard to attain!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 1005 //
"Having obtained the opportunity of beholding you, that evil-minded one (<s>Kāma</s>)
with his long-accumulated fury has begun to slay her too with his showers of arrows." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 1006 //
"That very staff with which you casually touched her —

children.text: jātaḥ sa eva tasyā Ananyabhavamārgaṇaḥ prathamaḥ // DKuṭṭ_1007 //
children.translated_text: that itself became for her the first arrow of the One-who-has-no-other-origin (<s>Kāma</s>)." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 1007 //
"Proud of her knowledge, she was quietly laughed at by her peers of equal skill

children.text: tvayi saktadṛśaḥ sakhyā visaṃṣṭhule nāṭyanirmāṇe // DKuṭṭ_1008 //
children.translated_text: when, with her gaze fixed on you, her dramatic performance became unsteady, O friend." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 1008 //
"Disregarding the preceptor's anger born from the commission of faults contrary to <s>Bharata</s>'s teachings,
the performance was prolonged by the slender girl out of desire to remain in your presence." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 1009 //
"Even after the spectacle was concluded, the states of emotion belonging to the subsequent roles

children.text: gṛha eva niravasānaṃ vitanoti na nāṭyadharmeṇa // DKuṭṭ_1010 //
children.translated_text: she continues to enact endlessly at home — not by the rules of dramatic art." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 1010 //

children.text: dhyāyata ekaṃ puruṣaṃ paramātmavidaḥ śaśaṃsa yā na purā /
children.translated_text: "She who formerly never spoke of the <s>paramātmavidaḥ</s> (knowers of the supreme self) meditating on a single being —

children.text: tānanukurute saiva dhyāyantī tvāṃ mahāpuruṣam // DKuṭṭ_1011 //
children.translated_text: she now imitates them, meditating on you, O great being." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 1011 //
"'Thus did he walk, thus did he sit, thus did he look, thus did he speak' —

children.text: iti vismṛtānyakāryā smarati kṛśāṅgī tvadīyalīlānām // DKuṭṭ_1012 //
children.translated_text: thus the slender-limbed girl, forgetting all other duties, remembers your graceful acts." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 1012 //

children.text: Nalakūbaro varāko Ratiramaṇo ramaṇa eva kiṃ tena /
children.translated_text: "Poor <s>Nalakūbara</s>! <s>Rati</s>'s husband (<s>Kāma</s>) is merely a lover — what use is he?

children.text: Aniruddho 'pi na buddho vidagdhavihitāsu suratagoṣṭhīṣu // DKuṭṭ_1013 //
children.translated_text: Even <s>Aniruddha</s> is not enlightened in the art of love-congress arranged by the sophisticated." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 1013 //
"Neither <s>Jayanta</s> of infinite virtues, nor <s>Kumāra</s> (<s>Kārttikeya</s>) removed from the deeds of <s>Māra</s> (Love) —

children.text: kena samatāṃ nayāmastamiti sakhī vahati mānasaṃ kleśam // DKuṭṭ_1014 //
children.translated_text: 'With whom shall we compare him?' — thus her friend bears mental anguish." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 1014 //
"Coming, approaching, before her, at her side, pleased, then angry —
the young girl sees you alone in every state, placed there by her imagination." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 1015 //

children.text: rucyaḥ kānto hṛdyaḥ subhagaḥ sukhado manoharo ramaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: "'Charming, beloved, delightful, fortunate, giver of pleasure, captivating, lover,

children.text: iṣṭaḥ svāmī dayitaḥ prāṇeśaḥ kelikaraṇanipuṇa iti // DKuṭṭ_1016 //
children.translated_text: desired one, lord, darling, lord of my life, skilled in the arts of love' — thus // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 1016 //
having abandoned all other activities, the beautiful girl, with unperturbed mind,
recites for the fulfillment of her desire the great hymn of your twelve names." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 1017 //
"'Go to that very woman upon whom you have fixed your heart and lingered, O shameless one!
Enough of these deceitful entreaties after such a long time!'" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 1018 //
"'I shall speak to him as to an offender, with anger quivering on my lip, with arched brows' —

children.text: iti vidadhāti sumadhyā hṛdayena manorathāvṛttim // DKuṭṭ_1019 //
children.translated_text: thus the slender-waisted girl rehearses the fulfillment of her desires in her heart." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 1019 //

children.text: utsahate na draṣṭuṃ pratibimbitamānanaṃ kutaḥ śaśinam /
children.translated_text: "She cannot bear to look at her own reflection; whence then at the moon?

children.text: kā saṃkathā mṛṇāle kṣipati bhujau sarvato vyathitā // DKuṭṭ_1020 //
children.translated_text: What need to speak of lotus-stalks? — distressed on all sides, she flings away her arms." // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 1020 //

children.text: dūre kadalīdaṇḍā ūrvorapi na sahate samāśleṣam /
children.translated_text: "Far off are the banana-trunk pillows; she cannot endure even the embrace of her own thighs;
averse to the touch of her own hands, she rests on tender leaves — how contradictory!" // <s>DKuṭṭ</s> 1021 //

children.text: ayi mañjari saiva tvaṃ vidagdhajanamaṇḍitā purī saiva /
children.translated_text: O <s>Mañjarī</s>, you are the same, this city adorned with refined people is the same,

children.text: Kusumāyudhaḥ sa eva vyasanaṃ kuta etadāyātam // DKuṭṭ_1022 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kusumāyudha</s> (the Flower-armed one, Kāma) is the same — from where then has this affliction come? // DKuṭṭ_1022 //
She for whom <s>Kāma</s> himself is wretched, whose power of attracting passion resembles a straw or a clod of earth,

children.text: sāpi gatā bhūmimimāṃ jīvantyā nekṣyate kimiha // DKuṭṭ_1023 //
children.translated_text: even she has departed this world — will she not be seen again while one yet lives? // DKuṭṭ_1023 //
Among those trained in the art of love's pursuit and those untrained in the gestures of <s>Madana</s> (Love),
O slender one, only those who are expert in such matters have the capacity to discern the distinction. // DKuṭṭ_1024 //
Though causing distress, possessing a beautiful complexion; though occasioning anxiety among attendants, yet delightful —
passion, which depends upon ever-fresh attachment, bestows upon you its splendor. // DKuṭṭ_1025 //
There has arisen in this world one unique man, a rival to the one of matchless arrows (<s>Kāma</s>),

children.text: tena śaśibimbaphalake sujanmanā lekhitaṃ nijaṃ nāma // DKuṭṭ_1026 //
children.translated_text: by that noble one his own name has been inscribed upon the tablet of the moon's orb. // DKuṭṭ_1026 //
His foot has been playfully placed upon the heads of those who pride themselves on their good fortune,
and by him the flower of fame and fortune of <s>Dhanapati</s>'s (Kubera's) son has been trampled. // DKuṭṭ_1027 //
You who are clever in the art of deceiving men, who have mastered the fabrication of deceitful flattery,

children.text: tvamapi vilāsini nītā gatimiyatīṃ yena subhagena // DKuṭṭ_1028 //
children.translated_text: even you, O graceful one, have been brought to this state by that fortunate man. // DKuṭṭ_1028 //
Then tell us his whereabouts — let us exert ourselves sufficiently to accomplish our purpose,

children.text: kurvata eva hi yatnaṃ bhiṣagjanāḥ kṛcchrasādhyaroge 'pi // DKuṭṭ_1029 //
children.translated_text: for physicians make every effort even in the case of a disease that is difficult to cure. // DKuṭṭ_1029 //

children.text: iti gadite sakhyā sā tadabhimukhaṃ cakṣuṣī samunmīlya /
children.translated_text: When this was spoken by her friend, she, opening her eyes slowly in his direction,
with great difficulty after a long time produces a faintly discernible, anguished sigh. // DKuṭṭ_1030 //
What personal gain does the moon seek when illuminating the night?

children.text: tarpayatāṃ bhuvamakhilāṃ salilamucāṃ ko 'bhikāṅkṣito lābhaḥ // DKuṭṭ_1031 //
children.translated_text: What desired reward do the rain clouds seek when satiating the entire earth? // DKuṭṭ_1031 //
<s>Indra</s>'s bow rises to adorn the sky without any desire for fruit —
the disposition to benefit others, without regard for one's own affairs, is innate to the virtuous. // DKuṭṭ_1032 //
Generally, abstaining from that which is the cause of a disease leads to the cure of ailments,

children.text: smaramāndyaṃ tu yadutthaṃ tadeva khalu bheṣajaṃ yatastasya // DKuṭṭ_1033 //
children.translated_text: but the languor born of <s>Smara</s> (Love) — that very same cause is indeed the remedy for it. // DKuṭṭ_1033 //
Therefore the slender one yearns for contact with the dust of your lotus-feet,
but she has no desire for the arising of pleasure from union, which is fraught with the poison of hope. // DKuṭṭ_1034 //
The peahen attains supreme delight merely by the sound of the rain cloud,
the female fish achieves complete fulfillment merely by the unblinking gaze of the male — // DKuṭṭ_1035 //
I do not proclaim his virtues with the garrulousness of idle praise, nor with the intent of enticing you,
but merely by way of describing his true nature as it is. // DKuṭṭ_1036 //
Rooted in sincere affection, sprouting branches of smiles, glances, and playful movements of the brow,

children.text: sevante hṛdyarasāṃ rāgatarau Mañjarīṃ dhanyāḥ // DKuṭṭ_1037 //
children.translated_text: the fortunate ones savor the delightful <s>rasa</s> (sentiment) in <s>Mañjarī</s>, who is a tree of passion. // DKuṭṭ_1037 //

children.text: tiṣṭhatu tadaṅgasaṅgo vilokitā yena jhagiti varagātrī /
children.translated_text: Let alone the contact with her limbs — he who has merely beheld that woman of beautiful body,
to him all other women appear as mere human forms. // DKuṭṭ_1038 //
Those who have even once tasted the delightful essence of the pleasure of her embrace,

children.text: viddhi narādhipa teṣāṃ dūrībhūtaṃ prajākāryam // DKuṭṭ_1039 //
children.translated_text: know, O lord of men, that for them the duty of procreation has become a distant matter. // DKuṭṭ_1039 //

children.text: āsthā kā khalu tasyā viṣayagrahadurbaleṣu puruṣeṣu /
children.translated_text: What regard indeed would she have for men who are feeble in grasping the objects of sense,
she in whose net of <s>vilāsa</s> (amorous sport) even <s>Kapila</s> would be caught like a bird? // DKuṭṭ_1040 //

children.text: dagdhvāpi punardagdho nūnamanaṅgaḥ Hareṇa tāṃ tanvīm /
children.translated_text: Surely <s>Anaṅga</s> (the Bodiless one, Kāma), though burnt by <s>Hara</s> (Śiva), has been burnt again upon seeing that slender woman,

children.text: dṛṣṭvāpi yena tiṣṭhasi nirākulaḥ svasthavṛttena // DKuṭṭ_1041 //
children.translated_text: since even after beholding her you remain unperturbed, of steady conduct. // DKuṭṭ_1041 //
Then, when she had ceased speaking and the prince's mind was enlivened,
someone sang a song that came to mind as fitting the occasion. // DKuṭṭ_1042 //
For a young couple whose hearts have been strengthened by intense mutual passion,
even the slightest passing of time becomes an obstacle to the joy of union. // DKuṭṭ_1043 //
Hearing this, the son of <s>Siṃhabhaṭa</s>, pleased, with a gentle smile at first,

children.text: nijagāda cārubhāṣiṇi gītikayā samayasammataṃ kathitam // DKuṭṭ_1044 //
children.translated_text: said, 'O sweet-spoken one, what has been told through the song is approved by mutual agreement.' // DKuṭṭ_1044 //

children.text: abhinandya sā tatheti prayayau pramadāvatī nijaṃ bhavanam /
children.translated_text: She, approving with 'so be it,' the joyful woman departed to her own dwelling,

children.text: akarocca viditakāryāṃ yukte 'vasare manoramāṃ gaṇikām // DKuṭṭ_1045 //
children.translated_text: and at the appropriate time she informed the charming <s>gaṇikā</s> (courtesan) of what was to be done. // DKuṭṭ_1045 //
Then she, having resolved her mind, quickly assuming a beautiful and elegant attire,
arrived at the royal bedchamber and entered, accompanied by her <s>saṃcārikā</s> (female attendant). // DKuṭṭ_1046 //
Having made her obeisance, she took the seat indicated by the <s>nāyaka</s> (hero, the prince),
and when asked about her well-being, the <s>dūtī</s> (female messenger) replied with modesty: // DKuṭṭ_1047 //
'O illustrious one, today all the blessings of the elders have been fulfilled with good fortune,

children.text: adya madanaḥ prasanno bhāgyacayairadya pariṇataṃ phalataḥ // DKuṭṭ_1048 //
children.translated_text: today <s>Madana</s> (Love) is propitious, today the accumulation of merit has borne its fruit. // DKuṭṭ_1048 //
Today our mother has truly given birth, today the dawn of auspicious qualities has been realized,'

children.text: tvayi vitarati sasnehaṃ nirāmayapraśnabhāratīṃ tasyāḥ // DKuṭṭ_1049 //
children.translated_text: as you affectionately bestow upon her the words of inquiry about her health. // DKuṭṭ_1049 //
For young men whose minds are agitated by eager longing, who are overwhelmed by excessive desire,

children.text: audāsīnyaṃ bhajatāṃ samāgatā bhavati nālikā yūnām // DKuṭṭ_1050 //
children.translated_text: the time of meeting arrives for those who assume an air of indifference. // DKuṭṭ_1050 //
'Wielding the bow of flower-arrows, stand with your ally, your beloved —

children.text: yāmo vayaṃ na rājati vijanasthitamithunasaṃnidhāvaparaḥ // DKuṭṭ_1051 //
children.translated_text: we shall depart, for the presence of another is not fitting near a couple in a secluded place.' // DKuṭṭ_1051 //
'She is fatigued from dancing, and made weary by <s>Madana</s> (Love), being exceedingly delicate;

children.text: tvamapi ratisamaraśūraḥ svargabhuvaḥ santu kuśalāya // DKuṭṭ_1052 //
children.translated_text: and you too are a hero in the battle of <s>Rati</s> (love) — may the heavenly realms grant you well-being!' // DKuṭṭ_1052 //
For indeed, the more a woman overcome by infatuation displays her helplessness,
the more a man's ardor puts forth its shoots. // DKuṭṭ_1053 //

children.text: iti śūnyīkṛtaveśmani harati śanaiḥ sahajamaṃśukaṃ tasmin /
children.translated_text: Thus, when the chamber had been emptied, as he slowly removes her natural garment,

children.text: darśitasādhvasalajjā jagāda sā kiṃ karoṣīti // DKuṭṭ_1054 //
children.translated_text: she, displaying bashfulness and modesty, said, 'What are you doing?' // DKuṭṭ_1054 //
'O innocent one, that is being done which is the essence of the four <s>puruṣārthas</s> (aims of human life).'

children.text: iti nigaditasasmeraḥ smaravidhurita ātatāna ratikalaham // DKuṭṭ_1055 //
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus with a smile, tormented by <s>Smara</s> (Love), he commenced the battle of <s>Rati</s> (passion). // DKuṭṭ_1055 //

children.text: Verses 1056-1059 are found only in two Nepalese manuscripts and in two editions.
children.translated_text: Verses 1056-1059 are found only in two Nepalese manuscripts and in two editions.
Having gratified the prince with various special forms of <s>surata</s> (lovemaking), that <s>gaṇikā</s> (courtesan) consumed all his wealth,

children.text: gaṇikāsau rājasutaṃ tvagasthiśeṣaṃ mumoca nāticirāt // DKuṭṭ_1056 //
children.translated_text: and before long released the prince, leaving him reduced to nothing but skin and bones. // DKuṭṭ_1056 //
'Therefore, by means of what I have taught — the method of acquiring wealth from amorous men —
you shall attain great prosperity through the riches extracted from the world of the love-struck.' // DKuṭṭ_1057 //
Thus, awakened and gratified by hearing this instruction, she went to her own home,
<s>Mālatī</s>, her delusion dispelled, having bowed at the feet of <s>Vikarālā</s>. // DKuṭṭ_1058 //
He who properly listens to this poem, observing the meaning of the <s>kāvya</s> (poetry),
shall never be deceived by <s>viṭas</s> (rogues), <s>veśyās</s> (courtesans), swindlers, or <s>kuṭṭanīs</s> (bawds). // DKuṭṭ_1059 //
